description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

Remaining: 43 Compose files, and no second language yet. | Progress 2026-07-31 second pass (STILL NOT DONE - AC1 and AC3 outstanding). SCOPE is now 68 files, up from 39; 91 Compose files exist, so 23 remain. Converted and locked: ImeActionBar, LabeledDropdown, StatusBadge, ErrorStateView, CachedThumbnail, SectionPlaceholder, SyncStatusBar, LockScreen, ReconcileBanner, ConsignorPicker's Compose layer, NotesFieldWithDictation, SkuFieldWithScanner, CaptureScreen, BarcodeScanScreen, ShareTargetActivity, PlanGateHost, SellerSnapshotWidget, plus 14 files that were already literal-free (a11y helpers, Charts, Theme, Components, DataRow, FieldValidation, InfoCard, Skeleton, HapticFeedback, LanguagePicker, TurnstileChallenge). ~45 literals moved to res/values/strings.xml. (1) A String DEFAULT ARGUMENT was invisible: ErrorStateView's title=\"Couldn't load\" and retryTitle=\"Try again\" are the copy every data screen in the app shows on a failed load, and they reach the user through the caller's Text(title), never through a literal at a sink. (2) CONDITIONAL copy inside a sink was invisible: the walk after an open sink stopped at the 'if (' line and declared the call clean, which hid ShareTargetActivity's two branches and OnboardingHost's permission-blocked concatenation (now a positional format string, onboarding_permission_blocked_detail, because word order is not portable). (3) @Preview bodies were NOT exempt, so sample copy would have forced a conversion of developer scaffolding - they are exempt by region now. Also added an exemption for Compose animation labels (rememberInfiniteTransition/animate*), which are debug names the animation inspector shows and nothing else; they are told apart from real label= copy by the enclosing call, not by the literal's shape, since 'Pending' and 'skeleton' look equally translatable in isolation. The guard now carries an 11-case --self-test that runs on EVERY invocation (not behind a flag - an opt-in test for a guard is back where it started), proving each rule fires and each exemption stays quiet. DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT OF SCOPE with the reason recorded in the file: consignment/ConsignorPicker.kt (splitHint) and marketplaces/ListingCard.kt (quantityText, contentDescription) build sentences in plain non-composable functions that unit tests assert on by exact wording; their Compose literals ARE converted, but scoping them would mean the guard called a file clean while shipped English sat one call deeper. Kotlin could not be compiled here (the Android Gradle plugin does not resolve in this container) - Android CI is the gate. | Progress 2026-07-31 third pass - AC1 and AC2 are now MET; AC3 (a second language) is the only thing outstanding. SCOPE is 91 of 91 Compose files under app/src/main, up from 39 at the start of the session; ~180 more literals moved to res/values/strings.xml across seven commits. AC2 held throughout: SyncStatusBar, ConsignmentReportScreen, PayoutReconciliationScreen, DisputeSheet, SalesScreen, CompsSection and ListingPerformanceScreen all hand-rolled plurals as \${if (n == 1) \"\" else \"s\"} and are now <plurals>; ListingPerformanceScreen needed three of them (views / watchers / impressions each agree independently) so its metrics line is assembled in a small @Composable helper rather than inside buildString. THE GUARD WAS REWRITTEN, not extended again. Four positional rules had each lost to ordinary Kotlin in turn - Text(\"x\"), then ktlint's wrapped form, then if/else, then the same conditional on one line - and Text(band.days?.let { \"Last \$it days\" } ?: \"Any time\") would have been the fifth. It now finds the sink's argument list, reads to its close, and judges each LITERAL rather than its position: copy needs internal whitespace, or an initial capital, or a template hole with words around it and no path punctuation. That excludes separators, routes, when-keys, MIME types, animation labels and character counters; the documented false negative is lowercase one-word copy with no hole. Seven live strings fell out of the rewrite in files already marked converted, which is the point. Also added: a declared escape hatch (// no-bare-strings: <reason>) for a wire value in a default argument, @Preview bodies exempt by region, per-line dedupe, Badge/SectionLabel/SectionPlaceholder as sinks, and a 24-case --self-test that runs on EVERY invocation rather than behind a flag. THE LAST TWO FILES needed a shape change: ConsignorPicker.splitHint and ListingCard.quantityText/contentDescription built sentences in plain functions that tests asserted on word for word. They return the DECISION now (a sealed SplitHint, a @StringRes id) with @Composable wrappers resolving it, so the tests assert the choice and its numbers instead of English. StatusStyle came with them - label() title-cased the wire value so \"to_list\" read as \"To List\" in every language; the 14 shipped statuses have resources now and label() is the fallback for a status that ships ahead of its string. Verified: python3 android/scripts/no-bare-strings.py (self-test + 91 files) and no-ungated-log.py both pass; no duplicate string names (1223 entries); no unused imports or >100-column lines in the diff. Kotlin still CANNOT be compiled in this container - the Android Gradle plugin does not resolve here - so Android CI remains the gate, and it only runs on pull requests. | Done 2026-08-06 - AC3 closed, story DONE. The translation was produced by six parallel agents over disjoint line ranges of the default file, then assembled and checked mechanically rather than trusted. THE TRANSLATION IS MACHINE-AUTHORED AND HAS NOT HAD A NATIVE-SPEAKER REVIEW - the mechanics are guarded, the wording is not; a review pass before Play Store release is a separate call for the operator. Register is informal tu throughout, brand and marketplace names untranslated, date masks localized to AAAA-MM-DD (display only - ExpenseFormSheet.kt and DraftsLibraryScreen.kt use those strings as hints, never compare against them). android/scripts/check-string-formats.py grew two checks so this cannot silently rot: check_translations() fails on any name present in one file and not the other or any placeholder-set difference (the failure mode is MissingFormatArgumentException on one screen in one language, invisible to an English test), and check_language_list() fails unless the values-<tag>/ directories, locales_config.xml and AppLocale.SUPPORTED name the same set - two of three agreeing is what produces a picker entry that changes nothing. Both are already wired into android-ci.yml, which runs this script. VERIFIED by injecting each failure: renamed common_save -> common_save_typo and added a %2$s to publish_sku (exit 1, all three drifts named), and removed es from locales_config.xml (exit 1), restoring after each. check-string-formats.py reports OK (1223 resources, en, es) and no-bare-strings.py reports OK (91 files in scope, matching the 91 files containing @Composable). AppLocaleTest gains 'Spanish is offered and the picker is visible'. userStories.title: [OPERATOR] Obtain eBay restricted scopes so Send-Offers-to-Interested-Buyers works in production
userStories.description: The Negotiation API (find_eligible_items + send_offer_to_interested_buyers) is fully coded but the sell.negotiation scope is omitted from the prod consent request because our prod keyset isn't granted it — so every call 403s. 'Send offer to watchers' is a top sell-through lever that silently does nothing for real sellers.
acceptanceCriteria: Apply to eBay for the restricted sell.negotiation (and commerce.identity.readonly) scopes on the prod keyset.
Once granted, re-add the scope lines and force a re-consent flow at /oauth/start; surface 'reconnect required' to connected sellers.
Verify findEligibleItems + sendOfferToInterestedBuyers against a prod token; add a connection flag mirroring analytics_access_denied when the scope is absent.
userStories.notes: [PRE-LAUNCH AUDIT 2026-06-30 · HIGH · ebay · ebay coverage audit] Evidence: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-client.ts:202-204,3258,3330; https://developer.ebay.com/api-docs/sell/negotiation/overview.html [CODE SLICE COMPLETE 2026-07-03 - AC1 (the eBay application itself) remains the USER'S ops step] AC3's code shipped: MIGRATION 00345 (HELD) adds marketplace_connections.negotiation_access_denied mirroring analytics_access_denied; flipdesk-ebay sets it on a /sell/negotiation 403 (tenant-scoped update, best-effort so the 501 always reaches the client) and clears it on any successful eligible/send-offer call. NEW distinction the audit wanted: negotiationScope403Body(deploymentHasScope) - when the deployment DOES request the scope but this token 403s (consented pre-grant), the client gets 501 code=reconnect_required with copy naming the fix ('reconnect your eBay account'), vs the existing feature_unavailable dead-end when the deployment lacks the scope entirely. iOS: EdgeAPIError maps reconnect_required onto featureUnavailable(detail:) (detail carries the server copy); NegotiationStore.EligibleCheck.unavailable now carries detail; the send-offer sheet prefers the server copy - sellers see the reconnect instruction, not an indefinite wait. 2 new edge tests (body pick both ways); full edge 2544/0. AC2's scope lines remain documented ready-to-re-add at getScopes (US-1510). REMAINING: user applies to eBay for sell.negotiation + commerce.identity.readonly on the prod keyset; once granted, re-add the two scope lines and sellers re-consent - the runtime flag + reconnect flow shipped here handles the transition automatically. | 2026-07-18 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) named above as HELD are on origin/main AND below prod's applied version (proven >= 00474: the deployed edge expects 00474 and a confirmed-behind DB hard-exits at boot, and the latest_schema_migration RPC exists so the guard's read cannot be failing open). So they are applied and pushed; nothing here blocks a push. This matters because CLAUDE.md's standing held-migration rule says a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator applies the SQL — so a stale HELD note tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, and invites a pointless prod session. The genuinely pending migrations are ONLY 00475 (US-1880) and 00476 (US-1897); PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's reconciliation header is the source of truth.

userStories.title: [OPERATOR] Apply to eBay for the sell.logistics scope so label buying switches on
userStories.description: US-2160 shipped the whole eBay Sell Logistics slice — rate shopping, label purchase, reprint, void, the real postage landing in sales.shipping_cost, and a capability gate so a seller without the scope sees a clean surface instead of a 403. None of it can actually run: sell.logistics is a limited-release scope, our prod keyset is not granted it, and the scope is deliberately kept off the default consent list for that reason. So every deployment today takes the feature_unavailable path by design. This is the same shape as US-1421 for sell.negotiation, and the same operator action: apply to eBay on the prod keyset, then turn it on.
acceptanceCriteria: Apply to eBay for the limited-release sell.logistics scope on the prod keyset.
Once granted, add sell.logistics to EBAY_SCOPES and force a re-consent at /oauth/start; connected sellers are told a reconnect is required.
Verify createShippingQuote and createShipmentFromQuote against a prod token, and confirm logistics_access_denied clears on the first success.
Buy one real label end to end and confirm the postage lands in sales.shipping_cost and the tracking number reaches the eBay fulfillment.
userStories.notes: [OPERATOR][FlipDesk/eBay] Blocked on eBay, not on code — do not assign this to an agent. Sits next to US-1421 (sell.negotiation), which is the identical application for a different restricted scope; if you are filing one, file both in the same sitting. The capability gate means nothing breaks while this is pending: the reconnect_required vs feature_unavailable split (US-1967) already distinguishes 'your token predates the grant' from 'this deployment never asked'. AC4 matters more than it looks — a label purchase is deliberately never retried, because eBay offers no idempotency key there and a retried 5xx buys and bills a second label.

userStories.title: No max_rows contract on any FlipDesk read — an over-cap seller could be shown a silently truncated catalog
userStories.description: As a reseller past whatever row cap PostgREST enforces, I want to be told my view is truncated, so I never make pricing or sourcing decisions on a quietly incomplete inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: The self-hosted PostgREST db-max-rows value in prod is established and recorded in vault/10-ops
Reads that could exceed it either paginate explicitly or request one row past their cap and surface a 'showing N of more' state
No FlipDesk surface can silently render a truncated set as if it were complete
The chosen cap is asserted in config so a future infra change can't move it unnoticed
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. Nothing in supabase/config.toml or docker-compose.coolify.yml sets a row cap, so the effective value is whatever the self-hosted PostgREST default is — unverified either way. If a cap IS in force, the unbounded reads in US-2167/US-2168 truncate with no error and no indication. Verify before assuming this is benign; the fix is cheap either way. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — AC2, AC3 and AC4 are MET; AC1 needs one operator step that cannot be done from this host, and the code is deliberately built not to depend on it. FINDING THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the story asked whether a cap is in force. It is not knowable from here (nothing sets db-max-rows in supabase/config.toml, which configures only the throwaway local verify stack, nor in docker-compose.coolify.yml, which is the edge service and not Kong/PostgREST), and worse, TWO EXISTING PAGING LOOPS were only correct while the cap was at least their page size — src/hooks/use-items-full.ts and src/pages/flipdesk/bulk-pricing.tsx both advanced by their CHUNK constant and broke on a short page. Below the ceiling every request comes back capped-short, so the loop stops on its FIRST request and the paging written to prevent silent truncation performs it instead. So rather than establish the number and depend on it, the reads no longer need to know it. NEW src/lib/paged-read.ts owns three things: fetchAllPages() advances by the rows ACTUALLY RETURNED and stops only on an EMPTY response (never a short one), so any ceiling costs round trips and nothing else; fetchCapped() asks for limit+1 and drops the probe row so the truncated flag is evidence rather than a guess; and READ_PAGE_SIZE / ASSUMED_DB_MAX_ROWS / CAPPED_READ_LIMIT name the assumption once. AC2 MET: use-items-full.ts and bulk-pricing.tsx now call fetchAllPages; listing-performance.tsx's flat .limit(1000) became a paged read (a cut at 1000 hid exactly the low-view tail the report exists to surface); autolister-drafts.tsx and scheduled-drops.tsx use fetchCapped. Every remaining fixed .limit() in FlipDesk is small enough (25/100/200) that it cannot reach any plausible ceiling. AC3 MET: NEW src/components/flipdesk/truncated-notice.tsx renders 'Showing the first N …. There are more.' on both capped queues. reconcile.tsx's link picker was the worst case and was not truncation at all — it fetched the 200 most-recently-UPDATED items and then filtered client-side to photo_count===0 + linkable status, so a seller whose recent touches were all photographed saw an EMPTY picker while plenty of candidates existed; the cap was silently choosing the WRONG 200 rows. Both predicates now run server-side (.eq(photo_count,0).in(status,…)) so the limit applies to real candidates, and a search that finds nothing against a capped pool now says the pool was capped instead of implying no such item exists. AC4 MET: NEW src/test/row-cap-contract.test.ts (13 cases) asserts CAPPED_READ_LIMIT+1 <= ASSUMED_DB_MAX_ROWS (or the +1 probe stops being answerable and the notice goes silent again), exercises fetchAllPages against a server that clips EVERY response at 137 rows against a 1000-row catalog, and scans src/ for both regression shapes — a hand-rolled short-page-break loop (.length < CHUNK then break) and any for-loop over .range() outside the shared reader. AC1 PARTIAL: vault/10-ops/postgrest-row-cap.md records the contract, the three allowed read shapes, why stop-on-short is wrong, and that the prod value is NOT established — with the operator step named. REMAINING: read db-max-rows off the self-hosted stack and record it in that note. VERIFIED: 2957 tests pass (232 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors (10 pre-existing warnings), build green, vault-lint 107 notes clean, impeccable clean on the new component. | 2026-08-01 AC1 MEASURED (not read from config - stating the difference because it decides whether this story closes). Probed prod PostgREST directly from an authenticated browser session against api.gradethread.com: item_photos?select=id&limit=100000 returned 1055 of 1055 rows (Content-Range 0-1054/1055) with no clip, and the same probe over the six largest RLS-reachable tables (inventory_items 840, listings 751, submission_images 266, sales 176, submissions 38) came back complete every time. SO: there is NO cap at or below 1055, which answers the question the story was actually filed to answer - nothing is being silently truncated at current volumes, and ASSUMED_DB_MAX_ROWS=1000 is either right or conservative, both safe because fetchAllPages advances by rows RETURNED. What is still not established is the literal db-max-rows value: it cannot be proven from a client without a table larger than the cap, and the largest one that exists is 1055 rows. PostgREST's own default is unset and nothing in the stack config sets it, so unset is the most likely answer. Recorded in vault/10-ops/postgrest-row-cap.md with the evidence, its limits, and a re-measure trigger (any single tenant table passing ~1000 rows) rather than a calendar reminder. KEPT passes:false because AC1 as WRITTEN asks for the value, and a bound is not the value - that is the owner's call to amend, not an agent's. RECOMMENDATION: amend AC1 to 'no cap is in force at the volumes we run, evidenced and re-measurable' and close, since the exact number is something the code is deliberately built not to depend on. | 2026-08-02 UNBLOCKING STEP, not a close. This story's last open AC needs a prod read, and so do four others -- US-2009 AC2 (column/version completeness), US-2021 AC3 (email_deliveries reclaim), US-2006 AC3 (unpurged past-retention imagery), US-2041 AC4 (disputes decided on a misrounded grade). That is five separate asks of the one person who can answer them, which is how a question stops being asked: each has sat open for weeks reading "needs prod access". NEW scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql answers all five in ONE psql session, so it is one paste instead of five conversations. Strictly read-only -- no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/ALTER/DROP -- and the heaviest query is a catalog size lookup rather than a scan, so it is safe during business hours. The output contains no keys, tokens, email addresses or image paths, which is stated in the header so the operator can paste it back without redacting. A MISTAKE CAUGHT BEFORE IT REACHED THE OPERATOR, and it is the reason this shipped with a test rather than a careful read: my first draft joined disputes.resolved_at. That column has never existed. The table's terminal states are enum values on `status` ('resolved','rejected') and `updated_at` is the only timestamp that moves with them. psql stops at the first error, so a wrong column name does not degrade into a partial answer -- it fails the whole session on prod and leaves an operator who now distrusts the entire file. NEW src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts holds both properties: no write verb may appear in the executable body (word-boundary matched, so updated_at does not read as UPDATE), and every table.column pair the script joins must be findable in a CREATE TABLE or ADD COLUMN across the migration corpus -- parsed, not hand-listed, so an unrelated rename fails here instead of on prod. Plus a case pinning disputes.resolved_at specifically, because it is the obvious name to reach for, and a case asserting all six advertised sections still exist so the header cannot end up lying about what the operator gets back. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED BOTH by injecting the two real mistakes -- a DELETE and the resolved_at join -- confirming each landed before trusting the result, watching both cases fail with the right messages, then restoring and confirming zero occurrences. VERIFIED: full web suite 244 files / 3126 tests 0 failed, eslint 0 errors. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not close any of the five stories. It converts each from "needs prod access" -- which nobody can act on -- into "run one command and paste the output", which is a five-minute operator task. The stories close when the answers come back. | Done 2026-08-05. AC1 ESTABLISHED — the last open criterion — so this is RESOLVED. AC2/AC3/AC4 were met on 2026-08-01 (paged-read.ts, truncated-notice.tsx, row-cap-contract.test.ts); those notes stand. THE ANSWER: there is NO row cap. db-max-rows is UNSET in prod. The 2026-08-01 pass could only prove a BOUND — it pulled 1055 of 1055 rows from the largest RLS-reachable table with no clip, which rules out a cap at or below 1055 but cannot detect a ceiling you never reach, and it explicitly kept passes:false because 'a bound is not the value'. This pass read the CONFIGURATION instead: SELECT rolname, rolconfig FROM pg_roles WHERE rolconfig IS NOT NULL. PostgREST connects as the authenticator role and with db-config on (default since v10) takes its settings from that role; on prod that role carries session_preload_libraries=safeupdate, statement_timeout=8s and lock_timeout=8s, and NO pgrst.db_max_rows. Three independent channels now agree and each rules out what the others cannot — the probe rules out any cap <=1055, the role config rules out an in-database setting, the repo rules out a committed one (config.toml is the throwaway local stack; docker-compose.coolify.yml is the edge service, not Kong/PostgREST). The only channel not read from here is a PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS env var on the PostgREST container, and a value there at or below 1055 would have clipped the probe — so the sole survivor is a cap ABOVE 1055, which fetchAllPages is deliberately built not to depend on because it advances by rows RETURNED. THE MORE USEFUL FINDING, and it inverts the story's premise: the bound that actually bites is a CLOCK, not a row count. anon=3s, authenticated=8s, authenticator=8s statement_timeout. A read is not silently truncated after N rows; it is KILLED after N seconds. That is the better failure of the two — an error rather than a short array with error:null — and it needs no new remedy, because the fix is the same paging this story already shipped: many bounded round trips each finish well inside 8s, while one unbounded query over a growing table works and works and then starts failing outright. The 3s anonymous budget is worth knowing before adding a join to a public certificate/passport/sitemap endpoint. RECORDED in vault/10-ops/postgrest-row-cap.md, whose summary and 'What the prod value is' section were rewritten with the measurement and the query that produced it, and whose re-measure trigger was RETIRED: the old one was volume-based ('when a table passes ~1000 rows') because the answer was a bound and a bound expires as data grows. A read of the configuration does not, so the trigger is now 'after any PostgREST reconfiguration' — with a standing note that the TIMEOUT is the thing to watch as volume grows. The vault note reviewed date was bumped to 2026-08-05 having actually re-read the code_refs: admin-dashboard.ts changed on 2026-08-05 but only swapped a column name (users.plan -> flipdesk_plan, US-2398) inside a count/head query, leaving the READ SHAPE this note governs unchanged. LOOSE END for the operator, not for this story: the 2026-08-02 note bundled five stories into scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql. Two of them (this one and US-2398) are now closed by real prod answers; US-2009 AC2, US-2021 AC3 and US-2006 AC3 are still waiting on sections 1-4 of that same script.

userStories.title: Four admin metrics are computed from users.plan, a column nothing has written since 2024
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the admin dashboard's paid-user count, churn estimate and plan mix to reflect who is actually paying, because today they are computed from the DEPRECATED users.plan column. 00001 defines it NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free'. 00039 backfilled flipdesk_plan FROM it — the legacy-to-new direction, one time — and deliberately kept the legacy column. A repo-wide search finds NO write to users.plan anywhere since: not in services/edge-functions (no .update({ plan: ... })), not in any migration (no SET plan =). So every user who subscribed, upgraded, downgraded or churned after 00039 still carries the value the backfill left, which for anyone who signed up afterwards is the DEFAULT 'free'. Four live metrics read it: 00514_admin_metrics_service_role_guard.sql:207 totalPaid = count(*) where plan <> 'free'; :215 churnFreeWithActivity = where u.plan = 'free' (the churn NUMERATOR); 00513_admin_dashboard_aggregates.sql:172 planDistribution grouped by plan; :181 topUsers[].plan. MRR is NOT affected — 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql joins pricing_plans on u.flipdesk_plan, which is correct and is why this went unnoticed: the headline revenue number is right while the counts beside it are not.
acceptanceCriteria: totalPaid, churnFreeWithActivity, planDistribution and topUsers[].plan read flipdesk_plan (or a documented mapping), not the frozen users.plan.

Vocabulary is handled deliberately: users.plan is user_plan ('free'|'starter'|'professional'|'enterprise') while flipdesk_plan is ('free'|'starter'|'pro'|'business'). A count of <> 'free' needs no mapping; planDistribution and the topUsers badge do, or they will show two spellings of the same tier.

Measure the size of the error before and after against prod, so the correction is quantified rather than asserted — an operator who has been reading these numbers needs to know by how much they moved and from when.

Decide the fate of users.plan itself: either drop it (US-2365 removed the last frontend PLANS alias, so this is the remaining reader) or document what still owns it. A column nothing writes and several things read is the state that produced this.
A guard fails the build if a new query reads users.plan, so the column cannot quietly acquire a fifth reader.
userStories.notes: [P2][Admin/Metrics] Found 2026-08-03 while acting on a note in US-2365 that turned out to be WRONG — recorded here because the correction is the useful part. That note said 'the admin revenue chart computes MRR from users.plan'. It does not: 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql prices MRR by joining pricing_plans on u.flipdesk_plan, which is correct. I re-verified before acting instead of trusting my own earlier note, and the real defect is adjacent and larger — MRR is right, and the paid COUNT, the churn estimate and the plan mix sitting next to it on the same dashboard are not. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE NUMBER: totalPaid undercounts every subscriber acquired since the backfill, and churnFreeWithActivity uses the same frozen column as its numerator — so churn% is inflated by the same users that totalPaid is missing. The two errors compound in the same direction, which makes the dashboard tell a consistent story about a business that is doing worse than it is. A number that is obviously broken gets questioned; a plausible one does not. NOT YET FIXED, and deliberately: the fix replaces two RPCs, so it is a migration, and 00524 is already held awaiting the owner. Filing it with the evidence rather than stacking a second held migration unasked. AC3 (measure the error against prod) wants doing in the same pass, since the before/after is only available before the fix ships. | 2026-08-03 AC1 + AC2 + AC5 DONE. Migration 00525 is HELD (standing rule) and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. THE COUNT IN THIS STORY WAS WRONG: I filed FOUR readers, there are SIX. The build script warned that a bare plan remained after my replacements, and the two extras were a second planDistribution inside admin_system_metrics and a subscribed count inside admin_platform_analytics — both bare-column forms my original grep missed because it keyed on u.plan and on specific line numbers. The story text above understates it; this note is the correction. 00525 replaces both functions WHOLE via CREATE OR REPLACE rather than patching, so re-running is safe and the definitions stay readable in one place. Built by EXTRACTING the current definitions programmatically rather than retyping ~250 lines, because a hand-copy is where a silent divergence gets introduced. AC2 (vocabulary) handled deliberately: a count of <> free needs no mapping, and planDistribution + the topUsers badge now report the LIVE tier names — professional/enterprise stop appearing because they were only ever the frozen vocabulary. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, not by reading: applied the full corpus to a fresh throwaway stack (00001..00525 all applied clean), then queried pg_get_functiondef for both live functions — admin_system_metrics and admin_platform_analytics each contain flipdesk_plan and NO legacy reference. AC5 DONE: src/test/legacy-user-plan-readers.test.ts now also pins that 00525 itself is not a reader, which is what distinguishes replaced from still-broken given that the superseded 00513/00514 text stays on disk forever. REMAINING: AC3 (measure the error against prod before/after) is an owner task and is only available BEFORE the apply — worth capturing the current totalPaid and churn numbers first. AC4 (decide whether to drop users.plan) stays open; 00525 removes the last live readers, so the column is now unread as well as unwritten. EXPECT THE DASHBOARD NUMBERS TO MOVE ON APPLY: paid users up, churn down. Nothing is recalculated retroactively — it starts reading the column the rest of the system already uses. | 2026-08-05 THE COUNT WAS WRONG A SECOND TIME, AND THE REASON IS THE POINT. This story was filed as FOUR readers; the 00525 pass found SIX; all of them were SQL, and the guard written to stop a seventh (AC5) SCANNED MIGRATIONS ONLY. The column is read from two languages. Scanning one and declaring the readers enumerated is what let the count be wrong twice — so this pass audited the TypeScript layer and found SEVEN more, two of which are not cosmetic.  BEHAVIOURAL, not display: (1) drip.ts:677 fed users.plan into the drip campaign branch field (drip-graph.ts fieldValue case 'plan'), so any step conditioned on plan took the FREE-TIER branch for every paying seller, and admin-drip.ts's dry run read the same column so the preview agreed with the bug rather than exposing it. (2) admin-flags.ts sampled users.plan to preview a flag's reach AND published the frozen vocabulary (free/starter/professional/ enterprise) as the valid targets, so a plan-targeted rule named tiers no live account can hold. (3) admin-dashboard.ts:146 counts active subscriptions with .neq('plan','free') — a SEVENTH metric, invisible to 00525 because it is a PostgREST filter in TS rather than SQL. (4) src/pages/admin/users.tsx filtered AND badged the admin user list off it, so 'Professional' returned only pre-backfill accounts and 'Free' returned everyone. Plus admin-fraud.ts and admin-safety.ts, which label the account beside a suspension decision. ALL of the above now read flipdesk_plan; admin-flags accepts the legacy spellings and rewrites them (professional→pro, enterprise→business) on save rather than rejecting a rule someone is mid-edit.  AC5 EXTENDED to the code: src/test/legacy-user-plan-readers.test.ts now scans services/edge-functions/src, src and functions for three query shapes — a column list naming `plan`, a `.update({ plan … })` write, and an .eq/.neq('plan') filter (the shape BOTH the dashboard count and the user-list filter were hiding in, and the one a select-only scan misses). Tightened twice against real false positives before it was trustworthy: a bare "plan" literal is a chart dataKey / switch case / CSV header far more often than a query, and `.update({ flipdesk_plan: plan })` — the commonest write in the repo — matched five files until the pattern required `plan` to be a KEY. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by planting a reader and watching it fail, then removing it.  AC3 IS STILL MEASURABLE AFTER THE APPLY, which the earlier note assumed it would not be. The legacy column is FROZEN: users.plan still holds exactly what the dashboard used to read and flipdesk_plan holds what it reads now, so the before and after are two counts over one table. NEW §17 in scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql: paid_before vs paid_after, the counted-as-churned-but-actually-paying overlap (both errors ran the same direction), the monthly divergence curve for 'since when', and the plan mix in both vocabularies. ⚠️ It only works while the column exists — do NOT drop users.plan before running §17.  AC4 IS NOW THE ONLY THING BLOCKING THIS, and the evidence for it is complete. After this pass users.plan is read by NOTHING that grants anything. Its last reader is also its last writer: POST /api/admin/users/:id/plan (admin-users.ts, added by US-2376). That route's own comment claimed it was 'the entitlement column the monthly grade allowance and every plan gate read' — VERIFIED FALSE across the repo: the allowance, the gates, MRR and the AI-action caps all read flipdesk_plan (payments.ts:1168, flipdesk-grading.ts:230, 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql). So an operator comp grant returns ok/changed:true, writes an audit row, and moves no entitlement. The false comment is corrected in place; the behaviour is left alone because rewiring a billing-scoped, step-up-gated route is the owner's call. AC4 = rewire that route to flipdesk_plan, or delete it and drop the column (after §17).  VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, deno lint + deno check clean on all 7 edge files, edge tests 76/0 (feature-flags, drip-graph, drip-send-gate, tenant-isolation), web src/test 738 passed / 2 failed — both pre-existing and reproduced on a stashed tree (react-router-8-contract, responsive-images). | 2026-08-05 AC4 DECIDED AND BUILT (owner: rewire the grant, don't drop the column). Only AC3 is left, and it is an operator paste.  THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN A FAKE FIX: pointing the route at flipdesk_plan is not enough on its own. effectivePlanFor() (grade-pricing.ts) demotes a paid plan to Free whenever subscription_status is 'none' or 'canceled' — which is exactly what a cardless account carries — so the grant would have written a real column and the seller's caps would still have read Free. The route would have kept reporting success and kept doing nothing, which is the same defect with a better-looking commit. NEW MIGRATION 00529 (HELD, packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md) adds a 'comp' value to the subscription_status enum: it entitles because it is not one of the non-entitling statuses, and it earns no MRR because 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql counts only 'active' and 'past_due'. effectivePlanFor checks it FIRST and explicitly rather than by fall-through, so a future status rule cannot silently un-grant every comp.  THE ROUTE NOW REFUSES the inverse case: an account whose status is active / trialing / past_due / paused gets a 409 with code EXTERNALLY_BILLED pointing at Change plan (Stripe). A direct write there would hold until the next webhook and then be overwritten — the operator sees the grant land and the user loses it later with nothing to point at, which is worse than refusing. Revoking a comp (grant → free) clears the status back to 'none', and only when this route owns it: an account already sitting at 'none' is left untouched.  SECOND-ORDER FIX the comp forced, and it would have been an ops papercut nobody traced: billing-reconciliation's detectDivergence compares cached state against the last recorded Stripe event. A comped ex-subscriber's last event is the cancellation, so every comp would have sat in the reconciliation queue permanently reading "cached 'comp' vs expected 'canceled'" with nothing to reconcile. Comps now short-circuit as not-diverged, with a test.  TWO MORE READERS FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS, both missed by the query-shaped scan because they read an already-fetched profile object rather than naming the column. (1) src/pages/bulk-submission.tsx gated bulk upload on profile.plan ∈ ['professional','enterprise'] — the frozen column — so a paid feature was LOCKED FOR EVERY CUSTOMER WHO HAS EVER PAID FOR IT, and had been since the backfill. Now ['pro','business'] off flipdesk_plan. (2) platform-analytics.tsx keyed PLAN_ORDER / PLAN_COLORS by the legacy names, so after 00525 started reporting the live vocabulary every planDistribution lookup resolved to 0 and every revenue slice lost its fill — a chart of zeros introduced by the previous pass's own fix. Both now use FlipdeskPlanKey. settings.tsx / dashboard.tsx / bulk-ai-enrich-dialog.tsx were checked and are FINE: they already prefer flipdesk_plan and only fall back to the legacy translation when it is null, which cannot happen (NOT NULL).  AC5's guard now asserts the code scan is EMPTY rather than enumerating known readers — users.plan is unread by every line of application code. Because a clean tree makes an all-clear indistinguishable from a broken matcher, the non-vacuous case moved to fixtures: each shape it claims to catch (column list, update-key, .eq/.neq filter) and each near-miss it must not report (flipdesk_plan: plan, case "plan", flipdesk_plan lists) is asserted directly.  REMAINING — AC3 ONLY, and it is five minutes of operator time: run §17 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql. ⚠️ users.plan must still EXIST when it runs; it is the only surviving record of what the dashboard used to say. Drop the column AFTER that, not before.  VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, deno lint + check clean, full edge suite green, web src/test 737 passed / 3 failed — all three pre-existing and unrelated (react-router-8-contract, responsive-images, and report-thresholds, which passes 10/10 in isolation and only fails under parallel load). iOS deliberately untouched: entitlingStatuses there answers 'who owns this subscription' for manage-billing routing and never gates a feature, so a comped account shows its granted tier from flipdesk_plan with no release needed. | Done 2026-08-05. AC3 MEASURED AGAINST PROD — the last open criterion — so this story is RESOLVED. The operator ran section 17 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql. THE ANSWER IS STARKER THAN THE STORY GUESSED: paid_before 0, paid_after 13, undercounted 13, overcounted 0, total_users 13. Not 'the paid count was somewhat low'. It was ZERO. Every single account on the platform holds a paid flipdesk_plan (12 pro + 1 business, per the plan-mix query), users.plan reads 'free' for all thirteen because the 00039 backfill is the last thing that ever wrote it, and so the admin dashboard reported a platform with no paying customers at all. The churn numerator read the SAME frozen column, so churnFreeWithActivity counted all 13 payers as churned free users: the two errors did not merely compound in the same direction, they saturated — 0% paid beside 100% churn, a perfectly self-consistent picture of a business with no customers, sitting next to an MRR figure that was correct the whole time because 00215 already joined flipdesk_plan. WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH READING TWICE: the story argued a plausible-but-wrong number does not get questioned the way an obviously-broken one does. At 13 users the operator KNOWS there are paying customers, so the dashboard was contradicting something they could see — and it still went unnoticed for long enough to accumulate seven SQL readers and nine TypeScript ones. The lesson is not about the size of the error. THE FIX IS LIVE: 00525 was applied to prod 2026-08-04 (owner-confirmed in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md) and prod /health/ready reports schema expected 00529 / applied 00529 / match, measured just now rather than inferred from commit history — the same discipline the US-1897 note had to correct itself into. So the dashboard is already reading flipdesk_plan; the numbers above are the size of what it used to be wrong by, not a pending change. AC4 was decided and built in the previous pass (rewire the admin comp grant to flipdesk_plan + the 'comp' subscription_status of 00529, rather than dropping users.plan) — and the column is deliberately KEPT, which section 17 has now justified retroactively: it is the only surviving record of what the dashboard used to say, and dropping it would have destroyed the evidence above before anyone measured it. AC1/AC2/AC5 were completed and verified in the earlier passes (00525 replaces both RPCs whole; the guard now asserts the code scan is EMPTY across SQL, edge TS, web TS and functions/, with the non-vacuous case moved to fixtures). NOTHING further is outstanding.

userStories.title: Category rubric activation was never filed — 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and nothing ever writes them
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the non-clothing grading scaffolding either finished or removed, because right now it is neither. Migration 00231 added grade_reports.factor_scores (jsonb) and rubric_key (text) to production, and the grading pipeline writes only the five TYPED clothing columns (fabric_condition_score … odor_cleanliness_score) — verified: the grade_reports insert in grading-pipeline.ts reads compositeResult.factor_scores.* into those five columns and never sets factor_scores or rubric_key. So both columns are permanently NULL on every row in prod. The edge module services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts is imported by nothing. Its client counterpart src/lib/rubrics.ts IS live — certificate.tsx:39 imports rubricForKey — so the certificate page is ready to render a rubric that the server will never populate. The only record of intent is commit bbd94005 'feat(grading): category rubric foundation (non-clothing scaffolding)', which says the work is 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline' and that the activation follow-up 'is documented in rubric.ts'. That follow-up was never filed as a story, so it has been invisible to the backlog ever since.
acceptanceCriteria: DECIDE FIRST: activate or remove. Non-clothing grading (sports cards etc.) is a product question, not a cleanup — do not default to whichever is less work

If ACTIVATING: the pipeline writes rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing categories; the five typed clothing columns keep their current meaning for clothing; the public cert endpoint's CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS allowlist is extended deliberately (00231's own comment defers that exposure to 'the activation phase')

If REMOVING: rubric.ts is deleted, src/lib/rubrics.ts and its certificate.tsx usage are resolved, and a migration drops the two dead columns — do NOT leave them NULL-forever with no owner, which is the state this story exists to end

Either way a drift guard: services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts and src/lib/rubrics.ts are declared to stay in sync and NOTHING pins them today. If both survive, add a shared behavioural fixture asserted by both suites (the same remedy US-1995 asks for on title-sync)
The decision is written into the story notes so the next reader does not have to re-derive it from a commit message
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Cleanup] Found 2026-07-18 by scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs — rubric.ts was one of 10 whole modules nothing imports. ⚠ CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM in this session's audit triage (US-1996 notes): the triage said 'exhaustive queries return no story mentioning rubric'. That is wrong — NINE stories mention it (US-1030, US-1031, US-1532, US-1534, US-1682, US-1948, US-1951 archived, plus US-1995/1996). I read each: they all use 'rubric' in the generic grading-criteria sense (wrinkle anchors, fabric-aware criteria, pSEO guides, homepage copy). None owns the CATEGORY-rubric activation this story covers. The conclusion stood; the stated evidence did not, which is why it is restated correctly here. P3 rather than P1 because there is no user-visible breakage: clothing grading is unaffected and the certificate simply never renders a rubric block. The cost is a permanently-NULL pair of prod columns, a dead edge module, and a live client module waiting on data that never arrives. | 2026-07-23 DECISION: ACTIVATE (owner, via AskUserQuestion) — non-clothing grading (sports cards / watches / shoes) is on the roadmap, so the scaffolding is kept and built out, not removed. Activation is a MULTI-PHASE program, not a single commit; this session landed the two pieces that are safe and completable in a sandbox and scoped the rest with a plan. REFRAME (important for the next reader): the columns are 'permanently NULL' NOT because clothing forgot to write them but BY DESIGN — clothing renders from the 5 typed columns; factor_scores/rubric_key exist to hold NON-CLOTHING scores, which don't exist until the grading pipeline actually grades non-clothing. Backfilling clothing INTO factor_scores would be redundant AND stale-prone (the human-review reseal + adjustment write paths at grading-pipeline.ts:570/813/965 update only the typed columns), so it was deliberately NOT done. DONE THIS SESSION: (AC4 drift guard) added src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json — the SHARED behavioural fixture (same remedy US-1995 used for title-sync) constraining key+label+weight; both suites assert against it — client src/lib/__tests__/rubrics.test.ts (10/10 GREEN in-sandbox) and edge services/edge-functions/src/tests/rubric-parity_test.ts (mirrors it; not deno-run here). Verified edge rubric.ts and client rubrics.ts already match exactly across all 4 rubrics, so the guard pins them without a reconciliation. (AC2 partial) extended CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS (content-public.ts) to expose factor_scores + rubric_key in the null-safe EXTRA set, so a non-clothing cert will serve its rubric once Phase 2 writes it; NULL clothing certs are unaffected (client already prefers them only when both present, else falls back to typed columns) and the 42703 genesis-fallback still protects clothing certs under 00231 drift. Verified web tsc -b + eslint clean; no test pins the CERT column string. REMAINING (Phase 2 — the actual non-clothing grading; CANNOT be done in this sandbox, needs a validatable env with deno + live traffic + real vision calls): (1) de-gate submissions.garment_type NOT NULL for non-clothing (rubric.ts checklist #1); (2) generalize the THREE lockstep rounding sites (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) from the hardcoded 5 clothing factors to variable rubric-driven factor sets, same commit; (3) build per-category composite prompts from rubric.factors/promptGuidance and route defects via rubric.defectRouting; (4) run those NEW prompts through the mandated prompt lifecycle — shadow-compare (grading-shadow.ts) -> golden-set eval gate (grading-eval.ts) -> canary — which REQUIRES a non-clothing golden set that does NOT yet exist (golden cases grow from real human-corrected grades, so Phase 2 needs a bootstrap: grade some non-clothing behind a flag, collect expert corrections, THEN gate); (5) persist rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing across ALL grade_reports write paths (insert + reseal + adjustment) to avoid the stale-JSONB bug above. KEPT passes:false: AC2 (non-clothing writes) + AC4-is-done-but-story-spans-more; the product feature is not live until Phase 2 ships through the eval gate. AC1/AC5 (decision documented) satisfied here.

userStories.title: EPIC: Public 'What's It Worth' — free photo -> grade + resale value
userStories.description: As a curious owner/seller, I want to upload a photo with no login and instantly get an AI condition grade AND a resale value estimate so that I get immediate value and a reason to sign up and certify.
acceptanceCriteria: One flagship free tool combines the grade-checker's AI grade with a condition-adjusted resale value (already available to the authed Snap tool) with no login required
Result is shareable and funnels clearly to signup / free Snap / paid certification
Abuse controls (per-IP limits, aggregate-only value, AI budget ceiling) preserved
userStories.notes: [P2][FREE-TOOL][EPIC] BASELINE (mostly built): unauth POST /api/grading/public/grade-check (public-grading.ts, 5/hr/IP, grade only, nothing persisted) backs /tools/grade-checker; authed Snap-to-Value (grade.ts /snap, snap.tsx) already returns value via valueAtGrade + condition_price_curves. quickGrade (quick-grade.ts) is the shared primitive. TECH/3P: none new. TIES: value index (EPIC 1), share cards (EPIC 9), signup funnel. BUYER/OWNER: instant free answer. SELLER: pricing + grading entry. Child stories: add value to free endpoint, shareable result card + funnel. | Done 2026-08-05. EPIC RESOLVED — both child stories shipped and are archived passes:true, and all three epic ACs were re-verified against the CODE rather than taken from the children's own notes. This pass found the work already complete and closed the parent, which nobody had gone back to do. AC1 (grade + condition-adjusted value, no login) MET: publicGradingRoutes.post('/grade-check') in services/edge-functions/src/routes/public-grading.ts:650 runs quickGrade() on the single photo, then — when brand or keyword identifies the item enough to comp it — suggestCategories() to a leaf and valueAtGrade({categoryId,q,brand}, overallScore) for the grade-positioned range, mirroring the authed /snap path. Shipped by US-1751. AC2 (shareable + funnels) MET: src/pages/tools/grade-checker.tsx builds a STATELESS OG card (shareCardUrl -> functions/og/grade-check.ts) carrying grade, tier, the aggregate range and the typed brand/item entirely in the query string — no stored result and no PII — plus onShare() using navigator.share with a clipboard fallback, a share landing URL tagged utm_source=share&utm_medium=result-card so the channel is attributable, and both funnel CTAs (/how-it-works for paid certification, /signup) instrumented via onCtaClick. Shipped by US-1752. AC3 (abuse controls preserved) MET and this is the AC worth re-reading, because it is the one an epic-level close would normally hand-wave: three independent bounds, each verified present. (1) PER-IP — gradeCheckRateLimited() at GRADE_CHECK_PER_IP_PER_HOUR=5, keyed by clientIpFor(), which proves the request transited Cloudflare and reads CF-Connecting-IP rather than the spoofable X-Forwarded-For; a request with no trustworthy IP collapses to ONE shared sentinel bucket, a degraded ceiling but never unlimited. (2) AGGREGATE-ONLY — publicValueFromRange() is a deliberate subset of the internal ValueRange (low/median/high/sampleSize/confidence/currency) and returns NULL unless range.sufficient, so the anonymous surface is gated HARDER than /snap: no falsely-precise number, no per-listing price, no PII. (3) AI BUDGET — the shared ai-limiter's global daily ceiling bounds Vision spend inside quickGrade, and an AiCeilingError returns a distinct non-retryable 503 (US-1883 AC3) rather than a generic 500 so a client stops retrying and burning quota. Also confirmed: the value lookup is best-effort inside its own try/catch, so a taxonomy or comp hiccup degrades to value:null and never fails the grade. NOTHING WAS BUILT IN THIS PASS and that is the finding — US-1751 and US-1752 both closed on 2026-07 and the epic stayed open behind them, which is how a delivered feature keeps reading as in-flight on the board. Worth a glance at the other open EPIC rows for the same shape. NOT IN SCOPE and still open on its own row: US-1843 ('What's It Worth' -> BUYER signup conversion funnel) references this epic but belongs to the buyer-platform program, not here.

userStories.title: Extension: store distribution + install funnel

userStories.notes: [P2][EXTENSION][NEW][GROWTH] Privacy policy page (Model A static route). Attribution reuses affiliate.ts click->conversion. Telemetry opt-in only (GDPR/CCPA posture, ties to legal geo-consent epic). [OPERATOR-GATED 2026-07-09] Core deliverable (AC1: publish to Chrome Web Store + Firefox AMO with screenshots/listing copy) is NOT automatable from this host — needs store developer accounts + a running browser to capture screenshots. AC3 attribution: the referral system (src/lib/affiliate.ts) attributes via a per-SELLER ?ref=<code>; a buyer-side extension has no seller code, so extension->signup is channel-level (utm_source=extension), not per-referrer. Deferred until an operator runs the store submission; codeable residue to pair with that: extension privacy-policy static page, opt-in telemetry toggle + endpoint, store-listing copy doc. Not marking passes; mirrors the US-1582 [OPERATOR] split. Extension CODE is done via US-1755/US-1756. | 2026-07-18 AC1 PRIVACY-POLICY HALF DONE. Found a genuine store-submission blocker: /privacy is live and returns 200, but it did NOT mention the extension anywhere — while extension-unified/SUBMISSION.md instructs the operator to submit that exact URL to the Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO, both of which require the submitted policy to disclose the extension’s data use. A reviewer following our own submission doc would have landed on a policy silent about the product being reviewed. Added section 6, The GradeThread browser extension, covering: what a condition read sends (public photo URLs + title/brand/price on user action, reading the page you are already on, never browsing on your behalf); that diagnostics are OFF BY DEFAULT and carry no listing, page address, account or install identifier (the selector-health telemetry I added this session under US-1880 AC3 — the policy now matches the code); that seller cross-posting runs in the user’s own tab and marketplace passwords/cookies are never sent; and the gradethread.com message relay. Every claim is checked against the shipped code rather than the marketing copy. Renumbered sections 7-14 and fixed the one Section-N cross-reference. New privacy-extension.test.tsx (6 cases) pins the disclosures so they cannot silently vanish, INCLUDING a sequential-numbering assertion and a cross-reference integrity check — I got the numbering wrong by hand while inserting the section, so the test encodes the mistake I actually made. Verified: tsc clean, lint exit 0, full web suite green. REMAINING on this story is operator-gated exactly as the notes say: store submission needs developer accounts + a browser for screenshots (AC1), AC2 usage telemetry (reads/click-throughs) is distinct from the selector-failure telemetry already shipped though it can reuse the same consent toggle, and AC3 attribution is channel-level utm_source=extension. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) SECOND, WORSE GAP OF THE SAME CLASS — the AUP. extension-unified/popup.js:84 points the consent clickwrap’s "Read the terms" link at /acceptable-use, next to a checkbox reading "I understand the Lister fills forms in MY browser session and that I am responsible for each marketplace’s Terms of Service." That page is live (200) and mentioned "extension" 0 times, "cross-post" 0, "cross-list" 0, "Lister" 0 — a consent gate whose linked terms never described the thing being consented to. Worse than the privacy gap because this one IS the legal basis for the seller automation (the versioned, revocable clickwrap US-1885 AC3 built). Added section 6, The browser extension and assisted cross-posting: the automation runs in the user’s own logged-in session and we never receive marketplace passwords or cookies (so responsibility sits with them); some marketplaces restrict or prohibit assisted listing and their rules take precedence; review before publishing; no evading listing caps, rate limits, suspensions or bans; no operating others’ accounts. Renumbered 7-9 and cross-linked to Privacy section 6. New acceptable-use-extension.test.tsx (6 cases) pins the disclosures + sequential numbering, and — the important one — READS extension-unified/popup.js to assert the termsLink still points at /acceptable-use, so repointing the popup fails the build instead of silently orphaning the clickwrap again. Verified: tsc clean, lint exit 0, full web suite green. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) Swept the rest of the extension’s outbound references — all clean. Every gradethread.com URL the extension sends a user to (/, /acceptable-use, /connect-extension, /pricing, /privacy, /extension/marketplace-selectors.json) returns 200 live, so the two gaps found today were about CONTENT, not dead links. Extended the same cross-artifact check to CLAUDE.md and added a durable guard: scripts/doc-refs.mjs + doc-refs.test.mjs, wired into verify:web beside prd-lint. CLAUDE.md currently cites 29 paths, 0 missing. Two of my own bugs are pinned as regression cases: (1) an alternation-ordering bug — ts listed before tsx matched the head of a .tsx path and reported four files missing that exist, the same mistake as COMPLETED? failing to match COMPLETION in the prd-lint guard; (2) contextual roots — CLAUDE.md legitimately writes lib/supabase.ts inside a paragraph about the edge service, so the checker resolves against known roots the way a reader does rather than flagging correct prose. Both matter for the same reason: a guard that reports correct writing gets switched off, which is how every unreliable check in this repo ended up ignored.

userStories.notes: [P2][BADGE][EPIC] BASELINE (infra built): functions/badge/cert/[id].ts (), functions/embed/cert/[id].ts (script), text fallback; snippet gens in src/lib/verified.ts (certBadgeEmbedHtml/certBadgeScriptEmbed/certBadgeEmbedText); render via cert-image-render.ts + cert-og-template.ts (buildCertBadgeHtml) + SLAB_FORMATS; public_passport_links bridges cert<->passport; cert-share-actions.tsx already bakes referral codes. CONSTRAINT: no cross-site iframe (X-Frame-Options DENY / frame-ancestors none) — must stay img/script/text. TECH/3P: existing satori+resvg-wasm, no new 3P. TIES: certificate, passport, verified directory, referral/affiliate. BUYER: trust signal on any marketplace. SELLER: paste-in credibility. Child stories: badge studio UX, click attribution+analytics, new formats. | Done 2026-08-05. EPIC RESOLVED — all three children (US-1759 studio, US-1760 attribution, US-1761 formats + storefront) are archived passes:true, and every AC was re-verified against the code. AC1 MET: src/components/verified/badge-studio.tsx + src/hooks/use-badge-studio.ts give one-click snippets from the three generators in src/lib/verified.ts — certBadgeEmbedHtml (img wrapped in a link), certBadgeScriptEmbed, certBadgeEmbedText — for a certificate or passport, with public_passport_links bridging the two. AC2 MET, and this is the one I nearly reported as MISSING: a grep for 'badge_clicks' returned nothing and I was about to say the funnel did not exist. The real names are badge-click / recordBadgeClick / badge_click_events, and the chain is complete: the snippet's href is certificateShareUrl(certId,'embed') → ?s=embed → certificate.tsx reads searchParams.get('s') and POSTs /api/content/public/badge-click → recordBadgeClick (lib/badge-analytics.ts) inserts into badge_click_events (migration 00404) → read back by sellerBadgeFunnel() in routes/verified.ts for the seller's own surface and platformBadgeFunnel() in routes/admin-growth.ts for the operator dashboard. Privacy holds at the recorder: the owner is resolved SERVER-SIDE from the cert id or handle and never trusted from the caller, only known ?s= sources are recorded, and a malformed ping returns ok:false rather than surfacing validation detail to a public endpoint. Worth recording that the near-miss was a NAMING gap, not a code gap — an epic closed on a grep for the wrong noun would have re-opened work that already shipped. AC3 MET: rendering goes through cert-image-render.ts SLAB_FORMATS via functions/badge/cert/[id].ts, which is deliberately a thin PROXY streaming bytes from the Deno edge rather than rendering in the Pages Function (workers-og blew the Free-plan Worker CPU limit and returned 503 'error code: 1102'); it stays a plain cacheable img with a transparent-PNG fallback on any upstream error, and the img/script/text triad exists precisely because the cross-site iframe route is closed by X-Frame-Options DENY / frame-ancestors none. NOTHING WAS BUILT IN THIS PASS. The children closed in 2026-07 and the parent row stayed open behind them — same shape as US-1750 and US-1795, all three found by one sweep for open EPIC rows whose children are all passes:true.

userStories.title: EPIC: Buyer Platform — buyer accounts, subscription, and the confidence layer
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to extend the seller-focused product into a two-sided buyer/seller platform whose sole purpose is increasing confidence in item listings, so that buyers pay a recurring subscription for point-of-purchase confidence AND their demand for graded items pulls more sellers into paying for grading (a two-sided flywheel).

Every buyer feature reuses (does not duplicate) an existing capability where one exists — extension US-1753, fit US-1776/1777, authenticity US-1767, video US-1762, circularity US-1785, What's-It-Worth US-1750, badges US-1758, Value Index US-1745, buyer guarantee US-867/guarantee_remedies — and is bound to the buyer entitlement layer

STRATEGY: the unique asset is objective per-item condition data + the grade_outcomes dataset (condition->realized price); the buyer product monetizes 'claimed condition vs objective condition, at the point of purchase'. TIERS (confirmed): Free / Guard (~$8/mo) / Connoisseur (~$19/mo). FLYWHEEL: buyer demand for graded items -> sellers must grade to sell -> more graded inventory -> better buyer product. TIES: reuses capability EPICs US-1745/1750/1753/1758/1762/1767/1776/1785 + buyer guarantee US-867. SEQUENCING: foundation (US-1795 sub-epic) ships first; idea sub-epics (US-1805+) depend on it. Child sub-epics: account+subscription foundation (1795), alerts (1805), grade-confirm rewards (1810), buyer trust score (1815), insured grade-locked guarantee (1819), wardrobe portfolio (1824), graded-wanted board (1829), extension confidence suite (1833), buyer bindings for existing capability epics (1839-1844), cross-cutting analytics/legal/QA (1845-1847).

Child stories: account model+account_type (1796), signup/onboarding (1797), profile+preferences (1798), plans+Stripe products (1799), entitlements+gating+metering (1800), billing surfaces (1801), dashboard shell+nav (1802), notification/alert delivery infra (1803), mobile IAP mirror (1804). MUST load the migrations skill for every table; MUST load tenant-isolation skill for every edge route. | Done 2026-08-05. EPIC RESOLVED — all NINE children named in this story's own notes are archived passes:true (US-1796 account model, 1797 signup/onboarding, 1798 profile+preferences, 1799 plans+Stripe products, 1800 entitlements+gating+metering, 1801 billing surfaces, 1802 dashboard shell, 1803 notification/alert infra, 1804 mobile IAP mirror), and the foundation is verifiable in the tree rather than only in their notes. AC1 MET: the buyer surface exists as its own page set — src/pages/buyer/{home,onboarding,settings,billing,portfolio,alerts,guarantee,demand,rewards}.tsx — on the reused Supabase-PKCE + Stripe + TanStack Query stack the epic specified, so a buyer signs up, onboards, saves preferences, subscribes and lands on a dashboard without a parallel auth or billing stack. AC2 MET: migration 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql introduces account_type, which is what lets one person be both buyer and seller without a duplicate identity. AC3 MET: services/edge-functions/src/lib/buyer-plans.ts is the shared entitlement resolver behind the buyer route family (buyer-profile, buyer-wants, buyer-closet, buyer-purchases, buyer-trust, buyer-authenticity, buyer-rewards), so client and edge gate off one definition rather than two drifting copies. AC4 MET per the children's migration-triple and tenant-isolation work. NOTHING WAS BUILT IN THIS PASS — the value here is closing a row that had been reading as in-flight since 2026-07 while nine of nine children shipped. FOR THE NEXT READER: this is a FOUNDATION epic, so closing it does NOT mean the buyer platform is finished. The parent program US-1794 and the feature epics above it stay open, and US-1805 (condition-based alerts) still has US-1808 (extension-fed listing ingestion) open under it. Closing this one says the plumbing every downstream buyer feature attaches to is in place, which is exactly what the story asked for and no more.

userStories.title: EPIC: Condition-based alerts & watchlist ('snipe on grade, not price')
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want to be alerted when an item matching my brand + size + minimum objective grade + max price appears so that I catch well-graded deals no marketplace filter can surface — because they filter on the seller's self-reported condition, not GradeThread's objective grade.
acceptanceCriteria: A buyer can create saved searches / watchlists keyed on brand, size, category, minimum GradeThread grade, and max price, and be notified on matches
Matching runs over GradeThread-graded inventory (public_grade_reports / graded listings) and, where available, extension-fed marketplace listings the buyer is browsing
Alert frequency and number of active alerts are entitlement-gated (Free: none/limited; Guard: standard; Connoisseur: unlimited/instant)
This umbrella tracks US-1806…US-1809
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][ALERTS][EPIC][NEW] BASELINE: no watchlist/saved-search/alert primitive exists anywhere (grep confirmed). Unique angle: filter on OBJECTIVE grade, impossible without the grading engine. DATA: public_grade_reports view + graded listings + grade_outcomes; buyer preferences (1798) as defaults. DELIVERY: notification infra (1803). TIES: extension ingestion (1808) feeds off-platform listings. Load durable-jobs skill for the matching cron. Depends on foundation (1795). Child stories: model (1806), matching engine (1807), extension ingestion (1808), delivery+UI (1809).

userStories.title: Alerts: extension-fed marketplace listing ingestion
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want listings I browse on marketplaces to count toward my alerts and watchlist so that GradeThread can flag matches even for items not yet on our platform.
acceptanceCriteria: The buyer extension can submit a browsed listing (URL + images + seller-claimed fields) to a hardened buyer-scoped endpoint that grades it and evaluates it against the buyer's saved searches
Ingested listings are rate-limited, quota-metered per entitlement, and SSRF-guarded (reuse the public grading endpoint hardening)
Matches from ingested listings notify via the same path as on-platform matches; ingested data respects marketplace ToS (buyer's own browsing, no bulk scraping)
Ingestion is tenant-scoped to the submitting buyer
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][ALERTS][EXTENSION][NEW] Reuse public-grading.ts hardening (gradeCheckRateLimited + safeFetch SSRF guard + quickGrade). This is the bridge between the extension (1833) and alerts. Quota via entitlements (1800). RISK: marketplace image-scraping ToS — constrain to buyer-initiated, per-listing, no crawling. Load tenant-isolation skill.

userStories.title: Buyer binding: Walk-around video grading credits for buyers
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want to request a walk-around video grade so that I get a richer condition read before committing to a higher-value purchase.
acceptanceCriteria: Video grading (US-1762/1765/1766) is available to buyers as an included/credit-metered action gated by entitlement (Connoisseur or credit packs)
Buyer-requested video grades reuse the existing capture + metering (cost = frames x per-image), with plan-based caps
Results surface in the buyer's item/portfolio context
Metering/debit reuses the credit precedence (1800)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][BINDING][VIDEO] REUSE US-1762 epic (metering 1765, capture 1766). Buyer credits via entitlements (1800). Cost math per US-1765 (frames x per-image). Depends on foundation (1795) + video epic (1762).

userStories.title: Buyer binding: 'What's It Worth' → buyer signup conversion funnel
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the free public grade+value tool to convert into buyer signups so that our top-of-funnel feeds the buyer subscription.
acceptanceCriteria: The public 'What's It Worth' tool (US-1750) gets buyer-oriented conversion moments (save this result, set an alert for it, verify future purchases) that route into buyer signup (1797)
Anonymous results can be claimed into a new buyer account without loss (session->account handoff)
Conversion is attributed (affiliate/referral) end-to-end
No change to the free tool's abuse controls
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][BINDING][GROWTH] REUSE US-1750 What's-It-Worth epic. Add buyer CTAs (save/alert/verify) -> signup (1797) with anon-session claim handoff. Attribution via affiliate.ts. Depends on foundation (1795) + What's-It-Worth epic (1750) + alerts (1805).

userStories.title: Buyer platform: analytics, funnel & revenue instrumentation
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the buyer funnel and feature usage instrumented so that we can measure conversion, retention, feature value, and the two-sided flywheel and optimize revenue.
acceptanceCriteria: PostHog events across the buyer funnel (public tool -> signup -> subscribe -> feature use -> retention) and per-feature usage (extension checks, alerts, confirmations, guarantee claims, portfolio, wants)
An admin buyer-growth surface (extend admin-growth) shows conversion, MRR by tier, feature adoption, and flywheel metrics (buyer demand -> seller grading)
Revenue attribution ties buyer subscriptions and metered credits back to acquisition source
Events are privacy-compliant (opt-in where required)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][ANALYTICS][GROWTH] Reuse PostHog + admin-growth surface + affiliate/referral attribution. Flywheel metric = buyer-demand -> seller-grading correlation. Depends on foundation (1795); instruments all buyer epics.

userStories.title: Buyer platform: legal, privacy & consent (PII, guarantee terms, extension)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the buyer platform's legal and privacy posture right so that we handle buyer PII lawfully and the guarantee/extension are compliant.
acceptanceCriteria: Buyer PII (body profiles, purchase history, preferences, reputation) is classified sensitive, RLS-protected, with data-export/delete honoring existing privacy flows and geo-consent
Guarantee/coverage terms + authenticity/fraud-flag copy are legal-reviewed before ship (confidence estimates, not definitive claims)
Extension privacy policy + opt-in telemetry (US-1757) cover the buyer confidence suite's data flows
Consent surfaces respect the existing legal geo-consent framework
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][LEGAL][PRIVACY] Reuse existing privacy/geo-consent framework + SECURITY.md posture. Coverage terms (1819) + fraud-flag copy (1836) + authenticity disclaimers (1840) all need legal review. Extension privacy ties to US-1757. Cross-cutting across all buyer epics.

userStories.title: EPIC: GradeThread Rewards — gamified grade -> share -> reward viral loop
userStories.description: As a user, I want to earn points, levels, badges, streaks and real rewards for grading items, completing activities, and sharing my finds so that engagement is fun and habit-forming — and as GradeThread I want the built-in loop (grade -> auto-generated share overlay -> social share -> reward -> public showcase -> new signups) to be our primary viral growth engine.
acceptanceCriteria: A rewards system supports BOTH cosmetic rewards (XP, levels, badges/medals, streaks, leaderboard rank, profile/overlay flair — free and unlimited) AND tangible rewards (free grade credits, subscription discounts, discounted grading — budget-capped and anti-abuse-gated)

The core loop is frictionless: grade an item -> get an auto-generated shareable overlay card -> share it -> the share (and verified click-throughs) earn rewards -> the find can appear in a public showcase feed
All reward earning is event-sourced, idempotent, fraud-resistant, and tangible-reward payout is capped to protect unit-economics margins with an admin kill-switch
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][EPIC] BASELINE (rails already built to reward ON): grade credits via grant_grade_credits RPC + grade_credit_transactions; referral_milestone_grants (reward-on-threshold precedent); referral_campaign_codes -> immediate credits (redemption model to mirror); Stripe billing in payments.ts; share renderer cert-image-render.ts + SLAB_FORMATS + cert-share-actions.tsx (referral-baked share); cert view/click tracking (content-public.ts /view ?s=) + affiliate_clicks/referral_events attribution; leaderboard opt-in (referrals.ts, referral-leaderboard.tsx) + verified directory. GAP (greenfield): no XP/points, levels, badges/achievements, streaks, quests, showcase feed, or redemption-of-XP-for-rewards. TECH/3P: none new (all in-stack: Postgres event ledger, Stripe coupons, existing renderer). TIES: EPIC 9 (US-1781/1782 auto grade-reveal cards) is the share engine this loop rides; referral/affiliate for attribution; verified directory for leaderboards; unit-economics (Pro 750 / Business 2000 AI-action caps, 40% margin floor) constrains tangible rewards; admin-fraud/admin-safety for anti-gaming; notifications/drip for re-engagement; feature_flags for kill-switch. BUYER: showcase feed to browse cool finds (SEO + social). SELLER/USER: fun, status, streaks, real discounts, effortless sharing. ECONOMICS RULE: cosmetic rewards unlimited; tangible rewards MUST be capped + fraud-gated + margin-aware. Child stories: points engine, achievements, levels/streaks, quests, tangible redemption, share-to-earn, showcase feed, leaderboards, rewards UI, economics/anti-abuse, re-engagement.

userStories.title: Rewards: event-sourced XP/points engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want an idempotent, event-sourced points ledger so that every rewardable activity grants XP exactly once and the whole system is auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: New reward_events (append-only: user_id, event_type, xp_awarded, source_ref, dedupe_key, created_at) + user_reward_state (xp_total, level, current_streak, longest_streak, updated_at) tables, tenant-scoped RLS
A grantReward(userId, eventType, sourceRef) primitive is idempotent on dedupe_key (e.g. grade:{submissionId}, share:{cardId}) so replays/retries never double-award

Rewardable events wired at their source with per-event XP configured in a catalog; the catalog is weighted by business/moat contribution (coverage completed, badge embedded off-platform, aspects filled, marketplace connected, arrival confirmed, verified share-click) rather than raw effort
Events that consume real AI spend (grading) only award XP when the action was PAID or credit-consuming — free/junk submissions earn nothing, making grade-XP self-limiting against farming

This is the ONE reward ledger for BOTH the seller/user track (US-1848 epic) and the buyer Trust Score track (US-1815..1818) — buyer scoring stories consume this engine and must not build a parallel one

userStories.title: Rewards: levels, seasons & buyer-side streaks
userStories.description: As a user, I want to level up through seasons of activity so that regular engagement is rewarding — without a streak mechanic that punishes the bursty, seasonal rhythm of reselling.
acceptanceCriteria: XP thresholds map to named levels/tiers (e.g. Thrifter -> Picker -> Curator -> Archivist -> Legend) shown as progress toward the next level; level is derived from user_reward_state.xp_total and NEVER decreases

Seller-side activity uses quarterly SEASONS (a season track with goals + season-end recap/rewards that resets cleanly) instead of weekly streaks — a slow sourcing month never destroys accumulated status; recency competition lives on the weekly leaderboards (US-1856), not on identity

Calendar streaks exist only where a genuinely daily/weekly surface exists — the buyer extension + confirmation flow (US-1814) — with grace/streak-freeze rules; seller surfaces show season progress instead
Levels unlock cosmetic perks (profile flair, exclusive share-card frames/overlays) with no hard paywall
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME] Level thresholds + season logic in a rewards lib; season rollover timezone-aware (reuse scheduled-drops tz handling). Cosmetic overlay frames = additional cert-image-render templates gated by level. No tangible cost = unlimited. Refined 2026-07-09: streaks are the wrong loyalty primitive for bursty resellers — replaced with seasons; streaks kept buyer-side only. Tenure/loyalty tiers split out to US-1914. | Done 2026-08-07. AC1: LEVEL_TIERS (Thrifter/Picker/Curator/Archivist/Legend) in edge lib/rewards-levels.ts, bands placed at the tangible milestones; levelProgress() feeds the bar; monotonicLevel() in rewards-engine.ts floors every user_reward_state write so a level NEVER decreases. AC2: lib/rewards-seasons.ts - quarterly seasons with 4 goals, derived as a WINDOW over reputation_events so there is no rollover job and NO new migration (9 are already held); paid/verified gate still applies to goal ticks. AC3: src/lib/buyer-streak.ts - the only human-facing streak, with a free grace week and 2 freezes per quarter budgeted by the quarter of the MISSED week; buyer/rewards.tsx shows at-risk vs freezes-left. AC4: cosmetic-only perks - flair on the verified seller profile (edge payload + SSR + SPA, tier vocabulary only, no XP leaked) and level frames painted onto the cert slab share card, cache-keyed by frame. Read API: GET /api/rewards/me + /seasons/:key/recap behind authMiddleware. VERIFIED: 57 edge reward tests green (rewards-levels_test 21, rewards-seasons_test 22), 15 buyer-streak vitests, 5 flair-parity vitests; tsc -b clean, eslint clean, deno check clean, ui:check 0 findings.
