userStories.title: Rewards: quests & time-boxed challenges (personal + community)
userStories.description: As a user, I want quests and seasonal challenges so that there's always a fresh reason to come back and grade/share.
acceptanceCriteria: Personal quests (e.g. 'grade 3 items this week', 'share 1 find', 'add measurements to 5 items') with progress tracking and XP/reward on completion
Time-boxed community/seasonal challenges (e.g. 'Best thrift find of the month') that can feed the showcase feed and leaderboards
Admin-configurable quest definitions (criteria, window, reward) with start/end and a kill-switch
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME] Migration triple for quests (config, deny-all) + user_quest_progress (tenant RLS). Progress derived from reward_events. Community challenges tie to the showcase feed + leaderboards. Admin CRUD via a new admin surface (mirror admin-growth patterns). | Done 2026-08-07. AC1: personal quests — edge lib/rewards-quests.ts scores a quest as WINDOW + PREDICATE + PAYOUT; progress derived from reputation_events (no user_quest_progress table, same reasoning as US-1851 seasons); GET /api/rewards/quests returns the live board. Completion is paid automatically inside grantReward (no claim step to forget), keyed on <quest_key>:<window-start> so a weekly quest pays once per week and again next week. AC2: window_kind fixed + scope community give time-boxed challenges; the showcase-feed and leaderboard tie-in is US-1855/US-1856 and is NOT built here. AC3: admin CRUD at /admin/growth/quests (edge routes in admin-growth.ts under the existing growth:write scope + audit log). Criteria are code predicates picked from a server-supplied list, not free text; quest_key is not patchable; new rows are enabled=false and the whole surface sits behind the fail-closed rewards_quests flag. Payout clamped to 200 XP on write AND on every re-score. DO NOT PUSH until the SQL is applied to prod. userStories.title: Rewards: milestone-granted tangible rewards (credits + discounts) — XP is never spent
userStories.description: As a user, I want crossing XP/badge milestones to GRANT me real perks (free grade credits, subscription/grading discounts) so that engagement pays off — without spending XP, so my level and leaderboard rank never go backwards for redeeming.
acceptanceCriteria: XP is permanent and only ever accrues (status currency: levels, leaderboards); tangible value is granted when crossing configured milestones — XP is NEVER debited. Spendable currency is the existing grade-credit ledger, not XP

A milestone-rewards catalog (reward_type free_grade_credits | subscription_discount | per_grade_discount, trigger = XP threshold | badge | season goal, value, monthly + lifetime caps) that admins configure

Granting free grade credits reuses grant_grade_credits into grade_credit_transactions; subscription discounts issue a Stripe coupon/promo applied in payments.ts; per-grade discounts apply at the payment-precedence step
Every grant is recorded in a redemption/grant ledger, is idempotent per (user, milestone), respects per-user and global caps, and cannot double-issue
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][BILLING] Migration triple for milestone catalog + user_reward_grants ledger. Credits reuse grant_grade_credits (as referral_campaign_codes already do). Stripe coupon path in payments.ts (subscribe/downgrade). Per-grade discount hooks runPaymentPrecedence (grade-billing.ts). MUST enforce caps from US-1858. Refined 2026-07-09: spend-XP model replaced with milestone-grant model — spending XP deflates status, penalizes redeemers on leaderboards, and invites hoarding; milestone grants avoid all three.

userStories.title: Rewards: share-to-earn loop (auto overlay -> verified share -> reward)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to be rewarded for sharing my graded finds so that showing off my finds is both fun and worthwhile — the core viral trigger.
acceptanceCriteria: Sharing a grade's auto-generated overlay card (from EPIC 9 / US-1782) creates a tracked share and grants XP; bonus XP/credit for VERIFIED click-throughs (real visits via the referral-baked link), not merely pressing share
Anti-gaming: rewards key off attributed unique clicks/signups (affiliate_clicks/referral_events), rate-limited, with fraud checks so self-clicking/bots can't farm rewards
A 'Viral Find' badge + escalating rewards for finds that drive N verified click-throughs or a signup
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][SHARE][GROWTH] Depends on EPIC 9 US-1782 (auto reveal card) + cert-share-actions.tsx referral bake + cert_view ?s= + affiliate_clicks/referral_events. Reward on verified conversion, not raw share, to prevent farming. Fraud gate via admin-fraud.ts + rate_limit_counters.

userStories.title: Rewards: public Showcase / 'Finds' feed
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want a public feed of cool graded finds so that I get inspired, discover GradeThread, and want to grade my own — and as a user I want my best finds featured.
acceptanceCriteria: An opt-in public showcase feed of graded finds (photo + grade + optional value + verified seller link), with filters (brand, category, grade, trending) and reactions/upvotes
Feed entries are SEO-indexable (edge-SSR Pages Function, Model B) with Product/ItemList JSON-LD and link to the certificate and seller profile
Featured/trending finds surface on the landing page and feed community challenges/leaderboards; only public, non-PII, seller-consented items appear
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][SEO][SHARE] Model B Pages Function (clone condition-index/[[path]].ts) + public edge endpoint over grade_reports (public_grade_reports view) filtered to opt-in/showcased. Reactions table (tenant RLS). Ties verified profiles + certificate. Sitemap + _routes.json + PWA denylist. Consent required (mirror verified_show_listings).

userStories.title: Rewards: leaderboards (weekly / all-time / category)
userStories.description: As a competitive user, I want leaderboards so that I can climb ranks for finds, grades, XP, and shares.
acceptanceCriteria: Leaderboards for XP, grades, best finds, and share-driven signups (weekly, all-time, and by category/brand), opt-in with a public alias
Built on the existing referral leaderboard opt-in + verified directory; anti-gaming safeguards and tie-breaks

userStories.title: EPIC: Thrift Radar — crowdsourced store-level sourcing intelligence ('Waze for thrifting')
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want to know which local stores are currently producing high-value finds for my brands — before I drive there — so I spend my sourcing hours in the right places. Every Prospect scan already carries the raw signal (location, brand, estimated grade, buy/pass verdict); aggregated across opted-in users it becomes a live map of secondhand supply that no listing-tool competitor can replicate without first building a grading-quality scanner and a fleet of users pointing it at store racks.
acceptanceCriteria: This is the umbrella/epic story — it does not ship code itself; child stories US-1861..US-1867 implement it.

Privacy stance (non-negotiable): contribution is strictly OPT-IN (default off); contributions are anonymized and aggregated at store/venue granularity only; no precise user coordinates retained after venue resolution; network aggregates are displayed only above a k-anonymity floor of distinct contributors.
The personal layer (US-1864) must be independently useful at n=1 with zero network data — that is the cold-start answer.
Monetization: network layers (map hotness, venue detail, route planner) are plan-gated Pro+; the personal history layer is free on all plans.
Viewing Radar and contributing to Radar are separate consents — using the map never silently enrolls you as a contributor.
userStories.notes: [EPIC][P2 Growth][FlipDesk][Scout] Parent of US-1861..US-1867. Origin: founder ideation session 2026-07-09 ('the Waze of secondhand sourcing'). Builds on the existing Prospect/Scout scan path (flipdesk-scout.ts, scout.tsx, iOS Prospect module). Distinct from US-1064 (per-user insights) — this is the cross-user network intelligence layer; distinct from US-1829 demand board (buyer demand, not store supply). Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: opt-in scan telemetry + consent & privacy model
userStories.description: As a privacy-conscious user, I want Radar contribution to be explicitly opt-in, anonymized, and clearly explained, so sharing where I source never exposes me or my spots to identification.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds radar_scan_events: rotating anonymized contributor key (no readable user_id in the analytical path), venue_id (or geohash cell while unresolved), brand, category, estimated grade band, buy/pass verdict, timestamp. Raw scan coordinates are NOT retained after venue resolution. Deny-all RLS, service-role writes only; register in rls-guard_test.ts.
Settings toggle 'Contribute to Thrift Radar' (web + iOS), DEFAULT OFF; Prospect scans emit Radar events only when it is on.

Consent copy states exactly what is shared and at what granularity; privacy policy gains a Radar section; iOS App Privacy declarations updated for location use consistent with the US-1214 opt-in posture.
Contribution is fire-and-forget: a Radar-event failure never degrades or slows the Prospect scan result itself.
New/changed edge routes carry tenant-isolation_test.ts cases (tenant-isolation skill); migration follows the US-1108 triple (migrations skill).
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar][Privacy] Child of US-1860. The consent boundary is the whole story — get this wrong and the feature is a liability. Emit from the existing prospect scan handler behind the flag. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: store venue resolution + registry
userStories.description: As the Radar system, I need to resolve raw scan coordinates into named, deduplicated store venues (Goodwill on Main St, Savers on Route 9), so intelligence accrues to places rather than coordinate soup.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration adds radar_venues: display name, centroid (lat/lng), geohash, chain tag (goodwill / savers / salvation_army / value_village / other), status (candidate / confirmed).
Resolver maps scan coordinates to the nearest known venue within a distance threshold; unresolved scans create a candidate venue (or bin to a geohash cell) that later scans converge onto.
Chain normalization: 'Goodwill Store #123' and 'Goodwill Industries' resolve to the same chain tag; per-venue identity stays distinct.
Dedupe merge path for near-duplicate candidate venues; unit tests cover threshold resolution, candidate creation, and merge.
Migration follows the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar] Child of US-1860. Keep it dependency-free: no external Places API required for v1 (chain inference from scan density + optional user naming); design the schema so a Places enrichment can be added later without rework. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: Thrift Radar: aggregation engine + k-anonymity floor
userStories.description: As the Radar system, I need scheduled aggregation that turns anonymized scan events into venue-level intelligence (brand density, grade quality, freshness) that is only ever served above an anonymity floor.
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduled aggregation job (durable-jobs conventions: claim/heartbeat/reclaim, cron_runs visibility) computes venue x brand x time-window stats: scan count, distinct-contributor count, average estimated grade, buy-verdict rate, last-activity freshness.

K-ANONYMITY FLOOR: aggregates for a venue x window are served only when distinct contributors >= K (configurable, default 3). Below the floor the venue shows no network data — enforced server-side, with a test proving a below-floor venue returns nothing.
Raw radar_scan_events older than the retention window are rolled up and pruned; retention is configurable.
Read-only edge endpoint serves aggregates (venue list by bounding box + venue detail); responses contain no per-user or per-contributor data.
deno tests cover the aggregation math, k-floor enforcement, and retention pruning; migration follows the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Radar] Child of US-1860. Load the durable-jobs skill for the job pattern and the migrations skill for the rollup tables. The k-floor is a hard privacy guarantee, not a display preference. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: EPIC: Inventory Equity — graded-inventory valuation (GradeThread Capital, Phase 1 ONLY)
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want to see the estimated liquidation value of my graded inventory — the capital sitting on my racks — so I understand what my stock is actually worth at current market prices and how much of it is unvalued because it is ungraded. Strategic context: this is Phase 1 of the 'GradeThread Capital' concept. It is display-only analytics built entirely from data we already have (grades, sold comps, Value Index condition curves, personal sell-through). It also creates the strongest organic grading incentive in the product: the more you grade, the more of your inventory is valued.
acceptanceCriteria: This is the umbrella/epic story — it does not ship code itself; child stories US-1869..US-1871 implement it.

SCOPE FENCE (founder decision 2026-07-09): Phase 1 is DISPLAY-ONLY valuation. Phase 2 — working-capital advances / lending against inventory (e.g. via the Stripe Capital platform program) — is EXPLICITLY DEFERRED due to legal and financial-responsibility concerns. No Phase 2 child stories exist by design; do not create them.

No new AI spend: valuation composes existing grade data, cached comps, and Value Index curves within existing comp-refresh quotas (US-1749 guardrails).

userStories.title: EPIC: Unified GradeThread extension — one install, role- and subscription-aware (buyer research for everyone, seller tools on top)
userStories.description: As a GradeThread user, I want ONE browser extension that gives every user the buyer-research surface (AI condition read on eBay/Poshmark/Grailed/Mercari/Depop/Vinted listings) and additionally unlocks the seller cross-posting Lister tools when I'm signed in as a seller, so I don't manage two installs — and sellers doing sourcing/comping get the same buyer research in the same session. Founder decision 2026-07-09: this supersedes the deliberate two-extension split (extension/ US-716 vs extension-condition/ US-1755/1756). Features gate on the signed-in GradeThread account's role and subscription tier.
acceptanceCriteria: Umbrella/epic story — child stories US-1873..US-1885 implement it; it ships no code itself

Target architecture: a single extension folder (merge extension/ + extension-condition/) with one manifest carrying both permission sets (marketplace host_permissions + gradethread.com), a shared background service worker, and a feature registry that exposes: condition-read overlay = always on (anonymous allowed, quota-capped), Lister cross-post/delist = only when authenticated with seller entitlements

Auth/entitlements reuse the signed extension token planned in US-1838 (buyer-subscription gating), extended to carry seller role + FlipDesk plan so one token answers both 'can this install cross-post' and 'what buyer quota applies'

Privacy posture is re-documented for the merged permission set (the old 'not host-permitted on gradethread.com' Lister claim no longer holds once merged — the privacy story becomes 'no cookies permission, no marketplace credential access, marketplace automation stays on-device') and store listing copy/privacy policy are rewritten accordingly (feeds US-1757)
The two legacy folders are removed once the unified extension reaches parity; READMEs updated; US-1757 (store distribution) targets the unified extension only
userStories.notes: Origin: 2026-07-09 extension deep-dive (3-agent audit of extension/, extension-condition/, and server integration). Related open stories NOT duplicated here: US-1833..1846 (buyer confidence suite + gating + legal), US-1757 (store distribution), US-1808 (extension-fed ingestion). Audit found the Lister privacy-by-manifest posture genuinely enforced today — the merge deliberately trades that isolation for one-install UX, so the privacy copy rewrite is mandatory, not cosmetic. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC4's STORE-KIT half done. The README's privacy posture had been rewritten for the merged permission set; SUBMISSION.md — what a store reviewer actually reads — had not, and carried three inaccuracies: (1) the gradethread.com host justification said only 'call the grading API / receive the token' and OMITTED that gt-bridge.js is a CONTENT SCRIPT injected into every gradethread.com page — exactly the privacy trade this epic exists to document; now stated plainly incl. why (Firefox has no externally_connectable) and what it does NOT do (reads no page content, forwards only our envelope), and the privacy-policy summary discloses it too; (2) it cited *://*.gradethread.com/* — we request https:// only, and *.gradethread.com does not match the apex in Chrome match patterns (hence the manifest carrying both); (3) it named v0.3.0 artifacts while the manifest is 0.3.5 and package-extensions.mjs derives zip names FROM the manifest, so the kit pointed at files that never existed. New extension-unified/test/submission-kit.test.cjs guards all of it (version match + only-that-version; every permission justified — 'alarms' shipped unjustified for 4 days until caught by hand, and that is a store rejection; every host justified; the bridge disclosed whenever the manifest injects it). Both new guards verified to fail on reintroduced drift. 12/12 extension test files. STILL OPEN: AC1 is umbrella-only (ships no code); AC5 needs the legacy extension/ + extension-condition/ folders removed once the unified reaches parity (US-1757 distribution targets unified only); children US-1880/1881/1882/1883/1884/1885 still open, and US-1873 is now VERIFIED COMPLETE.

userStories.title: Research surface: verify the five unverified adapters, fix the dead Poshmark upgrade rule, close intl host gaps, add selector-failure ping
userStories.description: As a shopper on any supported marketplace, I want the condition read to actually work there. Audit: 5 of 6 adapters are verified:false; the Poshmark image URL-upgrade regex ('/s_[a-z0-9]+/') requires a path-segment form that real CloudFront URLs don't use, so thumbnails get graded (selectors.js:71); manifest match gaps — eBay only 5 TLDs (missing fr/it/es/at/ch/ie/nl/pl/be), Vinted missing ~12 TLDs and matches are www-only while adapters accept apex, poshmark.ca subdomains unmatched; the 'corrected from telemetry' claim has no telemetry anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of Poshmark/Grailed/Mercari/Depop/Vinted verified against the live site: gallery/title/brand selectors + URL-upgrade rule produce full-res images on a real listing; verified:true + lastVerified set in BOTH config files (Poshmark's upgrade rule fixed to the filename form with a test using a real URL shape)

Manifest + adapter hosts cover the agreed international footprint (at minimum: eBay fr/it/es/ie/nl/at/ch/pl/befr-benl, all active Vinted TLDs incl. apex domains, *.poshmark.ca) — one list, generated or guard-tested against the adapter hosts so manifest and config can't drift

An anonymous, opt-in-gated selector-failure ping (adapter key + which selector list came up empty + config version, NO listing URL/user data) posts to a lightweight edge endpoint so broken adapters are discovered from telemetry as the README claims — consent + toggle shared with US-1757's telemetry story
srcset parsing picks the max-width candidate instead of assuming last-is-largest
Unknown/failed adapters keep degrading to the honest 'couldn't read the photos' state
userStories.notes:
Audit findings 4/6/15/26. The telemetry AC deliberately reuses US-1757's opt-in consent — don't build a second consent surface.

PARTIAL 2026-07-13 (agent loop — doable slices; story stays passes:false). DONE: (AC1 regex portion) fixed the dead Poshmark URL-upgrade rule — was /s_[a-z0-9]+/ (path-segment form real CloudFront URLs never have, so thumbnails got graded); now /(?:s|m|t)_(?=[^/]*$) matching the filename size-prefix, with a real-URL-shape test. (AC2) added intl hosts to the ebay adapter (fr/it/es/ie/nl/at/ch/pl/be) and vinted (be/at/ro/hu/sk/pt/se/lu/hr/gr/dk/fi) in BOTH config files; rewrote manifest content_scripts matches to canonical https://*.<host><path>* (the *. form covers apex+www+country subdomains, fixing the www-only + *.poshmark.ca gaps); new test/manifest-hosts.test.cjs derives the match set from adapters and fails on any drift (proven to catch missing+orphan). (AC4) srcsetLargest() picks the max-width candidate (was last-token) — wired into marketplace.js firstSrcFromAttr, unit-tested incl. comma-in-URL. (AC5) honest degrade unchanged/preserved. Config version bumped 2026.07.4->2026.07.5 in both files (lastVerified left 2026-07-10 — NOT live-reverified). NOT DONE (blocks passes): AC1 verified:true requires live-site QA of all 5 adapters (cannot do autonomously — verified flags left false); AC3 anonymous selector-failure edge ping needs a new endpoint + the shared opt-in consent from US-1757. Verified: node scripts/test-extensions.mjs green (3 files), node --check, both JSON valid, drift-guard negative checks. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). AC3 DONE: the anonymous selector-failure ping exists end-to-end. Migration 00475_selector_health_pings.sql (operator table, deny-all RLS, registered in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY) + POST /api/grading/public/selector-health in public-grading.ts + a popup opt-in toggle + the content-script report. ⚠ CONSENT DECISION MADE, NOT CONFIRMED BY THE USER: the AC says reuse US-1757's opt-in consent, but NO telemetry consent exists anywhere in the repo — the only consent surface is the Lister ToS clickwrap (tosAcceptedAt), which is legal acceptance for automating a seller's marketplace account and only renders behind caps.sellerEnabled. Gating on it would have collected nothing from anonymous research users, who are the entire population that hits a broken adapter. So this reuses the PATTERN (versioned/revocable key, renderConsent/wireConsent shape) under a separate selectorTelemetry storage key, default OFF, revoke deletes the key rather than storing false. Revisit if US-1757 meant something else. PRIVACY IS SERVER-ENFORCED, not client-trusted (the extension is user-modifiable): the endpoint takes a CLOSED vocabulary — 6 known adapter keys, 6 known selector-list names, version strings capped at 32 chars and charset-limited to [w.-] — so a URL cannot be smuggled through the adapter field, the selector array, or a version string; there is deliberately no free-text column to put one in. Tested as hostile-client cases in selector-health_test.ts (9 tests), and the adapter allowlist is DERIVED from marketplace-selectors.json so a new adapter whose telemetry would be silently dropped fails the test (negative-verified with a planted 'etsy'). The ping distinguishes 'gallery' (no selector matched — gallery selectors wrong) from 'gallery-no-urls' (elements matched, no usable URL — imageAttrs/urlUpgrade wrong, which is what the dead Poshmark regex was), because collapsing them wastes the signal. NO instance id is attached, unlike the grading calls, since that stable per-install id would make an anonymous counter linkable into a browsing trail. AC5 preserved and strengthened: renderError fires BEFORE the ping and never depends on it; the content script does not await it. Disclosure updated in both directions — SUBMISSION.md data-usage + privacy summary, and the packager now declares optional technicalAndInteraction to AMO (required would misstate an opt-in signal; omitting it would understate the add-on). STILL BLOCKS passes: AC1 (verified:true for the 5 adapters) needs live-site QA of each marketplace — cannot be done autonomously, flags left false. HELD MIGRATION: 00475 is committed locally and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md — do NOT push until it is applied to prod. Nothing client-side reads the new table, so the Pages auto-deploy is safe. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop, prompted by prd-lint findStaleHeldMigrations): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE and is superseded by this note — the migration file is already on origin/main, so the branch is NOT frozen and nobody should hold a push on its account. The distinction the old wording blurs and that still matters: PUSHED is not APPLIED. The file being on origin/main says nothing about whether the SQL has run against the prod DB; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth for what is actually applied, and 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending. So the correct residual action is an APPLY (+ NOTIFY pgrst), not a push-hold. | 2026-07-18 MEASURED CORRECTION to the status note above (agent loop): I wrote earlier today that "PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth ... 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending". That is FALSE and I am correcting my own claim. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00476, applied:00476, status:match} — the US-1566 block reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the DB own answer. 00475 and 00476 ARE APPLIED in prod. The only genuinely pending migration is 00477 (US-1999, correctly held/unpushed). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md has been corrected with the measured evidence and both sections re-marked APPLIED. The lesson: the answer was one unauthenticated HTTP GET away the whole time, and several passes (including mine) reasoned about prod schema state from commit history instead of measuring it.

userStories.title: Cross-browser: Firefox + Edge support for the unified extension
userStories.description: As a Firefox or Edge user, I want the extension to work. Audit: both extensions are Chrome-only in practice — background declares only service_worker (Firefox MV3 runs event pages via background.scripts; with only service_worker Firefox loads NO background at all); no browser_specific_settings.gecko.id (AMO requires it); the Lister additionally awaits promise-style chrome.* APIs that are callback-only on Firefox, and its onMessageExternal registration would throw at top level there. Edge is Chromium-compatible as-is and only needs a store submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest declares BOTH background.service_worker and background.scripts (the documented cross-browser pattern) + browser_specific_settings.gecko { id, strict_min_version: '109.0' }

A small runtime shim guarantees promise-style APIs on both browsers (use the browser.* namespace where present, or wrap the needed chrome.* calls); no top-level listener registration can throw on a browser lacking the event (guard onMessageExternal existence)

The research surface (condition read) works end-to-end on Firefox: config fetch, grade call (README's moz-extension origin in EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS documented in .env.example), overlay, popup, storage — verified manually on a real listing; Firefox's opt-in host-permissions flow is handled (prompt or graceful degradation)
Seller tools on Firefox: explicitly gated OFF with honest UI copy until US-1882 lands (externally_connectable does not exist on Firefox — no silent breakage)
Edge: the unified build loads and passes a manual smoke on Edge; store packaging checklist (Edge Add-ons) appended to US-1757's distribution scope
userStories.notes: Audit findings 18 + Lister §3 (four independent Firefox breakages). Safari deliberately out of scope (Xcode wrapper + no externally_connectable — revisit post-launch). | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC1 DONE — manifest declared only background.service_worker, so Firefox (which runs the background as a non-persistent EVENT PAGE and reads background.scripts) loaded NO background at all and the extension was inert there. background.js already documented+implemented its half of the contract; the manifest never did. Now declares BOTH service_worker and scripts (= importScripts deps + background.js, in order — background.js reads GT_LISTER_SELECTORS/GUARD/JOBS/REGISTRY at load) + browser_specific_settings.gecko {id: extension@gradethread.com, strict_min_version: 109.0}. AC2 load-time guards verified present (onMessageExternal + alarms). New test/background-deps.test.cjs derives the dep list from background.js's own importScripts and asserts the manifest matches exactly — the two copies only diverge on Firefox, which everyday Chrome work never exercises (US-1874 added job-store.js and nothing would have caught the omission). Guard verified against both the missing-dep drift and the pre-fix no-scripts state. 11/11 extension test files. BLOCKS passes: AC3 (research surface end-to-end on Firefox) + AC5 (Edge smoke) need a real browser. AC4 (gate seller tools off on Firefox) may be moot now US-1882's gt-bridge.js has landed — needs a decision, not a blind gate. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17 (b): AC4 RESOLVED AS MOOT + a shipped-build bug fixed. AC4 investigation: there is NO browser gate in extension-unified and none is needed — seller gating is capability-based off entitlements (registry.js:58 sellerEnabled, fail-safe false), and US-1882's gt-bridge.js gives Firefox a working transport (src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 falls back to sendViaBridge when chrome.runtime is absent; handleExternalMessage re-checks origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed either way). So no honest-copy gate is owed. BUT seller tools were still broken on Firefox for a DIFFERENT reason, in the packager rather than the extension: scripts/package-extensions.mjs hand-maintained a THIRD copy of the background dep list that predated US-1874's lister/job-store.js, so the shipped FF event page loaded with GT_LISTER_JOBS undefined; startJob threw at background.js:575 AFTER tabs.create had already opened the marketplace tab, sendResponse never fired, gt-bridge replied transportError, and sendListerJob deliberately does not settle on transportError (MV3 worker-death cover) — so the seller got an unfilled form and a 130s hang. Exactly the silent breakage AC4 was written to prevent, one file outside the guard. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: firefoxManifest() now DERIVES from the manifest instead of re-declaring it, which also fixed two more shipped-only bugs the same overwrite caused — strict_min_version was dropped entirely (add-on installable on pre-109 Firefox, no MV3) and the gecko id disagreed with the manifest's (extension@ vs unified@ = different add-on identity for a dev-loaded vs store build, and unchangeable post-AMO-submission). background-deps.test.cjs now imports the packager (run block guarded behind an isEntry check) and asserts the ACTUAL transform output, not a restatement of it; both regressions verified to fail the guard, then restored green. Shipped FF zip verified by unzip: 5 bg scripts incl job-store.js, min 109.0, externally_connectable stripped. 12/12 extension test files. STILL BLOCKS passes: AC3 (Firefox research surface end-to-end) + AC5 (Edge smoke) — both need a real browser + a human. NOTE for AC5: extension-condition's FF build has NO strict_min_version (its manifest declares no gecko block, so the packager fallback supplies only an id) — same pre-109 exposure, left alone as out of scope for this story. | 2026-07-19 THE AC5 SIDE-NOTE IS NOW FIXED (the story itself stays passes:false — AC3 Firefox end-to-end and AC5 Edge smoke still need a real browser and a human, which has not changed). A prior pass recorded, and then left alone as out of scope, that extension-condition's Firefox build has NO strict_min_version. Verified it: its manifest declared no browser_specific_settings AT ALL, so package-extensions.mjs supplied a gecko id from its config fallback and nothing constrained the version — the shipped Condition Check AMO zip had no floor. WHY THAT MATTERS: Firefox gained MV3 in 109, so the add-on installs on older Firefox where its own APIs do not exist, does nothing, and reads as our software being broken rather than as an unsupported browser. It is also a RECURRENCE, which is what makes it worth more than a one-line fix: the firefoxManifest() comment in the packager already lists 'a wholesale overwrite that dropped strict_min_version' as one of three drift breakages that shipped. It came back by a different route — absence rather than overwrite — so fixing only the instance would leave the third route open too. FIXED THE INSTANCE AND THE CLASS: declared gecko.id + strict_min_version 109.0 in extension-condition/manifest.json (manifest-first, per the packager's own stated rule that firefox.* config only FILLS GAPS), plus a packager guard that THROWS rather than warns — this is the step that produces a store upload, the artifact goes somewhere we cannot recall it from, and a warning in a build log is exactly what got missed the first time (verified exit code 1). Plus a repo-level test that derives its targets from the packager config, so a newly Firefox-enabled extension is covered the day it is enabled rather than the day someone remembers the file; it hard-fails if that derivation yields zero targets, because a guard that silently checks nothing is the failure mode it exists to prevent. Does NOT pin an exact version — raising the floor is a legitimate decision and a test that fights it gets deleted; having no floor never is. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED three ways: block removed, floor set to 102, and the packager run with no floor (exit 1). Note this hardens a DEPRECATED artifact, consistent with the US-2020 call: extension-condition is superseded but still packaged and still installed, so it has to keep working until its store listing is retired. 15/15 extension test files, 2472 web tests.

userStories.title: Web↔extension transport v2: postMessage bridge so seller tools work beyond Chromium
userStories.description: As a Firefox (later Safari) seller, I want 'Send to extension' to work. The current transport is chrome.runtime.sendMessage from the page via externally_connectable — Chromium-only by platform design. The standard alternative is a gradethread.com content script relaying window.postMessage to the background.
acceptanceCriteria: The unified extension adds a gradethread.com content script that relays a versioned, origin-checked window.postMessage protocol to the background (message schema validated exactly like the current external messages; responses relayed back with correlation ids)

src/lib/lister-extension.ts feature-detects transports: externally_connectable where available, postMessage bridge otherwise; isListerAvailable() reflects either; timeouts/settled-guard semantics preserved

Security parity: the bridge accepts messages only from window.top on allowed origins, validates payloads with the same schema, and never exposes marketplace responses to the page beyond the current result shape; the privacy copy (US-1872) already covers the gradethread.com host permission this requires
Chromium keeps using externally_connectable (no regression); Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark
userStories.notes: Unblocks the Firefox seller half of US-1881. The gradethread.com content script is the deliberate privacy-posture trade the US-1872 epic documents. | 2026-07-18 (agent loop): STATUS WAS STALE — this story read as unstarted but the bridge had already shipped (extension-unified/gt-bridge.js), which is why US-1881's notes referred to it as landed. Audited all four ACs against the code rather than the status. AC1 DONE: gt-bridge.js is a document_start content script on gradethread.com relaying a versioned envelope ({__gtExtReq,id,message} -> runtime.sendMessage -> {__gtExtRes,id,response}) with correlation ids, a `replied` guard covering Chrome's callback and Firefox's promise return, and responses posted to an EXPLICIT target origin (never '*'). AC2 DONE: src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 feature-detects — externally_connectable when chrome.runtime+id are present, else sendViaBridge; isListerAvailable() accepts the DOM marker alone (no extension id needed); the EXTENSION_TIMEOUT_MS backstop, the pushWaiters settled-guard and the deliberate do-not-settle-on-transportError semantics (MV3 worker-death cover) are all preserved. AC4 (Chromium no-regression) verified in code: the manifest still declares externally_connectable, sendViaRuntime is still PREFERRED, and both transports converge on the same handleExternalMessage which re-checks the sender origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed. GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (AC3): the AC requires the bridge accept messages 'only from window.top on allowed origins'. The origin half was satisfied (the content script only runs on gradethread.com, event.source!==window rejects other windows, and the background re-checks origin), but there was NO framing guard. The threat is clickjacking rather than forgery — event.source!==window already means only same-frame scripts can send an envelope and a cross-origin parent can run none — but a framed gradethread.com would let the page's OWN 'Send to extension' control be clicked through by a victim who cannot see it: a genuine seller action from a real click. gt-bridge.js now returns immediately unless window.top === window, installing NO marker and NO listeners (a marker alone would make the page offer seller UI in a context the extension refuses to serve), and fails CLOSED when reading window.top throws, which is what a cross-origin frame does. ⚠ NOTE this is defense in depth, not a live hole: gradethread.com ships X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP frame-ancestors 'none' — VERIFIED LIVE on the zone this pass. It is in the extension anyway because an extension must not stake its security on a response header it does not control; headers get relaxed for a partner embed or a preview host and the guarantee would vanish with nothing failing to signal it. TESTS: new extension-unified/test/gt-bridge.test.cjs EXECUTES the bridge against a stubbed window/document (rather than grepping source) and asserts: top-level installs marker+listener; framed installs NEITHER; a throwing cross-origin window.top also fails closed; the relay round-trips a correlation id and posts to an explicit origin; five malformed/foreign envelopes are ignored; and the background->page push relay forwards ONLY GT_LISTER_JOB_UPDATE/GT_LISTER_LISTED, never arbitrary background traffic. Both new guarantees negative-verified (removing the frame guard, and widening the push allowlist, each turn the suite red). 13/13 extension test files; packager still emits a valid FF zip. KEPT passes:false ON AC4 ONLY: 'Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark' needs a real browser on a real marketplace — same browser-gate as US-1881 AC3/AC5, and not something this agent can do. Everything else in the story is code-complete and tested.

userStories.title: Overlay feature richness: factor breakdown, photo-coverage hint, repeat-read recall, a11y + dark polish
userStories.description: As a shopper, I want the condition read to tell me more than one number — which factors scored low, how many photos it saw, and whether I already graded this listing — in an overlay that's accessible and doesn't clash with site/dark themes. Audit: the endpoint ALREADY returns factorScores and imagesAnalyzed and the overlay drops both; recentReads already stores past reads but the overlay never checks them; no aria-live so state changes are silent to screen readers; dark theme misses .gt-cc-note/.gt-cc-conf; popup has no dark theme; site-CSS bleed possible on child elements.
acceptanceCriteria: Result overlay renders the five factor scores (Fabric/Structural/Cosmetic/Functional/Odor) as compact labeled bars, plus 'graded from N photos' with a nudge when key shots are missing (no label/detail photo)
Before spending quota, the pill checks recentReads for this listing URL and offers 'View your read from <time>' with a one-click re-grade
Overlay container gets role=status + aria-live=polite (loading→result/error announced), focus moves to the result close button on open; keyboard dismiss (Esc) works
Dark theme covers every overlay element; the popup gets a prefers-color-scheme dark theme; child elements are hardened against site CSS (consistent all:unset per element or a shadow root)
UI strings centralized ready for _locales i18n (actual translations deferred), and NaN scores can never render (validated before display/save)
userStories.notes:
Audit findings 11/21/22/23/24/25 + buyer feature-gap list. Factor bars + photo-coverage are pure client work on data already returned. Deeper buyer features (discrepancy, price-fairness, fraud, fit) stay in US-1833..1840 — do not duplicate. 

PARTIAL 2026-07-15 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). DONE (AC1 factor breakdown + photo-coverage; AC5 NaN guard): new pure UMD helper content/condition-format.js (self.GT_CC_FMT) — factorBars() maps the endpoint-returned factorScores (fabric/structural/cosmetic/functional/odor, weight order) to render-ready {label,score,pct,cls} rows and DROPS any NaN/non-finite/out-of-range factor (safeScore gate) so "NaN" can never render; photoCountLabel()+lowCoverage() surface imagesAnalyzed ("Graded from N photos" + a thin-set nudge) which the overlay previously dropped; UI strings centralized in STRINGS (ready for _locales, translations deferred). Wired into renderResult of BOTH overlays (extension-condition/content/marketplace.js + extension-unified/research/marketplace.js) with compact labeled bars reusing the .gt-cc-s-* palette; overall-score render now guarded (NaN → em dash). overlay.css factor-bar styles + dark-mode overrides in both. New content script registered in both manifests (before marketplace.js). New unit test test/condition-format.test.cjs asserts the NaN/garbage gate + bar ordering + photo-count/low-coverage; covers BOTH physical helper copies. Verified: node scripts/test-extensions.mjs = 8 files green (was 7), node --check all 4 JS, both manifests valid JSON, drift guards still green. NOT DONE (blocks passes, browser-verification-gated): AC2 recentReads recall-before-grade UX ("View your read from <time>" pill + one-click re-grade); AC3 a11y (role=status + aria-live=polite, focus-to-close-on-open, Esc dismiss); AC4 full dark-theme coverage + child-CSS hardening / shadow-root; AC5 remaining (centralize the OTHER existing overlay strings). 

PARTIAL 2026-07-15 (cont.) DONE (AC3 a11y): overlay root gets role=status + aria-live=polite so loading→result/error transitions are announced; Escape closes the overlay (capture-phase keydown listener, torn down in removeOverlay); on a terminal state (result/error) focus moves to the close button (never during the transient loading state). Applied to BOTH overlays. Verified node --check + node scripts/test-extensions.mjs (8 files green). NOTE (AC2): the recentReads recall-before-grade is ALREADY implemented (boot() → GT_CC_GET_CACHED/readGradeCache keyed by listingKey, TTL-bounded) — it recalls the saved read WITH its timestamp ("Saved read · <time>") and a one-click Re-read, spending no quota; the original audit predated it, so AC2 is functionally satisfied. Semantic pills re-inked (dark tint + light ink) rather than inverted, which would leave near-black ink on a near-black chip; s-fair/s-poor ambers retuned. Guarded by src/test/popup-theme.test.ts (6 cases) via a real CSS parser: media-query parsing, :root var overrides, last-job vars, light-theme intact, and EVERY .pop-status variant having a dark override. Pill contrast asserted by relative luminance, not hex (a hex match cannot fire — the CSSOM normalises to rgb()); verified it fails on an injected regression. NOTE: the loop deferred AC4 wholesale as browser-gated, but that only applies to the overlay's site-CSS-bleed hardening — the popup has no site to bleed from, so it was always verifiable. BLOCKS passes: overlay child-CSS hardening (all:unset-per-element or a shadow-root refactor) genuinely needs cross-site browser verification.

userStories.title: Listing Quality Score: one 0–100 number per listing aggregating every verified ranking lever
userStories.description: As a seller, I want a single score telling me how well each listing plays eBay's actual ranking game — and exactly which fix earns the most points — so optimizing 300 drafts stops requiring SEO knowledge. Audit: no listing-quality score exists anywhere (verified against current prd + archive); components exist piecemeal (aspect blockers, compliance card, category nudge).
acceptanceCriteria: Edge lib computes score + component breakdown from verified levers only: title quality (US-1890 lint + utilization), required+recommended aspect coverage (US-1895 math), photo standards (US-1896 data: count, hero type, dimensions), category confidence (leaf + suggestion match), condition-tier/description consistency (US-1894), and fulfillment signals read from the listing's resolved business policies (returns accepted, ≤1-day handling, free-shipping) — weights documented in the lib with playbook citations

Returned in the validate/preflight response and persisted on the listing row for sorting; drafts list + pipeline board show the score with a breakdown popover where each component links to its fix surface
Score never invents folklore signals (no Best Offer, no relist-freshness); copy for fulfillment components cites 'eBay Best Match factors'
Deno tests: component fixtures produce expected scores; a fully-optimized fixture scores 100

iOS surfaces the same score: PublishDialog shows the score + component breakdown (each component naming its fix surface) read from the validate/preflight response the app already calls, and drafts-library rows show a score chip usable for sorting — no client-side recomputation of weights (parity audit 2026-07-09: original criteria covered only the web drafts list + pipeline board)
userStories.notes: [P2][SEO][Capstone] Depends on US-1890/1894/1895/1896 landing first (build after them). See EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md. Added 2026-07-09. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). Dependencies confirmed landed first (US-1890/1894/1895/1896 + US-1490 all archived passes:true), so the capstone is genuinely unblocked. DONE: AC1 scoring lib + AC3 + AC4. New lib/listing-quality-score.ts — pure, every input supplied by the caller because assemblePublishContext already computes all six signals in one pass. Weights sum to 100 and each cites its EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md section: aspects 30 (§1 'single highest-confidence lever'), photos 25 (§6 thumbnail = 'biggest CTR lever'), title 15, category 12, fulfillment 10 (§4 eBay-CONFIRMED returns/≤1-day handling/free shipping), condition 8. The playbook publishes NO numbers deliberately, so the values are a judgement call but the ORDERING is not — a test pins aspects > photos > title > fulfillment. New lib/business-policy-signals.ts closes the gap the audit found: PolicySet carries only policy IDs, but syncBusinessPolicies already writes eBay's ENTIRE raw policy object into business_policies.policy_data, so the three fulfillment signals are parsed from that jsonb — nothing new is fetched. handlingTime is normalised across DAY/BUSINESS_DAY/HOUR (24h == 1 day, since rejecting it would under-score a seller who IS meeting the bar); free shipping accepts both the explicit flag and a zero shippingCost; a free INTERNATIONAL service does not count (Best Match ranks for the buyers being served). Everything fails to null, never false — 'unreadable policy' and 'seller refuses returns' are different facts and collapsing them would tell a seller to fix something already correct. AC3 (no folklore) drove a real design call. AC1's phrase 'title … utilization' invites rewarding titles near 80 chars — which is EXACTLY the vendor lore §2 flags as not an eBay statement. So title scores policy cleanliness (US-1890, a real blocker) plus a floor below which there is too little searchable text to match queries; there is no optimal band and no positional weighting. Tests assert 68 vs 78 chars TIE and that word order never moves the score, plus a guard that no component string mentions Best Offer / relist / Sell Similar / stemming / templates (§10 non-factors). TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS worth reviewing, both made after eyeballing the score across realistic listings rather than trusting green tests: (1) BLOCKED_SCORE_CEILING — the purely additive score LIED about exactly the listings a seller most needs to find: one missing required specific scored 70 and a non-leaf category scored 88, both for listings eBay refuses to list at all, so triaging 300 drafts by score would sort them into the 'fine' pile. Any publish-blocking component (no title, title policy violation, missing required aspect, no photos, sub-500px hero, non-leaf/not-found category) now caps the whole score at 40 and sets blocked + blockingReasons. A test asserts a blocked listing sorts BELOW the worst publishable one, and another asserts merely-weak listings are NOT marked blocked (a seller must be able to tell 'will not list' from 'will list badly'). (2) the aspects component was rebalanced from required 55%/recommended 45% to 25%/75% — paying most of the component for having no MISSING required aspect is paying for table stakes (it is a blocker otherwise), and it left recommended coverage barely moving the number (2/8 filled still scored 80; now 74). Unknown signals are excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator and the score rescales, so an unsynced business policy cannot drag a perfect listing below 100 — the score must not drift with OUR sync health. Verified: 25 tests in listing-quality-score_test.ts; full edge suite 4124 passed / 0 failed; deno lint (1168 files); deno check src/main.ts. NOT DONE (blocks passes): AC2 — the score is NOT yet returned from POST /listings/validate (the natural home is PublishContextOk in flipdesk-ebay.ts, which already computes every input) and NOT persisted on the listing row for sorting; persistence needs a migration + the drafts list / pipeline board breakdown popover. AC5 — iOS PublishDialog + drafts-library score chip; cannot be built or tested on Windows (Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only). The lib is deliberately pure so both surfaces can consume it without recomputing weights client-side, which AC5 explicitly forbids. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 FIRST HALF DONE: the score is now RETURNED from POST /listings/validate as qualityScore. assemblePublishContext gained a qualitySignals block carrying the RAW structured signals it already computes (title policy violations, photo blockers/warnings/count, category leaf status + whether it came from a Taxonomy suggestion, required-missing aspects) — deliberately raw, not a score, so the scorer never string-sniffs the blocker array, which would break silently the first time a message is reworded. The score itself is assembled in buildQualityScore() on the VALIDATE route, not inside assemblePublishContext, because it needs one extra DB read (business policies) and the publish + auto-publish paths share that function: scoring is a validate-time concern and the hot path should not pay for it. loadFulfillmentSignals() reads business_policies.policy_data tenant-scoped on user_id (US-268; ownerId comes from workspaceOwnerId ?? userId, never the body) and fails to UNKNOWN_FULFILLMENT so a policy read can never break a preflight. NOTABLE: this is the FIRST production caller of conditionDescriptionConsistency() — US-1894 (archived passes:true) shipped that check tested but never wired into any path, so the condition/description consistency it promised was not actually running anywhere until now. categoryWasSuggested maps to matchesSuggestion=true, and a hand-picked category stays null (unknown) rather than false: asserting false would penalise every category we never cross-checked. VERIFIED: the flipdesk-ebay.ts diff is 105 insertions and ZERO deletions — purely additive, no existing publish behaviour altered; deno check + deno lint (1168 files) clean; full edge suite 4124 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 second half — persisting the score on the listing row for sorting (needs a migration) + the drafts list / pipeline board breakdown popover; and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 SECOND HALF — PERSISTENCE DONE. Migration 00476_listing_quality_score.sql adds listings.quality_score SMALLINT (0-100, NULL until first computed), quality_blocked BOOLEAN and quality_scored_at TIMESTAMPTZ, plus a 0-100 CHECK and a partial index (inventory_item_id, quality_score) WHERE quality_score IS NOT NULL for the drafts/pipeline sort. US-1108 triple satisfied: idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS x3, duplicate_object-guarded ADD CONSTRAINT, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 00475->00476 in the SAME commit, self-record footer; schema-version_test.ts green. DESIGN CALLS: (1) the component BREAKDOWN is deliberately NOT stored — it is cheap to recompute (the preflight already loads every input), it changes whenever the weights change, and a stored copy would silently go stale and show a seller a breakdown that no longer matches the number beside it. Store the sortable scalar, recompute the explanation. (2) quality_score is NULLABLE with no default: NULL (never scored) and 0 (scored zero) are different states, and a NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 would make every unscored draft look broken and poison the sort. (3) quality_blocked is STORED rather than derived from score <= BLOCKED_SCORE_CEILING, because that ceiling is a policy constant that may move and old rows should stay honest if it does. WIRING: scoreAndPersist() on the validate route writes the scalar as a best-effort side effect — awaited but swallowed, because preflight is what tells a seller whether they can publish and must not start failing over a sort key (notably if the edge deploys ahead of 00476). A draft with no listings row yet is skipped: nothing to sort, nothing to store. Tenant-safe without an extra filter — ctx.listing came from assemblePublishContext, already owner-scoped, so the id is ours by construction and never from the request body (US-268). HELD MIGRATION: 00476 is committed locally and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md (apply AFTER 00475, then NOTIFY pgrst). No client-side read in this change, so the Pages auto-deploy is safe. Verified: deno check + lint (1168 files) + full edge suite 4126 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 UI (drafts list + pipeline board score chip and breakdown popover — the columns now exist to sort by) and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 UI COMPONENT DONE — and my earlier claim that web UI was unverifiable here was WRONG. The repo has jsdom + 160 component tests that assert rendered markup via renderToStaticMarkup (no @testing-library) plus axe-core, so UI IS verifiable headless; I had assumed otherwise for several rounds without checking. New src/components/flipdesk/quality-score-chip.tsx exports QualityScoreChip + QualityScoreBreakdown + scoreBand, with 11 tests. Nothing is recomputed client-side (AC5 forbids it) — the component consumes the score the edge already returns on /listings/validate. Design points, each test-pinned: blocked is its OWN colour band and renders "Can not list" instead of a number, because painting a blocked listing the same amber as a weak-but-listable one would undo on screen the very sort-ordering the server-side cap exists to create; an unscored listing renders an em dash, never 0 (NULL and 0 are different facts); an unknown component shows "not checked" rather than 0/10, matching the server excluding it from the maths; a Fix action appears only for genuinely fixable components; and the breakdown states "Scored on N of 100 points" when weightCounted < 100 so partial information is admitted rather than passed off as a full assessment. Negative-verified: removing the blocked band, and rendering 0 for unscored, each turn the suite red. STILL OPEN for passes: wiring the chip into the drafts list + pipeline board (needs those pages routing a fixSurface handler), and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 DRAFTS-LIST WIRING DONE. autolister-drafts.tsx renders the QualityScoreChip per row and gains a "Quality: low first" sort. ⚠ THE IMPORTANT DETAIL: the score is fetched in a SEPARATE, FAIL-SOFT query, not added to the existing drafts select. That query does "if (error) throw error", so adding quality_score to it would 42703 and take the WHOLE DRAFTS PAGE DOWN the moment the frontend deploys ahead of migration 00476 — the exact hazard CLAUDE.md’s held-migration rule warns about for client-side reads of a new column. With a separate query a missing column just means no chips, and every draft honestly reads "not scored". The two judgement calls were extracted to src/pages/flipdesk/draft-quality.ts so they are testable without rendering the page (the repo’s status-param-to-tab.ts pattern): scoreMapFromRows OMITS a NULL quality_score rather than coercing it to 0 (never-scored and scored-zero are different facts, and a 0 would both render a confident chip and sort an unscored draft in with the genuinely worst), and qualityRankOf sinks unscored drafts to the END of the worst-first sort ("we do not know" is not evidence of low quality; floating unknowns to the top would bury the listings we DO know are weak, defeating the sort). 6 helper tests + 11 component tests; the sinks-to-end rule negative-verified by inverting it (2 tests go red). Full web suite 162 files / 2162 tests green, lint exit 0, tsc clean. REMAINING for passes: the pipeline board surface (AC2 names drafts list AND pipeline board) and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 PIPELINE-BOARD SURFACE SCOPED (not built — there is a real design question first). The drafts cockpit was straightforward because it queries `listings` directly, so the persisted quality_score is a column on the row it already renders. pipeline.tsx queries `inventory_items` instead, and an item can have SEVERAL listings (a draft plus a live one, or historical ended rows). So 'the item's quality score' is ambiguous: newest listing? the draft? the live one? worst of them? Each answer changes what a worst-first sort means on that board, and picking one silently is how a number ends up meaning different things on two screens. DECIDE FIRST, then wire — the mechanics are already proven (fail-soft separate query keyed by inventory_item_id + QualityScoreChip + qualityRankOf, per the drafts-list commit). Deliberately not guessed at, since US-1897 cannot close anyway while AC5 needs a macOS session. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop, prompted by prd-lint findStaleHeldMigrations): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE and is superseded by this note — the migration file is already on origin/main, so the branch is NOT frozen and nobody should hold a push on its account. The distinction the old wording blurs and that still matters: PUSHED is not APPLIED. The file being on origin/main says nothing about whether the SQL has run against the prod DB; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth for what is actually applied, and 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending. AC1/AC3/AC4 (the scoring lib + weights + 25 deno tests), AC2 (validate response, migration 00476 persistence, the web chip, the drafts cockpit and the pipeline board) all landed across 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-30; the prior notes hold. WHAT SHIPPED: NEW ios/GradeThread/Marketplaces/Publish/ListingQualityScore.swift (ListingQualityScore + QualityComponent + QualityFix + QualityScoreBand + QualityScoreSummary) and QualityScoreViews.swift (QualityScoreChip + QualityScoreCard); ValidateResponse gained qualityScore; PublishDialog renders the card in the composer AND on the blocked screen; DraftListing/DraftsService read the persisted quality_score + quality_blocked columns; DraftsLibraryStore gained a pure static sorted(_:by:) with a 'Quality: low first' order and a toolbar picker; DraftLibraryRow renders the chip. Decoding is forgiving in exactly one direction: a reshaped advisory field degrades rather than failing the whole validate decode and costing the seller their publish, BUT an unrecognised component status reads as , never as a pass — a check this app version has not shipped support for must not be painted green. THREE FACTS KEPT DISTINCT, each test-pinned, because collapsing any one is how the number starts lying: never-scored is not zero (a NULL yields no summary, renders an em dash, and does not sort with the worst); blocked is its own band, not 'poor' (the server caps blocked listings so they sort with the wreckage — same-amber-as-weak would undo that on screen); an unreadable signal shows 'not checked', not 0/10 (the server excludes it from both numerator and denominator, so a zero would tell a seller to fix something already correct). It compiled everywhere it was WRONG and only failed where a test tried to unwrap it; the production call site passed optionals and always picked correctly, so ONLY the test caught it. Now a named factory, fromColumns(score:blocked:), with no overload to resolve. userStories.title: Android universal APK ships 4 ABIs — ML Kit native libs cost ~42MB
userStories.description: As a seller on a metered connection, I download only the native libraries my device can run.
acceptanceCriteria: Release distribution is an App Bundle (or ABI splits) so each device downloads one ABI, not four
ML Kit OCR + barcode native libs (libmlkit_google_ocr_pipeline.so ~11MB/ABI, libbarhopper_v3.so ~5MB/ABI) contribute their per-device size only
CI records the per-ABI download size so a future model dependency cannot silently double it
userStories.notes: [P2][Android/Build] Found while implementing US-1333. Adding ML Kit text recognition took the universal debug APK from 45MB to 87MB; ~41MB of that is libmlkit_google_ocr_pipeline.so duplicated across armeabi-v7a/arm64-v8a/x86/x86_64. The Japanese script model itself is only ~1.8MB of assets, so dropping it is NOT the fix — the native pipeline is required by Latin too. There is currently no abiFilters, no splits block, no bundle config and no release job in android-ci.yml.

userStories.title: Seller Grade Integrity score — buyer confirmations become seller reputation
userStories.description: As a verified seller, I want a Grade Integrity score built from real post-sale outcomes (buyer arrival confirmations, dispute rate, coverage, tenure) so that my proven accuracy — not just my activity volume — is my standing; and as GradeThread we want a reputation asset no listing-tool competitor can replicate without first building a grading-quality scanner and a buyer confirmation base.
acceptanceCriteria: An integrity aggregate per seller (confirmed-accurate rate from US-1812 outcomes, upheld-dispute rate, avg photo-coverage %, graded volume, tenure) computed into named tiers with transparent, explainable rules the seller can view

Score is anti-gameable: minimum confirmed-outcome volume before a tier displays (below the floor shows 'building history', never a bad score), self-purchases/linked-account confirmations excluded (reuse referral self-click blocking), and dispute outcomes only count after human-review resolution
Integrity tier surfaces on the public verified profile and certificate pages (read path via the existing public-cert/verified RLS carve-outs, PII-safe)
Tier changes emit reward_events (US-1849) and a tier-up is a celebration moment (US-1857); a tier-down notifies the seller privately with the specific driver, never publicly announced
Migration triple satisfied; aggregate recompute is idempotent and tenant-scoped

THE connective story: US-1810..1814 buyer confirmations currently feed only model accuracy — this makes them feed seller reputation too, closing the two-sided loop. REMAINING: recompute must apply AC2 self/linked-account exclusion + human-review-resolved-disputes-only filtering and store tier+coverage/tenure inputs (migration for tier fields on seller_grade_integrity); AC3 surface tier on public cert/verified-profile (RLS carve-outs, PII-safe); AC4 emit reward_events + tier-up celebration BLOCKED on US-1849 (Rewards engine / reputation_events ledger decision), tier-down private notify. grading-engine/tenant-isolation apply to the impure recompute+surfacing, not this pure fn. 

PARTIAL 2026-07-15 (agent loop, NO migration → pushable). AC2 anti-gaming advanced: added pure countableSellerOutcomes(rows, {sellerUserId, linkedUserIds, requireResolvedDispute}) in buyer-grade-confirmation.ts — drops self-purchase + linked-account confirmations (a seller can no longer inflate their integrity via their own/colluding accounts; reuses the referral self-click-blocking idea) AND counts a dispute only after human-review resolution (an unresolved dispute is excluded entirely — not bad, not total — so a frivolous dispute can't dent a score before an expert rules). Wired into recomputeSellerGradeIntegrity: select now includes buyer_user_id + human_review_flagged; self/linked exclusion is ACTIVE; a review-flagged (material) dispute is treated as PENDING (uncounted, benefit-of-the-doubt) until resolved, a minor never-reviewed dispute counts immediately. 7 deno tests (self-exclusion, linked-exclusion, unresolved-dispute-excluded, resolved-material-counts-double, requireResolvedDispute:false, self-dispute-excluded, null-buyer-kept); full edge suite green, deno check/lint clean. REMAINING (unchanged blockers): the resolved-dispute RE-count once a flagged dispute's human review RESOLVES still needs the grade_reports/human_reviews join (approximated here via human_review_flagged); AC2 tier/coverage/tenure STORAGE needs a migration; AC3 surface tier on public cert/verified profile (RLS carve-outs); AC4 emit reward_events + tier-up celebration remains BLOCKED on US-1849 (Rewards-engine/reputation_events decision). Story stays passes:false — AC4 is the hard blocker. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — the named AC2 remainder is done: the resolved-dispute re-count now READS the review instead of inferring it. No migration. Story stays passes:false; AC4 is still blocked on US-1849. WHAT WAS WRONG, and it ran the wrong way for a trust score: the previous pass approximated `dispute_resolved` as `human_review_flagged !== true`. That is right at the moment a dispute is raised and wrong forever after — a flagged dispute is one an expert was ASKED to rule on, so the expression excluded it PERMANENTLY, including after the expert ruled and agreed with the buyer. The act of escalating was what removed the dispute from the seller's record. A seller could accumulate confirmed-material disputes and keep a spotless public integrity score. The benefit-of-the-doubt was correct; making it permanent was not. THE JOIN IS SIMPLER THAN THE NOTE ASSUMED: human_reviews has NO status column — a ROW EXISTING is the resolution (reviewed_at is NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), 00003). So the predicate is 'does a review row exist for this outcome's grade_report_id', not a proxy for one. grade_outcomes already carries grade_report_id (00036), so nothing schema-side was needed. NEW pure withDisputeResolution(rows, reviewedReportIds) holds the rule, deliberately extracted rather than left inline: the old approximation survived precisely BECAUSE it was one expression inside an async function nobody could exercise. The recompute only looks up reports for outcomes that were actually escalated, so the extra read is bounded by the dispute count rather than the outcome count. FAILS TOWARD THE SELLER: if the human_reviews read errors, the reviewed set stays empty and escalated disputes remain pending for that run. An unreadable review table must not start counting disputes nobody has confirmed — that would dent public reputation numbers on a database blip, and the next recompute self-corrects. TESTS: 7 new cases — an unreviewed escalation stays pending, the SAME row counts once its review exists (the half the approximation could never reach), a never-escalated dispute still counts immediately, a review for a DIFFERENT report does not resolve this one (otherwise one resolution clears every pending dispute a seller has), an escalated dispute with no report id stays pending ('cannot tell' must never read as 'expert ruled against them'), confirmations pass through untouched, and a source guard on the join. ⚠ ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS CHECKING PROSE, caught by negative verification: the fail-toward-the-seller case matched the phrase 'still pending', which lives in the LOG MESSAGE — so deleting the reasoning left it green. It now asserts the construct (the reviewed set is populated only inside the success branch), which is the actual property. That is the same satisfied-by-its-own-comment shape this session keeps producing. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS: the flag-only inference returning, the join losing its per-report scoping, a missing report id counting against the seller, the recompute no longer reading human_reviews, the reviewed set populated outside the success branch, and the error branch removed. Each reddened on its own case. REMAINING (unchanged): AC2 tier/coverage/tenure STORAGE needs a migration; AC3 surface the tier on the public cert / verified profile; AC4 emit reward_events + tier-up celebration is BLOCKED on US-1849 (rewards engine not built), which is the hard blocker keeping this story open. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5377 passed / 0 failed, deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1341 files.

userStories.title: RLS policies never wrap auth.uid() / workspace-member helper in a scalar subquery → per-row re-evaluation on large reads
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want per-user reads to stay fast at scale. Grep shows 178 `USING/WITH CHECK` clauses calling bare `auth.uid()` and zero using the `(select auth.uid())` initplan form Supabase recommends. For the ~28 child-table policies using correlated `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parent WHERE ... = auth.uid())` (submission_images, item_photos, grade_reports, shipments, ...) the planner re-runs the subquery per candidate row. Separately, the listings/sales/inventory policies (00146) call `is_workspace_member_with_role(user_id, 'viewer')` — a SECURITY DEFINER function whose STABLE caching only collapses same-`user_id` calls, so a cross-tenant scan re-invokes it (and its workspace_members lookup) per distinct owner.
acceptanceCriteria: High-traffic per-user policies rewritten to `USING ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)` (and equivalents) so the planner hoists to a single initplan; prioritize the correlated-subquery child tables

A supporting index on `workspace_members(workspace_owner_id, member_user_id, role)` exists; the `is_workspace_member_with_role` helper short-circuits the owner case before querying, and callers pre-filter by `user_id`
EXPLAIN (or the supabase-postgres-best-practices lane) confirms the initplan form on a representative large per-user SELECT; migration follows the US-1108 triple
Load the `supabase-postgres-best-practices` and `migrations` skills
userStories.notes: [P2][DB/Perf] Code-review sweep 2026-07-11. Combines two related planner findings. Load `supabase-postgres-best-practices` + `migrations` skills. | 2026-07-15 (branch cursor/measurements-ebay-live-sync): CODE COMPLETE, HELD — migration 00451_rls_initplan_perf.sql. Rewrote the hot-path per-user RLS to the Supabase initplan form ((select auth.uid())) + gave every workspace-member-helper policy a cheap owner fast-path disjunct ((select auth.uid()) = user_id OR is_workspace_member...) so the SECURITY DEFINER helper is never CALLED for owner rows on a single-tenant scan (AC1). Tables: submissions, submission_images, grade_reports, inventory_items, listings, sales, shipments, item_photos (owner + workspace policies each). CREATE OR REPLACEd is_workspace_member/_with_role (internal auth.uid()->(select auth.uid()), owner OR-branch kept as short-circuit) + added covering index idx_workspace_members_owner_member_role (owner_id, member_id, role) (AC2). Set membership provably unchanged (scalar-subquery returns same value; owner disjunct already implied by helper). US-1108 triple done: idempotent DROP-IF-EXISTS+CREATE, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00451 same commit, self-record footer. Edge tests green (schema-version sync + rls-guard). KEPT passes:false: AC3 (EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan form on a representative large per-user SELECT) needs Docker (down at author time) or a prod check — run npm run verify:db when Docker is up, or EXPLAIN in prod post-apply. HELD migration: apply to prod + NOTIFY pgrst before pushing (see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md). | 2026-07-18 STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the 'HELD migration: apply to prod + NOTIFY pgrst before pushing' instruction above is STALE and should not be acted on. 00451_rls_initplan_perf.sql is on origin/main, and prod's applied schema version is proven to be >= 00474 (the deployed edge expects 00474 and a confirmed-behind DB hard-exits at boot; the latest_schema_migration RPC exists — it returns 42501 permission denied to anon, not PGRST202 not-found — so the guard's version read cannot be failing open). 00451 <= 00474, so AC1/AC2's DDL is applied in production and this story is NOT waiting on an apply or a push. AC3 remains the only blocker: an EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan form on a representative large per-user SELECT. That needs either Docker for the verify:db lane (unavailable on the authoring host) or a prod DB session — the anon key cannot reach pg_policies or run EXPLAIN through PostgREST, so it is not checkable from the agent sandbox even with network access. ⚠ CAVEAT worth carrying: the version read reports the MAX applied migration, so 'prod >= 00474' does not by itself prove 00451 specifically was applied rather than skipped in a cherry-pick. Everything is idempotent, so if there is any doubt, re-running 00451 is free and settles it. See the reconciliation header in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. | 2026-07-19 THE OPEN CAVEAT IS NOW SELF-ANSWERING. The note above carries a caveat worth resolving: 'the version read reports the MAX applied migration, so prod >= 00474 does not by itself prove 00451 specifically was applied rather than skipped in a cherry-pick.' That is exactly the blind spot US-2009 closed today. The edge now ships a manifest of every footer-era migration and checkSchemaCompleteness() compares the WHOLE SET at boot, reporting any version in the manifest that is absent from applied_migrations. So on the next edge deploy the container log answers this definitively: if 00451 was cherry-pick-skipped it will be NAMED as missing, and if it is absent from that report it was applied. No psql session needed. (The same mechanism will also name the phantom 00479 that prod reports but this repo has no file for — see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md.) AC3 ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED: an EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan form needs Docker for the verify:db lane or a real DB session, and the anon key cannot reach pg_policies or run EXPLAIN through PostgREST — so it is not checkable from here even with outbound network. Worth being precise that these are two DIFFERENT questions that the note previously ran together: 'was the DDL applied' (now self-answering) and 'does the planner actually hoist to an initplan' (still needs EXPLAIN). Confirming the first does not confirm the second. | 2026-07-19 AC1 HAD ALREADY REGRESSED, AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE TOLD US. I set out to close AC3 and could not (see below), so I checked whether AC1 was still TRUE rather than assuming a shipped fix stays shipped. It is not: 00474_push_subscriptions (US-1901) added FOUR policies in the bare auth.uid() form, 23 migrations after 00451 swept them out. 00451 was a one-time edit with no mechanism to stay fixed — structurally the same as the rounding-site drift (US-2041) and the hand-synced image sitemap (US-2111): a correct change that nothing holds in place. Added the missing guard to rls-guard_test.ts, which already statically parses the migration corpus so it was the natural home rather than a new file. It strips the CORRECT `(select auth.uid())` form FIRST and then looks for what remains — searching for bare auth.uid() directly would match inside the wrapped form and flag every correctly-written policy, i.e. it would be red on the fix. Scoped to migrations after 00451 because flagging ~253 legitimately-older files would be permanently red, and a permanently red guard gets switched off. DID NOT FIX 00474, deliberately, and the reason is recorded in the exemption itself rather than left implicit: applied migrations are immutable so it needs a NEW migration, RLS DDL cannot be validated from this host (I confirmed Docker is unavailable — `docker info` hangs and was SIGTERMed at 60s, so the verify:db lane cannot run), and push_subscriptions is one row per user per device, so the per-row re-evaluation this guard exists to prevent is negligible there. Shipping an unverifiable RLS policy rewrite for a negligible gain is the worse trade; the exemption says to fix it opportunistically alongside the next push_subscriptions migration and NOT to add entries for a hot table. Also added a SELF-CHECK test that exercises the detector on the bare form, the correct form, and the realistic half-migration (USING fixed, WITH CHECK missed) — because this session has twice shipped a guard that could not fail (US-2103's hand-listed builder sweep, US-2104's import-line match), and a guard over RLS is the last place to repeat that. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED both directions: a planted migration with a bare policy fails and names the file; removing the exemption surfaces 00474, proving the exemption is load-bearing rather than decorative. AC3 UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED — an EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan needs Docker or a prod session; now verified unavailable on this host rather than inherited from an earlier note. Note the guard does NOT close AC3 and does not claim to: it keeps the SOURCE in the shape the plan needs, which is a different assertion from observing the plan. Verified: 4445 edge tests, deno check + lint clean.
