userStories.title: US-1891 backwards title sync never shipped server-side — the edge title-sync module has zero callers
userStories.description: As a seller, when I correct an item's Brand/size/color/style/department from ANY surface, I want the listing title to update — not just from the web item canvas. US-1891 (P1, archived passes:true) required the substitution on 'the edge item update path AND web item-canvas save' (its AC2). Only the web half shipped. src/lib/title-sync.ts is wired into item-canvas.tsx persist(); its declared lockstep mirror services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts is imported by NOTHING — verified 2026-07-18, every export has zero production references. So an edit made through the edge item-update API, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit or CSV import still corrects the brand and leaves the OLD brand in listing_title: exactly the bug US-1891 exists to fix, on every surface except one. Both suites are green because each calls its own copy directly, so nothing signals the gap.
acceptanceCriteria: Item edits from EVERY non-canvas write path apply the same substitution the web canvas does, under the same conditions (GT-origin non-ebay listings only; both title_variants; hand-edited-vs-ai_generated_snapshot sets needs_review; live listings queue the revise-in-place prompt, never end/relist). NOTE: there is no generic edge item-update endpoint — see the 2026-07-18 scope correction; the concrete surfaces are web bulk-edit (brand/size/color/style, nearest gap), identification-verify, and iOS
It cannot DOUBLE-APPLY against the frontend path — decide one owner per surface, or make the substitution provably idempotent for the web canvas case that already ran it

iOS is the ONLY remaining surface (audited 2026-07-18): AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style and iOS never writes listing_title. identification-verify only annotates provenance, and CSV import is fill-only so a blank old value makes the substitution a provable no-op — neither needs wiring. Needs a macOS session; test the Swift port against src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json so it cannot drift from the two JS copies

A BEHAVIOURAL parity fixture shared by both suites: one table of (title, field changes) -> expected output asserted by the deno test AND the vitest test, so the two copies cannot drift. They currently differ by ~80 lines and nothing pins them — the frontend inlines the trim because it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects, which is legitimate, but that is exactly why source-diffing cannot be the guard
The ⚠ block at the top of the edge title-sync.ts is removed once it has real callers
userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/SEO][Regression of an ARCHIVED story] Found 2026-07-18 by the unwired-export audit that also produced US-1994. This is the more serious of the two: US-1994 is a contract divergence with no known live bug, whereas this is a P1 feature that measurably does not run on most surfaces. US-1891's own notes describe the web wiring in detail ('Wired into item-canvas persist()') and never claim the edge half — the AC asked for both, and the story was marked done anyway. Worth asking what else in the archive has the same shape: a 'lockstep mirror' is a strong smell, since only one copy usually gets a caller. Do NOT just import the module in an edge route and call it — see AC2/AC3; the double-apply and needs_review semantics are the hard part, not the substitution. Meanwhile the edge module carries a ⚠ header naming the gap so its green tests stop reading as proof the feature works server-side. | 2026-07-18 (cont.): the audit is now a repeatable tool — scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs. Re-running it correctly found 10 WHOLE MODULES that no production file imports, carrying 143 test references between them: drip-trigger.ts (4 exports/31 refs — US-933s unified trigger engine, SUPERSEDED by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts, so dead rather than broken), title-sync.ts (4/29 — this story), authenticity-eval.ts (6/24), measure-eval-stats.ts (3/16 — the MeasureCard accuracy gate, plausibly just pending its OPEN story US-1582), ai-size-estimate-core.ts (3/15), brand-seed.ts (2/12), grading-reliability.ts (2/11), grade-badge.ts (1/5), content-ai-email.ts (4/0), rubric.ts (1/0). Each needs verifying by hand: superseded, pending, and half-wired all look identical to the tool. NOTE the tool initially MISSED title-sync.ts — the module that motivated it — because its exports call each other (syncTitle uses applyTitleSubstitution), so per-function reference counting read internal cohesion as reachability. Whole-module deadness is now decided by the IMPORT GRAPH, which is the only signal that cannot be faked from inside the module. | 2026-07-18 SCOPE CORRECTED — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG. This story (and its first AC) assumed 'the edge item update path' exists. IT DOES NOT: there is no generic item-update endpoint anywhere in services/edge-functions — no route does .update() on inventory_items. Anyone picking this up would have started by hunting for an endpoint that was never built. WHAT ACTUALLY WRITES ITEM FIELDS (verified 2026-07-18): (1) web item-canvas.tsx — a DIRECT supabase write, no edge round-trip, and the ONLY surface that runs title-sync; (2) web autolister-bulk-edit.tsx:872 — also a direct supabase .update(), and it patches brand/size/color/style, i.e. FOUR OF THE FIVE SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELDS, with NO title sync at all; (3) edge lib/ai-listing.ts:1793 and lib/grading-pipeline.ts:657 — but US-1891's notes state the AI-apply path REGENERATES titles wholesale so it deliberately needs no sync; (4) edge lib/identification-verify.ts:245 (attributes); (5) iOS. SO THE HEADLINE CHANGES: the nearest, cheapest gap is NOT iOS or the edge — it is WEB BULK EDIT, in the same codebase, with src/lib/title-sync.ts already sitting there importable. A seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts gets 40 stale titles, and that is the exact bug US-1891 was written to kill. AND THE REAL QUESTION IS ARCHITECTURAL, not a wiring task: with writes distributed across five+ surfaces in three languages, per-surface mirrors do not converge — that is how there came to be two copies of title-sync with only one wired. The decision to make FIRST is WHERE THE INVARIANT LIVES: a DB trigger on inventory_items (fires for every writer, including iOS and any future one), funnelling item writes through a single edge endpoint (large change, but kills the whole class), or accepting per-surface mirrors with a shared behavioural fixture as the guard. Do not start coding before that is settled. The AC list above still stands EXCEPT AC1's 'edge item update path' phrasing, which should be read as 'every non-canvas write path'. | SIZING THE BULK-EDIT GAP (same pass): it is smaller than it looks. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx ALREADY selects listing_title AND ai_generated_snapshot from listings (line ~190) — which are exactly the two inputs title-sync needs, ai_generated_snapshot being the hand-edited-vs-AI check that decides whether to set needs_review — and it ALREADY writes back to listings (line ~707). It imports title-sync zero times; item-canvas.tsx imports it three. So IF the chosen answer is per-surface mirrors, this specific fix is roughly 'call changesFromItemDiff + syncTitle in the existing patch loop', not a new data path. I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT CHANGE. This same note argues scattered per-surface call sites are the disease — two copies of title-sync with one wired — so adding a fifth call site before the where-does-the-invariant-live decision would be inconsistent with the advice above, and wasted work if the answer turns out to be a DB trigger on inventory_items (which would cover iOS and every future writer for free). The sizing is recorded so whoever makes the call knows the per-surface option is cheap, not so the decision gets skipped. | 2026-07-18 ARCHITECTURE DECIDED + AC4 DONE. THE DECISION: per-surface mirrors with a shared BEHAVIOURAL fixture — NOT a DB trigger. I had earlier offered the trigger as my pick and then argued myself out of it: applyTitleSubstitution is 100+ lines of token-boundary, case-transfer, multi-word-brand and size-pattern string handling, so porting it to plpgsql would create a THIRD implementation in the language with the worst string handling of the three. That is a bigger version of the disease, not a cure. Funnelling every item write through one edge endpoint was also rejected for now: item writes are direct supabase calls from multiple clients (web canvas, web bulk-edit, iOS), so that is a large migration of its own and does not have to be paid before fixing the actual bug. AC4 SHIPPED: src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json — 13 cases (10 syncTitle + 3 changesFromItemDiff) read by BOTH suites, services/edge-functions/src/tests/title-sync_test.ts and src/lib/__tests__/title-sync.test.ts. A source diff could never have been the guard: the two files legitimately differ by ~80 lines because the web copy inlines the trim (it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects). Behaviour is the only thing that can be compared. FINDING: the two copies currently AGREE on all 13 cases — I ran the fixture against each implementation before wiring it in, so a disagreement would have surfaced as data rather than as a red test I then rationalised. So they had not behaviourally drifted; the risk was that nothing would have caught it if they did. Negative-verified: breaking case-transfer in the web copy alone turns 3 web tests red naming the exact fixture case, and the edge suite stays green (which is the point — the failing side identifies itself). Verified: edge 4129 passed / 0 failed, web 2164 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. STILL OPEN: the actual gap. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx patches brand/size/color/style with no title sync, and it already loads listing_title + ai_generated_snapshot and already writes to listings — so with the fixture now guarding the copies, wiring that call site is the next step and is safe to take. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BULK-EDIT GAP IS CLOSED. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx now syncs the listing title when its reverse-projection writes brand/size/color/style back onto the item — so a seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts no longer gets 40 titles still naming the old one. I did NOT inline item-canvas's ~30 lines of orchestration, which would have been a FOURTH copy — of the orchestration this time, the substitution already being shared. Extracted it instead to src/lib/title-sync-patch.ts: buildTitleSyncPatch is pure (inputs -> listings patch, no IO) and owns the decisions wrapped around syncTitle — refuse ebay-origin listings (the sync-precedence guard), move BOTH A/B variants, and flag needs_review when the title was hand-edited away from ai_generated_snapshot or the listing is live. 9 unit tests. That extraction is the actual fix for this story's root cause: the pure helper was shared and the ORCHESTRATION was not, which is why only one surface ever ran it. NOTE the guard is explicit, not inherited: this page filters batch_id + listing_status='draft', which implies GradeThread origin via deriveListingOrigin, but relying on that implicit invariant is how these contracts rot — listing_origin is now selected and checked directly (the column has existed since 00232, far below prod's >=00474, so unlike quality_score it is safe to read). TYPESCRIPT CAUGHT A REAL BUG MID-WIRING: I threaded the new columns onto DraftRow but the save loop iterates EditRow, a different shape — tsc flagged four property errors rather than letting it fail at runtime on undefined. Fixed by carrying listingOrigin/titleVariants through the EditRow mapping. Verified: web suite 2173 passed (was 2164), tsc clean, lint exit 0. REMAINING for passes: the OTHER non-canvas surfaces — identification-verify (edge) and iOS — plus confirming CSV import routes through a covered path. Those are separate surfaces, not this one; buildTitleSyncPatch is deliberately pure so the edge and a future iOS port can consume the same decisions rather than re-deriving them. item-canvas.tsx should also be refactored onto it (it still has the longhand version) — mechanical, but it touches a large working component so it wants its own change. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) item-canvas.tsx REFACTORED onto buildTitleSyncPatch, so the orchestration now exists ONCE in the web app. I had created a second copy in the previous commit by extracting the helper for bulk-edit while leaving the canvas's longhand in place — which is the same duplication this story exists to remove, so leaving it would have been incoherent. ~30 lines of inline logic replaced by one Object.assign; tsc then flagged syncTitle and trimTitleToLimit as unused imports in that file, which is the tidy confirmation that the longhand path is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. PROVED BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BEFORE COMMITTING, not asserted: transcribed the OLD inline block verbatim into a throwaway test and compared it against buildTitleSyncPatch across the full input matrix — locked/unlocked x 4 change-sets x 4 titles (incl. empty, over-long-so-pure-retrim, and a token-boundary near-miss) x 3 variant shapes (incl. null entries) x 4 snapshot states x live/not = 768 combinations, 0 mismatches. Same standard as the 2048-subset proof used for US-1994's route swap. The throwaway was deleted after it passed; the durable coverage is title-sync-patch.test.ts (9 cases) plus the shared edge<->web fixture. Verified: web suite 2173 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. | 2026-07-18 REMAINING SURFACES AUDITED — three of the four need NO work, and the scope is now exactly ONE surface (iOS). Evidence per surface rather than assumption: (1) identification-verify.ts (edge) — NOT APPLICABLE. It updates only { attributes, ai_field_sources }, and the attributes it writes spread the existing map and add just identification_verified + market_title_keywords. Neither is a SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELD, so it never changes a value a title could contain; it annotates provenance/confidence, it does not re-identify the garment. (2) CSV import (src/pages/flipdesk/import.tsx) — NOT APPLICABLE, for a subtler reason worth writing down. It is FILL-ONLY (isBlank(existing[field]) && !isBlank(incoming)), so it can only populate a brand that was previously blank. A blank old value means there is nothing in the title to substitute: syncTitle with a blank `from` is a deliberate no-op, pinned by the shared fixture case 'blank from/to is ignored rather than blanking the title'. Filling a blank brand cannot fix a title that never named one, so wiring sync here would add a call that provably does nothing. Its own comment also confirms 'Listings/sales are left untouched on re-import'. (3) iOS — GENUINE REMAINING GAP, and the only one. ios/GradeThread/AIExtract/AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style to inventory_items via a sparse FieldUpdate, and it is NOT fill-only: it keeps a Snapshot of pre-fill values expressly so an undo can restore them, which only matters if the write can overwrite a populated column. A repo-wide grep shows iOS NEVER writes listing_title anywhere. So an AI-fill on iOS that corrects a brand updates the item column and leaves the listing title naming the old one — the original US-1891 bug, surviving on exactly one surface. CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE: Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only (CLAUDE.md), so this needs a macOS session. The port is small and the decisions are already made for it — buildTitleSyncPatch is pure precisely so a Swift equivalent can mirror the same rules (refuse ebay-origin, move both variants, flag needs_review on hand-edited/live), and src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json is the behavioural contract a Swift copy should be tested against so it cannot drift from the two JS copies. | 2026-07-19 THE AUDIT'S CONCLUSIONS WERE NEVER WRITTEN BACK INTO THE CODE OR THE NOTE — fixed. The per-surface audit recorded above settled that there is NO edge item-update endpoint and that bulk-edit was the real gap (since closed), leaving iOS as the only remaining surface. But both durable artifacts still told the old story: services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts opened with '⚠ NOTHING IN THE EDGE SERVICE IMPORTS THIS MODULE' and named 'the edge item update path, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit, CSV import' as the affected surfaces, and vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md filed it under 'Accidentally dead' repeating the same list. THREE OF THOSE FIVE SURFACES ARE NOW WRONG: the edge endpoint does not exist, bulk edit is wired, CSV import is a provable no-op. So the two places a future reader would actually look were both directing them to wire an edge route that was never built — which is precisely the wasted session this story's own scope-correction warned about. Rewrote the module header as a per-surface table with the verdict for each, and an explicit DO NOT WIRE THIS instruction explaining that audit-unwired-exports.mjs will keep reporting it and that the report is correct. Moved the vault entry out of 'Accidentally dead' into a new 'Uncalled by design' section, since leaving a section titled accidental containing an entry titled by-design is its own small lie. NOT DELETED, deliberately: the edge copy is the reference the Swift port mirrors AND one half of the behavioural parity fixture asserted by both suites, so deleting it would remove one side of the only guard keeping the implementations honest. THIS IS THE SAME-COMMIT RULE BEING PAID LATE — the audit happened in a prd note and the artifacts it invalidated were left standing, which is exactly how the original US-1891 'lockstep mirror' claim survived being false. Story stays passes:false: iOS AIItemFieldWriter.swift is untouched and needs a macOS session. Verified: 16 edge + 19 web title-sync tests pass, deno check + lint clean, vault:lint clean.

userStories.title: Backlog integrity: archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED — starting with US-1770's unenforced authenticity safety gate
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want passes:true to mean the behaviour runs. Three archived stories say DEFERRED in their own notes and are marked passing anyway, and the unwired-export audit confirms at least one of them never shipped. The severe case is US-1770 (authenticity golden-set eval gate): its notes read '[DEFERRED 2026-07-09] Needs a HELD migration' — it was deferred BY the held-migration rule and then closed. runAuthenticityEval has zero callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. The unmet ACs are the safety ones: AC1 requires a candidate prompt to clear an accuracy gate BEFORE activation and AC3 requires per-brand regressions to BLOCK activation — neither is enforced by anything, AC2's human-review routing, by contrast, IS implemented and tested (authenticityNeedsReview, wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054) — an earlier draft of this story claimed otherwise and was wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: US-1770 is reopened (or a successor story filed) and its authenticity eval gate is actually wired: no authenticity prompt version can activate without clearing the gate, and a per-brand regression blocks activation

US-1770 AC2 needs NO work — verified 2026-07-18: authenticityNeedsReview() routes a red_flags verdict (or a low-confidence branded assessment) to human review at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, with unit tests. Do not re-implement it. This AC is retained only so the correction is visible.
US-744 and US-1399 are triaged the same way: both are passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED and no later resolution note. Either reopen them or record why the deferral is now satisfied

A guard makes this class visible: passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED / 'blocks passes' marker in notes should be reported by prd-lint (a warning is enough — US-1883 shows a later note can legitimately supersede an earlier blocker, so it must not hard-fail)

US-1716 AC4 is corrected: it claims brand-fact provenance is "schema-enforced" and it is not — 00389 declares source_url text and confidence numeric(3,2) as NULLABLE with no NOT NULL, and admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 explicitly permits a null confidence. FIRST run: select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null (needs DB access — deny-all table). Zero rows ⇒ add the constraints; non-zero ⇒ this is a data migration, not a one-liner. NOTE the admin route ALREADY handles source_url (it is in the editable allowlists), so no plumbing is needed — only the requirement

ai-size-estimate-core.ts is resolved one way or the other: ai-size-estimate.ts re-declares all of its helpers rather than importing it, so the tests point at a dead copy and the LIVE helpers are untested. Either make the live module import core (as its header used to claim) or delete core and repoint the test

TRIAGE OF THE 10 DEAD MODULES the audit found, so nobody repeats this work: GENUINELY MISSING — authenticity-eval.ts (US-1770, above) and brand-seed.ts (US-1716 AC4: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts are the only code that would reject an unsourced fact and nothing imports them). SUPERSEDED, behaviour intact, safe to delete or mark — content-ai-email.ts (US-918; the live newsletter path calls generateNewsletterCopy from newsletter-copy.ts), grade-badge.ts (US-118/766; deliberately removed in commit 8e1802a6 for an eBay-policy pivot to TEXT-ONLY grade signals, replaced by applyGradeListingPromotion), drip-trigger.ts (US-933; superseded by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts). PENDING, working as designed — measure-eval-stats.ts (US-1582 is OPEN and explicitly a human/operator task; it also HAS a caller, scripts/measure-eval.ts, so it was a false positive of the module-level check). JUDGEMENT CALL — grading-reliability.ts (US-481 AC3's self-consistency gate exists and runs in CI but only over hand-written fixture arrays, so it can never fail from a grading change; the notes concede a live-traffic feed is 'a future env-gated job'). NO OWNING STORY AT ALL — rubric.ts: migration 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and they are permanently NULL; the only record of intent is commit bbd94005 saying 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline... activation follow-up documented in rubric.ts', and that follow-up was never filed. Its client half IS live (src/lib/rubrics.ts, certificate.tsx), and the two 'MUST stay in sync' with no test pinning them — file the activation story. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts and ai-size-estimate-core.ts carry ⚠ headers naming the gap, because their green tests otherwise read as proof the feature exists. ai-size-estimate-core.ts's previous header actively asserted a false link ('ai-size-estimate.ts re-exports everything here') which would stop a reviewer looking further. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC4 DONE — prd-lint now warns on passes:true + an unresolved blocker marker (findUnresolvedDeferrals, exported + pure). CORRECTION TO THE COUNT ABOVE: it is FOUR stories, not three — US-744, US-1399, US-1770 and US-1931. I had cleared US-1931 last round using the same loose word-matching that this guard exists to replace; its notes are a SINGLE segment ending in DEFERRED 2026-07-11 with no later closing note, so it is unresolved. ⚠ THE GUARD SHIPPED WITH THE EXACT BUG IT TARGETS, CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT: v1 matched /(DONE|SHIPPED|...)/i anywhere after the marker and therefore cleared US-1770 — its motivating case — because ~2300 chars later the prose read "best done in a user-present session". Searching long free text for a common English word always finds it. Resolution is now a CASE-SENSITIVE uppercase closing token (DONE/CLOSED/SHIPPED/COMPLETED/RESOLVED/VERIFIED) in a LATER pipe-separated note SEGMENT, with an explicit NOT DONE exclusion so the negated form cannot clear anything. Verified against the real 1878-story archive: flags exactly US-744/1399/1770/1931 and correctly leaves US-1883 alone (its later CLOSED segment supersedes the earlier blocks-passes note — which is why this is a WARNING and can never be an error). ⚠ SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: npm run test:scripts is BROKEN ON A CLEAN TREE — both scripts/prd-lint.test.mjs and scripts/prd-digest.test.mjs fail with SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and run ZERO tests, while scripts/verify.mjs:63 runs that command in the web lane. Proven pre-existing by stashing my changes and re-running. node --check passes both files, esbuild transforms both fine, and a trivial probe .mjs test under the same config passes — so it is neither syntax nor the transform, and the cause is still unidentified. The 9 guard cases were therefore verified by executing findUnresolvedDeferrals directly under node instead; the vitest cases are committed and will cover it once the harness is fixed. This is the same class as the dead modules: a suite that looks like coverage and runs nothing. Needs its own story. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BROKEN test:scripts HARNESS IS FIXED — root cause was a CRLF SHEBANG. vite/esbuild strip a shebang by matching #!...
; with CRLF the stray  survives and the module fails to parse, so importing scripts/prd-lint.mjs or prd-digest.mjs from a vitest test threw SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and BOTH suites ran ZERO tests while scripts/verify.mjs:63 still invoked them in the web lane. Isolated by a 3-way experiment: shebang+CRLF FAILS, shebang+LF passes, no-shebang+CRLF passes — so it is the combination, not either alone. WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the git blobs are already LF and core.autocrlf=true rewrites them to CRLF ON CHECKOUT, so this is WINDOWS-ONLY and CI on Linux stayed green throughout. Every Windows checkout has been running zero script tests. Fix is .gitattributes: *.mjs and *.cjs now text eol=lf, extending the rule CLAUDE.md already documents for .githooks/** and *.sh (which exists for the same CRLF-shebang hazard, just a louder failure). Verified: npm run test:scripts goes 0 -> 27 tests passing across 2 files; the 9 findUnresolvedDeferrals cases from the previous commit — which I had to verify by hand under node because the harness was dead — now execute through the real harness and pass; node scripts/test-extensions.mjs still 13/13. ZERO content churn: the blobs were already LF, so after renormalizing, the only staged change is .gitattributes (+13 lines). | 2026-07-18 ⚠ CORRECTION — I OVERSTATED THIS STORY. AC2 (human-review routing on a counterfeit verdict) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, and my description saying it is 'absent' was wrong. ai-authenticity.ts:439 exports authenticityNeedsReview(), whose own docstring is tagged 'US-1770 (AC2)' — the exact AC I claimed was unmet — returning true on a red_flags verdict or on a recognisable brand assessed below AUTHENTICITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD. It is wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, where the grade_report is written as `needs_human_review: compositeResult.needs_human_review || authenticityNeedsReview(authenticityAssessment)`, and it is unit-tested in ai-authenticity_test.ts. So a counterfeit call DOES route to a human today. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, since it is instructive: the audit grepped red_flags, found the note site (grading-pipeline.ts:1663, which writes detailedNotes.counterfeit_confidence and sets no review flag), and concluded 'a note, and nothing else'. The ROUTING is ~400 lines further on and reaches the assessment through a helper rather than through the red_flags field, so a field-name grep could not see it. I verified the story's other two claims (US-1770 marked passes:true while its notes say DEFERRED; runAuthenticityEval having zero callers) and did NOT verify this one before writing it into a P1 description. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, re-checked this pass: AC1 — runAuthenticityEval still has ZERO callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate, so 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' is unenforced. AC3 (per-brand regressions block activation) depends on the same missing activation path. The severity drops accordingly: the safety net that catches a bad call at grade time EXISTS; what is missing is the gate that would stop a bad PROMPT VERSION shipping in the first place. Still worth doing, no longer 'counterfeit calls route nobody'. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) ai-size-estimate-core AC DONE. The live ai-size-estimate.ts now IMPORTS and re-exports the four shared helpers instead of re-declaring byte-identical copies, so the existing ai-size-estimate_test.ts — which imports the -core file — covers the functions that actually run. Proved with an identity check: core.isMeasurementPhoto === live.isMeasurementPhoto (and the same for normalizeSizeEstimate and prioritizeMeasurementPhotos, plus the constant), so it is genuinely one definition rather than two that happen to agree today. scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs no longer lists the module, which is the independent confirmation it now has a real importer. CHOSE 'live imports core', NOT 'delete core and repoint the test' — the AC allowed either, but core exists for a sound reason its header stated: the pure helpers must be testable WITHOUT dragging in the Anthropic SDK and env-gated config that ai-size-estimate.ts loads. The test sets no env stubs, so repointing it would have forced them and coupled a pure unit test to the AI client. Deleting core would have thrown away the correct half of the design. Verified byte-identity of all five shared declarations BEFORE merging, so this is a pure cleanup rather than a silent behaviour change; the now-dead private clamp01 was removed from the live module (deno lint flagged it, and core owns the copy that runs). Edge suite 4129 passed / 0 failed, lint 1168 files clean, deno check 0 errors. Net -29 lines. PROCESS NOTE: my first attempt used a brace-matching script to excise the declarations and silently corrupted the file — normalizeSizeEstimate's RETURN TYPE annotation contains braces, so the matcher closed early and left the body behind. tsc caught it immediately (TS2304 'Cannot find name raw'). Reverted with git checkout and redid it with explicit line ranges plus assertions that each range starts and ends on the expected text — clever beat correct, and the assertion-checked version was faster than debugging the clever one. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) DEFERRAL TRIAGE DONE, and it corrects my framing of US-1770 a THIRD time. US-1399: FALSE POSITIVE of my own guard — its notes carry '[COMPLETION 2026-07-03 - un-deferred]' and the work genuinely shipped (prerender.mjs fetches the transparency API with graceful degradation as the contract). The guard missed it twice over: COMPLETED? does not match COMPLETION, and the resolution sits in the SAME note segment, which my segment-only rule ignored. Both fixed; the archive now flags exactly US-744 and US-1931. US-744: TRUE POSITIVE — no resolution language anywhere after 'DEFERRED 2026-06-08'. Its own note says the remainder is service-worker/offline work that cannot be verified headless, so it is legitimately browser-gated rather than forgotten; it should be reopened or explicitly closed as won't-do, not left marked passing. ⚠ US-1770 IS NOT A DEFERRAL-INTEGRITY CASE AT ALL, and my P1 framing was overblown. Its notes DO carry a later '[DONE 2026-07-09] Eval machinery + human-review routing shipped', and both halves of that claim are TRUE: authenticityNeedsReview is wired (already corrected earlier today) and migration 00405 (authenticity_eval_cases/runs) plus authenticity-eval.ts do exist and are recorded in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. The DEFERRED marker it carries refers to GOLDEN-SET POPULATION — real labeled authentic/counterfeit data, which the grading-engine rules say must never be fabricated, so it is operator work by design and correctly not done by an agent. So the guard now CLEARS US-1770 and is right to. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT on US-1770 is narrow and structural: runAuthenticityEval has no callers because there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. AC1's 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' cannot be enforced until such a path exists — that is a build, not a wiring oversight. Downgrading the severity accordingly: this is not 'a safety gate was skipped', it is 'the gate has nothing to attach to yet'. LESSON, since I conflated them: the NOTES guard and the unwired-export AUDIT catch different things and neither substitutes for the other. The notes guard finds stories whose own history says unfinished. The audit finds code that no one calls. US-1770 was found by the audit and is invisible to the guard — correctly, because its notes are honest about what was built. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AUDIT TOOL FIXED — it had a real blind spot and was OVER-reporting. scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs only walked services/edge-functions/src, missing services/edge-functions/scripts/, where operator scripts are genuine callers. That produced at least three false positives: measure-eval-stats.ts (scripts/measure-eval.ts imports it and calls releaseGate at line 125 — it is the backbone of the US-1582 accuracy gate, not dead code), plus cron-runs renderCronDocs and renderCronSetupGuide (called by render-cron-docs.ts and render-cron-setup.ts). With scripts/ in the corpus the whole-dead-module list drops 10 -> 8 and the per-function list 54 -> 45, so the audit was over-reporting by roughly 17%. Re-checked that every story filed off this audit still rests on a STILL-FLAGGED item: title-sync.ts (US-1995), authenticity-eval.ts + brand-seed.ts (US-1996), rubric.ts (US-1997) — all still listed, so no filed story was built on a false positive. NOTE the direction: here my NOTES were right (they already recorded measure-eval-stats as a false positive, from the original triage) and my TOOL was wrong. An audit that over-reports gets ignored exactly as fast as one that under-reports, which is why this was worth fixing rather than annotating. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) BRAND-SEED CLAIM VERIFIED — substance HOLDS, one inherited detail was WRONG. VERIFIED TRUE, by reading the migration myself: 00389_brand_knowledge_base.sql declares source_url as plain `text` and confidence as `numeric(3,2) CHECK (confidence >= 0 AND confidence <= 1)` — both NULLABLE, with no NOT NULL. So US-1716 AC4's 'Provenance + confidence are REQUIRED on every seeded fact (schema-enforced)' is not enforced by the schema. VERIFIED TRUE: admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 does explicitly permit a null confidence (`if (value === null) { patch.confidence = null; continue; }`), so the write path allows what the AC says is required. VERIFIED TRUE: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts — the only code that would reject an unsourced fact — are imported by nothing (re-confirmed with the scripts/-aware audit, so this is not another blind-spot artefact). WRONG, and it was mine to check: the triage claimed the admin path 'never touches source_url'. It does — 7 references, and source_url sits in the editable-field allowlists at lines 48/53/57/61/65. The admin surface can set provenance perfectly well; what is missing is any requirement that it be set. That distinction matters for whoever fixes this: the work is a constraint (plus a backfill decision for existing rows), NOT plumbing source_url through an admin route that already handles it. ⚠ STILL UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: whether existing prod rows already violate the constraint. The suggested check — select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null — needs DB access; brand_knowledge is a deny-all operator table, so the public anon key cannot read it. Run that BEFORE adding NOT NULL, because a non-zero count turns a one-line constraint into a data migration. | 2026-07-18 ⚠ prd-lint AND prd-digest WERE SILENT NO-OPS ON WINDOWS. Both guarded their CLI with import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`, which compares a URL to a RAW FILESYSTEM PATH. On POSIX that coincides by luck (argv[1] starts with /, so file:// + /a/b is a valid file URL); on Windows argv[1] is C:Users... with backslashes and no third slash, so the comparison is ALWAYS false and main() never runs. node scripts/prd-lint.mjs exited 0 having done nothing. I ran that command ~15 times this session and read exit 0 as a passing lint every time; it is also the verify:web "web: prd-lint" step. Same shape as the CRLF-shebang bug: Windows-only, so CI stayed green and nobody noticed. Fixed both with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, and pinned with a test that greps for the broken form — a behavioural test cannot catch this, because the module under test imports fine either way. With the CLI actually running, prd-lint immediately reported two real things: the new stale-HELD warning, and that scripts/ralph/LEARNINGS.md is 1308 lines against an 800-line threshold (read every Ralph iteration — that warning has existed and been invisible). ALSO ADDED (the durable fix for the stale-HELD class): findStaleHeldMigrations() warns when a story calls a migration HELD that is already on origin/main. Keyed on PUSHED, not on version numbers, which makes it immune to its own correction text — the correction names the genuinely-pending pair, and a number-based check read those back out and reclassified corrected stories as pending. An explicit correction marker silences it, because notes are append-only so the stale sentence never goes away. 6 new tests; test:scripts 43 passed. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) grade-badge SUPERSEDED CLAIM VERIFIED MYSELF — and it holds, but both copies were actively lying about being in use. Checked commit 8e1802a6 directly: it removed compositeGradeBadge from the publish path and replaced it with applyGradeListingPromotion, under an explicit comment — 'Grade authority signal — TEXT ONLY (eBay-policy pivot). We never overlay a badge or attach the QR slab onto listing PHOTOS'. So the removal was a POLICY decision about third-party-grading marks on listing imagery, not neglect. Confirmed no policy violation survives: compositeGradeBadge has zero callers in src, edge, iOS or functions, and applyGradeListingPromotion IS wired at flipdesk-ebay.ts:5702. THE RESIDUAL RISK, now closed: both dead copies opened by describing themselves as live. The edge header read 'It runs at PUBLISH time (assemblePublishContext in routes/flipdesk-ebay.ts) so the badge reaches eBay for EVERY publish path', naming a call site that no longer calls it; the web header read 'Used by the listing composer (US-118)'. Both now carry a ⚠ block saying NOT WIRED, DELIBERATELY, do not restore, with the policy reason and the commit — because the next person to find an unused badge compositor and 'fix' it would reintroduce exactly the problem someone already paid attention to. Same false-link class as ai-size-estimate-core.ts claiming its live sibling re-exported it. This closes the last unverified entry in the 10-module triage table. Final tally of subagent claims I checked by hand: authenticity-eval WRONG on AC2 (routing existed), measure-eval-stats RIGHT (my own tool was blind to scripts/), rubric 'no owning story' WRONG in its evidence but right in conclusion, brand-seed RIGHT on substance and WRONG on the admin-path detail, grade-badge RIGHT. Roughly half needed correction, which is the argument for verifying every inherited claim before it reaches a story. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop, prompted by prd-lint findStaleHeldMigrations): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE and is superseded by this note — the migration file is already on origin/main, so the branch is NOT frozen and nobody should hold a push on its account. The distinction the old wording blurs and that still matters: PUSHED is not APPLIED. The file being on origin/main says nothing about whether the SQL has run against the prod DB; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth for what is actually applied, and 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending. So the correct residual action is an APPLY (+ NOTIFY pgrst), not a push-hold. | 2026-07-18 (agent loop) THREE ACs CLOSED, two remain. AC4 — VERIFIED ALREADY DONE, not re-implemented: findUnresolvedDeferrals() + the US-1996 warning block already exist in prd-lint.mjs and fire as warnings (never errors), which is what the AC asked for. AC6 — RESOLVED, and the resolution was already in the tree: ai-size-estimate.ts now imports + re-exports the four helpers from ai-size-estimate-core.ts instead of re-declaring them, so ai-size-estimate_test.ts (which imports core) covers the code that actually runs. What was still WRONG and is fixed here: core.ts header still opened with a big "⚠ THIS MODULE IS DEAD" block, which had become false — the exact stale-assertion failure mode this story is about, just inverted. Rewrote it to state the live relationship, keeping the history as a deliberate lesson (a comment asserting a link is not the link; make the dependency real and let the type checker hold it). AC3 (partial, via prd-lint rather than hand-triage) — the stale-HELD warning fired on US-1880/US-1897/US-1996; all three were verified against origin/main (files ARE pushed) and annotated with the sanctioned STATUS CORRECTION marker. Note the distinction the old notes blurred and that the corrections now state: PUSHED is not APPLIED — the file being on origin/main says nothing about the prod DB, so the residual action is an apply + NOTIFY pgrst, not a push-hold. ⚠ My first correction attempt RE-TRIGGERED the warning because it quoted the migration numbers with the word HELD and my wording did not match HELD_CORRECTED; the escape hatch exists and is documented in prd-lint.mjs — use the literal "STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM" / "STATUS CORRECTION" phrasing. STILL OPEN: AC1 (wire the authenticity eval gate — the real safety work) and AC5 (needs DB access to a deny-all table). ALSO DONE this pass, prompted by the OTHER standing prd-lint warning nobody had acted on: LEARNINGS.md was 1308 lines against its own 800 threshold and is read EVERY iteration. Split the three epic-specific bodies into scripts/ralph/learnings/{ios,brand-kb,email-marketing}.md and left LEARNINGS.md at 370 lines of cross-cutting content with a pointer section; scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md now tells the loop to read a topic file only when the story touches that surface. Verified NOTHING was lost: every non-empty line of the original 1264 is present across the four files (0 missing), headings 42 -> 43 (the +1 is the pointer). prd-lint is now fully clean (0 warnings) for the first time. | 2026-07-18 MEASURED CORRECTION to the status note above (agent loop): I wrote earlier today that "PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth ... 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending". That is FALSE and I am correcting my own claim. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00476, applied:00476, status:match} — the US-1566 block reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the DB own answer. 00475 and 00476 ARE APPLIED in prod. The only genuinely pending migration is 00477 (US-1999, correctly held/unpushed). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md has been corrected with the measured evidence and both sections re-marked APPLIED. The lesson: the answer was one unauthenticated HTTP GET away the whole time, and several passes (including mine) reasoned about prod schema state from commit history instead of measuring it. | 2026-07-19 AC1 ADDRESSED (as a guard, deliberately not as an implementation); AC4 + AC6 VERIFIED ALREADY DONE; AC5 still needs DB access. AC4 is shipped: prd-lint.mjs has findUnresolvedDeferrals (a WARNING, never an error, exactly as the AC required since a later note can legitimately supersede an earlier blocker). AC6 is shipped: ai-size-estimate.ts now imports the pure helpers from ai-size-estimate-core.ts (line 36, with a US-1996 marker), so the tests no longer point at a dead copy while the live helpers go untested. Both verified in the TREE rather than trusted from notes. AC1 IS THE INTERESTING ONE AND I SCOPED IT DELIBERATELY. Stating the situation precisely, because it is easy to misread in both directions: authenticity-eval.ts implements the gate and works; NOTHING imports it; but there is ALSO no authenticity prompt-activation path anywhere — the grading prompt lifecycle knows exactly three stages (per_image, composite, listing_gen) and none is authenticity. So 'no authenticity prompt version can activate without clearing the gate' is currently TRUE, VACUOUSLY: nothing can activate at all. The exposure is not present-tense. It is that someone later builds the activation path, does not know this module exists — its own tests are green, which reads like coverage — and ships an ungated one. I DID NOT WIRE IT, and that is the judgement to review: wiring today would mean inventing an authenticity prompt-version lifecycle nobody has asked for, a speculative feature built to satisfy a checkbox, which is precisely how authenticity-eval.ts became dead code in the first place. Instead the requirement is now impossible to miss AT THE MOMENT IT BECOMES REAL: authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts fails the build if any lib/ or routes/ file activates an authenticity prompt without calling runAuthenticityEval, plus a second test pinning that the gate module still EXISTS — otherwise deleting it as 'dead code' would make the first guard pass for the wrong reason, an empty check over an unenforced requirement. TWO MISTAKES CAUGHT WHILE BUILDING IT, both worth recording. (1) My first heuristic ORed the two concepts across a whole FILE and fired on ai-grading.ts — a false positive: ~3000 lines that legitimately mention per-image authenticity types and, hundreds of lines away, cache invalidation for 'a newly activated prompt version'. I read the hit rather than suppressing it, and replaced co-presence with PROXIMITY (300 chars). A guard that cries wolf is one people delete. (2) Shell escaping mangled the regex to activatew*s*w*prompt — it still PASSED, because the literal alternative matched, so it was green for the wrong reason. Fixed via a direct edit. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED with a real temporary fixture module that activates an authenticity prompt with no gate call: the guard names the file and fails; removing the fixture returns green. Verified: edge 4256 passed, deno check + lint clean. STILL OPEN: AC3 (triage US-744 / US-1399) and AC5 (US-1716 AC4 needs 'select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null' against a deny-all table). | 2026-07-19 TRIAGED THE THREE REMAINING DEAD MODULES from audit-unwired-exports.mjs (this story's family — the tool's own output says superseded, pending and half-wired look identical and each needs verifying by hand). Verdicts recorded in vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md. (1) content-ai-email.ts = SUPERSEDED: US-922's newsletter-copy.ts carries the same header and IS imported by newsletter-assembler.ts step 2; the old one generated AND persisted, the replacement is pure prompt-building. 4 exports, 0 tests, 0 callers — dead like drip-trigger.ts. (2) rubric.ts = PENDING and correctly so: it self-documents as FOUNDATION ONLY and is covered by the open US-1997. (3) brand-seed.ts = THE INTERESTING ONE, AND A REAL UNENFORCED GUARANTEE. Its header says every seed run passes through validateBrandFact so an unsourced fact is 'REJECTED, not stored'. It has zero callers and COULD NEVER HAVE HAD ANY: brand facts are seeded by 37 SQL MIGRATIONS (178 inserts) and SQL cannot call a TypeScript validator; admin-brand-knowledge.ts performs no writes at all; and the schema does not enforce it either — 00389 declares source_url as NULLABLE. So the guarantee rested entirely on author discipline across 37 hand-written files. I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING: 178 of 178 inserts list source_url, so the discipline held perfectly — which is exactly when a ratchet is free. Added brand-fact-provenance_test.ts, verified by planting a column-list omission (fails naming 00389:181). WHY THIS ONE EARNED A GUARD when I declined others this session: brand_knowledge grounds AUTHENTICITY assessments, and an unsourced row does not announce itself at read time — it reads like every other fact and makes the model MORE confident, not less. Scope is deliberate: it checks the insert COLUMN LIST, not values, because a deliberate NULL is a visible choice in review whereas a missing column is the mechanical slip. GENERALISABLE FINDING, now in the note: a module can be unwired because THE PATH IT WAS BUILT FOR DOES NOT EXIST — brand-seed and title-sync both failed that way, so check a module's declared callers are real before wiring it. Verified: 4458 edge tests, deno lint clean, vault:lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) TRIAGED THE HIGH-STAKES ENTRIES ON THE AUDIT'S SECOND LIST ('tested but never called', 49 functions — the tool warns some are legitimate test-only helpers). Picked the four whose names imply money or safety. THREE WERE FINE and I am reporting them as such rather than inflating them: (1) evaluatePoolGate — SUPERSEDED by US-2144's move into the reserve_guarantee_pool_drawdown RPC, so the caps are decided and recorded under one advisory lock instead of racing. I SUSPECTED THE MOVE HAD DROPPED THE THIRD GATE and checked rather than filing it: all three gates AND all three reason strings (account_cap, period_budget, loss_ratio) are in 00490, including the only-once-accrued condition. Nothing was lost. (2) isLedgerConsistent — a unit-test helper in credit-ledger_test.ts; the integration suite that would exercise it live is the one still skipped for want of credentials (US-2038 AC2), so this is that gap, not a new one. (3) sellerIntegrityTier — PENDING behind the open US-1912, which is the correct state. (4) resolveHalt WAS A REAL FINDING and is now fixed: agent-kernel.ts:432 REIMPLEMENTED IT INLINE — same precedence, same two reason strings — while the pure tested resolveHalt sat with zero callers, so its 6 tests were proving a copy nobody ran. The kernel now calls it. PROVED EQUIVALENT BEFORE COMMITTING rather than asserting it: transcribed the old inline block verbatim into a throwaway and compared across every status x globalPause combination (14, including casing variants and the empty string) — 0 mismatches; throwaway deleted, the durable coverage is the existing agent-policy tests now exercising the live path. ALSO ANNOTATED guarantee-pool.ts: evaluatePoolGate and the SQL are a LOCKSTEP MIRROR WITH ONLY THE SQL SIDE LIVE, so editing a cap rule in TS changes nothing in production — the exact shape US-1995 documents, flagged in-file so the next reader is not misled by its green tests. Verified: 4458 edge tests, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) FINISHED THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF OF THE 'tested but never called' LIST — and CORRECTED MYSELF: I claimed last pass that the remainder was 'mostly _resetForTest helpers'. Filtering those out leaves ~22 real functions, so that was wrong. Triaged the rest of the high-stakes ones. THE PATTERN IS NOW CLEAR AND IS THE USEFUL OUTPUT: this repo repeatedly writes a PURE, TESTED SPECIFICATION and then implements the live path DIFFERENTLY — inline (resolveHalt, now fixed), in SQL (evaluatePoolGate → 00490), via a shared registry (buildListingPullPatch/buildCsvFillPatch/isGradeThreadOwned → the route executes EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS directly, which is US-1994's recorded resolution), or via a stronger atomic claim (canExecute → the pending→approved claim in approveAndExecute). None of those four is a bug. But every one is a SILENT-DRIFT SITE: edit the tested spec and production is unchanged, with green tests either way. So the triage question for this list is NOT 'is this dead?' but 'WHAT IMPLEMENTS THIS INSTEAD?'. TWO GENUINE GAPS FOUND: resolveHalt (fixed last pass) and crossCheckDecodeResult — the decoder cross-check that flags impossible production dates, the strongest deterministic counterfeit signal available, whose consuming plumbing exists but whose producer is never called. Recorded against US-2138, whose founding premise it falsifies. delistMethodFor remains unchecked-but-uncalled and is the one loose end; it is a pure planner helper on a non-money path, so it is the lowest-value of the set. | 2026-08-02 AC4 CORRECTED — it shipped BLIND TO ITS OWN FOUNDING CASES, and that is the finding. The guard was built and negative-verified, but it read only prd.json, and all THREE stories it was written for (US-1770, US-744, US-1399) had already been ARCHIVED. It could not see a single one of them. A check that structurally cannot reach the cases that motivated it reads as green for the wrong reason, which is exactly the failure this warning exists to surface, one level up. FIXED: lintPrd now takes archivedStories and scans [...active, ...archived]; main() parses prd.archive.json best-effort (a missing or unparseable archive leaves the guard scanning the active backlog rather than failing a lint it only reads for warnings). Cost is a ~50ms parse of 1.6 MB on an on-demand lint. THE OUTPUT IS ACTIONABLE, NOT NOISE, which is why it is worth turning on: over the entire archive it flags TWO stories, US-744 (DEFERRED 2026-06-08, needs real device/PWA QA) and US-1931 (DEFERRED 2026-07-11, wants a schema migration for an idempotent per-job reservation). A warning naming hundreds would be ignored, and the active-backlog half would be ignored with it. 4 new tests: an archived blocker is reported, an active one still is and both appear in ONE warning (two warnings for one class is how a reader starts skipping the second), an archived blocker resolves by the same rule as an active one (the archive must not get a stricter rule, or the warning fills with things somebody already handled), and a missing archive is not an error. THREE OTHER ACs RE-CHECKED AGAINST CODE, and two of the story's own premises are now stale. AC6's premise is FALSE: ai-size-estimate.ts does NOT re-declare core's helpers — it imports them (lines 33-36), re-exports them (41-44) and CALLS the imported ones (152, 208). I grepped for a shadowing local declaration and there is none. So the tests pointing at core ARE testing the live helpers; someone made the module import core as its header always claimed, and the AC text was never updated. AC1's SUBSTANCE is resolved, but not by this story: US-2130 added assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (fail-closed) plus authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, a source scan that fails the build if an authenticity prompt-activation path appears without calling runAuthenticityEval. There are zero activation sites today and absence is the correct current state, so the gate cannot be bypassed by a future path without turning the build red. runAuthenticityEval is also no longer callerless — admin-grading.ts:1358 invokes it. AC3: US-1399 carries "[COMPLETION 2026-07-03 - un-deferred]" and is genuinely resolved; US-744 is genuinely unresolved and the widened guard now names it. A GUARD BEHAVIOUR WORTH KNOWING, found while checking this: US-1770 is NOT flagged even with the archive scanned, and it is cleared for the WRONG REASON. Its single note segment reads "[DEFERRED 2026-07-09] Needs a HELD migration ... [DONE 2026-07-09] Eval machinery + human-review routing shipped". The same-segment resolution rule sees the uppercase [DONE] and clears it — but that DONE is scoped to the eval machinery, while the DEFERRED was about the held migration for the eval CASES tables. The outcome happens to be right (US-2130 resolved the substance) so this is not a live defect, but the guard's own header claims it was hardened against precisely this by making the token case-SENSITIVE. A bracketed uppercase [DONE] about a different sub-part still clears a deferral. Recorded rather than changed: tightening it needs a rule for "which blocker does this closing refer to", and inventing one on a single example is how a guard starts crying wolf. STILL OPEN ON THIS STORY: AC5 (needs a DB read — now answerable, see the prod-diagnostics note) and AC3's disposition of US-744 (reopen or record the deferral as standing — an owner call, since the work is real PWA/offline work that was never done). VERIFIED: scripts suite 245 tests pass (up 4). One PRE-EXISTING failure unrelated to this change: scripts/ralph/run-sdk.test.mjs cannot import @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, which is not installed. That is a test file no runner can execute — the same shape as everything else in this story — and it is worth its own story. | 2026-08-02 AC3 TRIAGED — both stories, opposite answers. This is the AC that said "US-744 and US-1399 are triaged the same way: both are passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED and no later resolution note. Either reopen them or record why the deferral is now satisfied." With the guard now reaching the archive, the actual list is US-744 and US-1931 (US-1399 carries "[COMPLETION 2026-07-03 - un-deferred]" and was never a real hit). US-1931 IS A FALSE POSITIVE AND IS NOW RESOLVED. Its 2026-07-14 segment records the finished work but carries no uppercase closing token, so the 2026-07-11 DEFERRED was never cleared — exactly the shape the guard's own header warns about ("a later note legitimately supersedes an earlier blocker"). I checked the work rather than taking the note's word: migration 00445 adds listing_generation_jobs.ai_reserved and is applied to prod (below the measured 00512 watermark), needsAiReservation reads the flag at flipdesk-autolister.ts:216, and AC4's test EXISTS AND PASSES — "US-1931: crash-after-reserve → reclaim consumes exactly ONE reservation" in autolister-reliability_test.ts, 16/16 green. Appended a VERIFIED/RESOLVED segment to the archived story (targeted text edit on prd.archive.json, not a JSON round-trip — a 4 MB reserialize would have reformatted the whole file for a 987-byte append; the anchor was asserted unique and the result re-parsed). Its "Migration HELD (not pushed)" line was also stale and is now noted as such. US-744 IS A TRUE POSITIVE AND STAYS FLAGGED. Its deferral reads "needs real device/PWA QA" and that is still true — service-worker offline behaviour, install prompts and a real device are the substance of the story, and none of it can be verified from a checkout. It is correctly passes:true-with-a-blocker only in the sense that the record is wrong; the honest state is that the work was never done. RECOMMENDATION: file a successor story rather than editing the archive to say DONE — the archive is history and US-744's history is that it was closed without the work. userStories.title: FlipDesk is described but never shown publicly; contradictory 'Join waitlist' CTA signals vaporware
userStories.description: As a high-volume reseller evaluating FlipDesk, we want to see the actual tool before signing up. The public site describes FlipDesk with icon+text cards but shows ZERO product screenshots, GIFs, or demo; the genuinely strong AutoLister (batch upload, HEIC/Live Photo, auto-group, bulk generate, auto-publish) is only visible AFTER signup. The power-reseller persona had to commit on faith and nearly bounced. Compounding the vaporware read: the homepage closing section pairs 'Join waitlist' next to 'Start Grading Free' even though the product is clearly live — a mixed launch signal at the exact conversion moment.
acceptanceCriteria: Homepage and /for-resellers show real FlipDesk/AutoLister imagery (screenshots and/or a short Loom/GIF) of the bulk pipeline
The contradictory 'Join waitlist' CTA is removed or reconciled now that the product is live
userStories.notes: [P3][Web/Conversion] 5-persona QA sweep 2026-07-13. Power-reseller persona: the tool is strong but hidden behind a signup wall; 'Join waitlist' next to 'Start Grading Free' reads as vaporware. | 2026-07-14 (branch claude/prd-stories-review-lsem0z): AC2 SATISFIED + AC1 SUBSTANTIALLY ADDRESSED. AC2: audited the whole app — there is NO public "Join waitlist" CTA rendered anywhere (WaitlistForm component is unused; the homepage/for-resellers closing CTAs are "Try FlipDesk Free"/"Start Grading Free" + a legit newsletter signup), so the vaporware CTA contradiction is already gone. AC1: the landing page already showed the FlipDesk pipeline via honest per-stage stylized mocks (labeled "not a real screenshot"); /for-resellers only DESCRIBED it in text. Extracted the stage data to src/components/marketing/flipdesk-stages.ts and a reusable presentational src/components/marketing/flipdesk-pipeline-preview.tsx (no landing-only data-flipdesk-* scroll-scene hooks, so flipdesk-scene.ts does not bind it), then added a "The full reseller workflow, built in" section to /for-resellers rendering the full source→grade→list→reprice→reconcile pipeline + a "Try FlipDesk Free" CTA. landing.tsx now imports the shared FLIPDESK_STAGES (dropped its inline copy + now-unused Boxes/Tag icons). Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean; npm run build prerenders 213 routes and dist/for-resellers.html (36KB) contains the pipeline stages + honesty caption + CTA. KEPT passes:false: AC1 literally asks for real screenshots and/or a short Loom/GIF — the stylized mocks show the flow honestly but real product imagery is a design-asset follow-up (no FlipDesk/AutoLister screenshots exist in the repo to wire in). | 2026-08-02 AC2 RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not taken from the previous note): grepped every .tsx/.ts under src for waitlist CTAs. WaitlistForm has ZERO importers — the only hit outside its own file is a COMMENT in newsletter-signup.tsx saying it mirrors WaitlistForm's prerender-safe dynamic import. So the string "Join waitlist" exists only inside a component nothing renders, and the vaporware CTA contradiction is genuinely gone from every public surface. AC2 holds. AC1 IS NOT COMPLETABLE FROM A CHECKOUT and I want that stated plainly rather than left as "substantially addressed". The AC asks for REAL FlipDesk/AutoLister imagery — screenshots or a short GIF of the bulk pipeline. What exists is honest stylized mocks, explicitly labelled "not a real screenshot", now shared between the landing page and /for-resellers via flipdesk-stages.ts + flipdesk-pipeline-preview.tsx. That was the right intermediate step and it removed the /for-resellers text-only gap, but a labelled mock is precisely what the story says is insufficient: the persona in the description "had to commit on faith", and a drawing that admits it is a drawing does not fix that. Producing the real thing needs the app running against a real account with real inventory, someone to capture it, and a judgement call about what seller data is safe to show publicly. That is a human with the product open, not a code change. RECOMMENDATION: treat AC1 as an asset-production task and either assign it or split it out, rather than leaving the story open against a checkout that cannot satisfy it. A SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME GREP, worth its own attention: the waitlist BACKEND is still live while its only public entry point is orphaned. /api/waitlist exists, /admin/waitlist is in the admin nav, and edge-fetch.ts:160 still routes a waitlist-gated account to a dedicated pending page — but nothing on the public site can add anyone to that list. So the system is half-wired in the direction that is hard to notice: an operator opening the admin page sees a waitlist that can only ever shrink. Same shape as vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md catalogues, and the same decision it always needs — either the waitlist is a live feature whose public capture form should be rendered somewhere, or it is retired and the form, the admin page and the gating branch go together. Not decided here because removing gating touches the auth path, and rendering a waitlist form on a live product would reintroduce the exact vaporware signal AC2 exists to prevent. That tension is the reason it needs a decision rather than a default.

userStories.title: bulkMigrateListing — bring a seller's existing eBay (Trading) listings under management
userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. Implement Inventory API bulk_migrate_listing to convert eligible legacy listings into managed Inventory offers.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge calls POST /sell/inventory/v1/bulk_migrate_listing for eligible active Trading listings and links the resulting SKU/offerId to the inventory_items/listings rows
Migrated listings flip to a managed origin so revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote become available (respecting the sync source-of-truth contract)
Ineligible listings (variations/other) are reported with the eBay reason, not silently dropped
Idempotent; a seller can trigger migration from the app and see progress/results
userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. The listing would be marked GT-managed while being unmanageable: strictly worse than the read-only mirror it replaced, because the origin flip ALSO stops the inbound pull from mirroring it (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS are only overwritten while origin='ebay'). So the row would go stale AND be unmanageable. THE DECISION (needed before implementing): where does eBay's migrated sku live? (a) listings.platform_fields.migrated_sku — jsonb exists (00113), NO migration, but both sku-deriving sites must learn to prefer it; (b) overwrite inventory_items.sku with eBay's — there IS precedent (ebay-sku-match.tsx:983 already writes eBay's Custom Label into item.sku 'so the two systems agree'), and it is user-initiated rather than a pull, BUT SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH lists sku under GRADETHREAD_OWNED_ITEM_FIELDS ('always owned by GradeThread — no eBay pull may write these') and item.sku is unique-per-user so a migrated sku can COLLIDE with an existing item; (c) a new listings.platform_sku column — cleanest, needs a MIGRATION (blocked while the agent loop consumes 00468-00473 for the Brand KB block). Recommend (c), or (a) if the migration must wait. This is a documented-contract decision (CLAUDE.md flags SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md as the contract for this area), not a coin flip — deliberately not decided unilaterally. Everything else about the story is ready: eBay's contract is confirmed, the origin flip works, and the flip must happen ONLY after eBay confirms the per-listing migration succeeded (a partial failure must leave origin='ebay', or the row becomes stale AND unmanageable). BLOCKED ON US-1999 (filed 2026-07-18). The SKU problem this note identified is not specific to migration — it is a live defect in its own right: the eBay Inventory SKU is derived at three sites from the freely-editable inventory_items.sku and never pinned, so a seller renaming a SKU can orphan an already-live listing. US-1999 adds the stored SKU. Migration cannot link bulk_migrate_listing's returned sku to anything until that column exists, so do US-1999 first and this story gets much smaller. | 2026-07-18 EDGE COMPLETE (agent loop) — THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The 2026-07-17 investigation ended on an open design question (where does eBay own migrated sku live?); US-1999 answered it this session by adding listings.inventory_sku (00477), so option (a) platform_fields.migrated_sku is moot — the SKU has a real, indexed, listing-scoped column and BOTH derive sites already read it. AC1 — lib/ebay-migrate.ts (pure) + bulkMigrateListing() in ebay-client.ts + POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate. AC2 — the origin flip and the SKU write happen in ONE update and ONLY when eBay returned a SKU; the module header and a dedicated test spell out why: flipping origin without the sku produces a row that is marked managed, is not addressable by any Inventory call, AND has stopped being refreshed by the inbound pull (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH only overwrites EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS while origin=ebay) — strictly worse than the mirror it replaced. The single most important test asserts a 2xx WITH NO SKU is a FAILURE, not a success. AC3 — every listing is accounted for: eBay errors surface longMessage verbatim; listings eBay omitted from responses[] are reported rather than vanishing; and OUR OWN pre-flight skips (not found / already GT-published / no platform_listing_id / not active) each carry a reason, since a listing that silently disappears from the result is the same defect whether we or eBay dropped it. AC4 (partial) — idempotent: an already-migrated row returns already_managed instead of erroring, so retrying a partly-failed batch is safe; eBay 5-per-call cap enforced by chunkForMigrate, plus a separate 50-per-REQUEST cap so one HTTP call cannot fan out into 40 sequential eBay calls and time out. US-268: ids come from the request body, so the read is scoped .eq(user_id, workspaceOwnerId ?? userId) and only rows that come back are acted on; a request naming ONLY foreign ids 404s rather than returning 200 with per-item not-found (a bulk 200 would make a cross-tenant probe indistinguishable from success at the status level), and tenant-isolation_test.ts has the required case. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4144 edge tests pass (8 new). ⚠ HELD — depends on 00477, so it ships with that migration; the route SELECTs inventory_sku. STILL OPEN for passes: AC4 UI (trigger + progress/results in the app — the Reconciliation page is the natural home) and a real-eBay end-to-end run, which cannot be done in the sandbox. | 2026-07-18 AC4 UI DONE (agent loop). Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 2232 vitest tests pass, 4144 deno tests pass. Everything code-side across all four ACs is complete. Still HELD behind 00477. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE. The stack was pushed and BOTH migrations are APPLIED IN PRODUCTION — measured, not assumed: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00478, applied:00478, status:match} with database ok and status ready, and the deployed frontend bundle reports release 91d466d22f2ef6061e07d6dd56f2a521a5aa562a (the head of origin/main). So the apply-before-push ordering was honored and nothing is frozen. So the feature is still healthy in prod. The ONLY remaining item is unchanged and unreachable from a sandbox: a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it) needs a live seller account with legacy listings. userStories.title: Handbags and small leather goods cannot be graded — 'bag' routes into the clothing rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of handbags, I want a bag graded on the things that determine a bag's price, because 'bag' is already a garment_category and item_category has 'bags' (00230), while the only rubric that will accept it grades fabric condition at 30% and odor at 10%. A handbag's condition is corner and edge-paint wear (the single most-inspected area and the most expensive to restore), handle and strap darkening and cracking, hardware plating loss and zipper pull function, interior lining staining and pen marks and odor, structural slouch and base sag, and glazing on the edges. The category also carries the most authenticity weight of anything we touch — the existing tells (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) are ALL bag brands — so grading and the authenticity add-on land on the same item here, and the certificate has to be careful not to let a condition grade read as an authenticity verdict.
acceptanceCriteria: A handbags/leather-goods rubric is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Photo slots cover the areas that decide a bag's grade: corners, base, interior, hardware, handles/straps, and the date-code/serial location.

A condition grade on a bag must NOT read as an authenticity statement anywhere on the certificate or in the buyer writeup — an explicit separation, test-asserted on the rendered copy, given these are the brands the authenticity add-on covers.
Measurement templates cover bag dimensions (width, height, depth, strap drop).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.

userStories.title: Neckwear and small accessories cannot be graded — ties, belts, scarves and gloves have no rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of accessories, I want ties, belts, scarves and gloves gradeable, because belt and scarf are already garment_category values with nowhere to route and neckwear is not even representable. These share a shape — small, single-construction, few failure modes, and a condition profile the clothing rubric's five factors describe badly. A tie's condition is the blade shape and roll, the tipping and keeper loop, the interlining (a tie that has lost its roll is damaged even with a perfect face), and stains that are effectively permanent on silk. A belt's is the strap creasing and cracking, the buckle and prong and the hole elongation. A scarf's is fringe integrity, pilling and pulls. Odor and cleanliness at 10% and structural integrity at 25% do not carry those.
acceptanceCriteria: An accessories rubric (or a small set of them where the categories genuinely diverge) is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Decide and record whether ties/belts/scarves/gloves share one rubric or split — the decision goes in the story notes, not a commit message.
garment_category is widened to represent neckwear and gloves; the migration follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats.
Measurement templates cover the fields the categories are actually sold on (tie blade width and length, belt length and hole positions, scarf dimensions).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a golden set bootstrapped for these categories.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.

userStories.title: Headwear cannot be graded — hats have a garment_category, no rubric, no photo slots and no measurements
userStories.description: As a seller of hats, I want to grade a cap the way I grade a hoodie, because headwear is a high-volume resale category and today 'hat' is a garment_category value that routes into a clothing rubric which cannot express it. Verified: GARMENT_CATEGORIES includes 'hat'; rubric.ts has clothing, sports_cards, watches and shoes and nothing else; MEASUREMENT_TEMPLATES has top/bottom/dress/outerwear/shoes/watch/generic and nothing else; the required image types are front/back/label. The weighted-overall computation stays in lockstep across all three rounding sites in the same commit as any factor-set generalization this requires.
