userStories.notes: [P2][Ops/Payments] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Smallest fix-to-impact ratio in the audit: one line converts silent revenue loss into a page. Blocked in practice on the alert-channel story (setting the webhook secrets), since the fan-out currently has nowhere to go. | 2026-07-18 FIXED (agent loop). recordWebhookDeadLetter now emits a CRITICAL ops event alongside the existing captureException, so a dropped webhook reaches the on-call fan-out instead of only Sentry (whose routing is separately unverified — US-2003). Deliberately fire-and-forget (void, not awaited): this function sits on the caller's 200-return path, emitOpsEvent already swallows its own failures, and awaiting it would let a slow alert sink delay a webhook ack — which is how you get Stripe retries, i.e. the exact storm the dead-letter path exists to prevent. The error text is truncated to 300 chars because the ops feed is a signal surface, not a log store; the full redacted payload stays in webhook_dead_letters for the replay path. Verified: deno check clean, existing webhook-dead-letter_test.ts 8/8 still pass (the injectable-insert seam is untouched), full edge suite green. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 — force a dead-letter in staging and confirm the alert actually lands in the on-call channel. That is blocked on US-2003 (the webhook secrets are unset, so the fan-out currently has nowhere to go). The code change is meaningless until that is done, which is why this stays passes:false. | 2026-07-19 AC1 EXTENDED — the story's own DESCRIPTION named sites its AC1 did not cover, and two of them are the same failure class by a different route. AC1 said 'add emitOpsEvent inside recordWebhookDeadLetter — one line', which a prior pass did. But the description also cited 'routes/webhooks.ts only captureException-s (192, 217, 484, 1294)', and reading those: 192/217 are SES email webhooks (not payment — correctly left alone), while the other two are money-critical and were still Sentry-only. (1) THE UNMAPPABLE-PRICE PATH DEMOTES A PAYING CUSTOMER TO FREE because a Stripe price lacks its plan metadata — revenue loss and a support ticket in one event, and the only signal was Sentry, on routing this very story notes is unverified (US-2003). (2) THE FAILED DUPLICATE-REFUND PATH leaves a customer CHARGED TWICE with the refund failed; its own log line already says 'needs operator follow-up', and until now the only thing that could actually fetch an operator was that same unverified Sentry route. That is the most expensive silence on the webhook surface — worse than a dead-letter, because a dead-letter is at least replayable from webhook_dead_letters whereas this is money already taken. Both now emit CRITICAL ops events. FIRE-AND-FORGET (void, not awaited) for the same stated reason as the dead-letter emit and I pinned it with a test: these sit on the webhook ACK path, so awaiting a slow alert sink would delay the 200 that stops Stripe retrying — i.e. the alert about a webhook problem would itself cause the retry storm. The duplicate-refund error text is truncated to 300 chars because the ops feed is a signal surface, not a log store. 3 tests, source-asserted (these handlers talk to Stripe and the service-role client with no injection seam, so the property worth pinning — 'does this path reach the on-call fan-out at all' — is visible in the source). NEGATIVE-VERIFIED both directions: deleting the unmappable-price emit and switching an emit from void to await each turn the suite red. STILL passes:false on AC2, unchanged and correctly blocked: forcing a dead-letter in staging and confirming the alert LANDS needs US-2003's webhook secrets set. Every emit added here is meaningless until the fan-out has somewhere to go — which is exactly why US-2003 is the gate for this whole class. | 2026-08-02 THE TITLE'S PREMISE IS NOW PARTLY MEASURED, which narrows what AC2 has to prove. The title says Sentry's routing is "unverified". Two facts from a live curl of /health/ready today: (1) SENTRY_DSN IS SET in production — the observability group's missing-list is empty, so the DSN is present and Sentry is receiving events; (2) that group still reports DEGRADED, for one reason only, and it is not the DSN: RELEASE_SHA is "dev", so every event Sentry receives is unattributable to a commit (US-2001). So the accurate statement is no longer "we do not know if Sentry gets anything" — it gets events. What remains unverified is whether a Sentry event ROUTES to a human, which is a Sentry-side alert-rule question and exactly what AC2's drill exists to settle. ALSO RELEVANT AND MEASURED: features.alerting reports "ok", so the ops-event fan-out AC1 hooked into HAS at least one live channel (MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL). That matters for this story specifically: AC1's emitOpsEvent means a dead-letter no longer depends on Sentry alone, and the second path is configured rather than theoretical. What is still unproven for BOTH paths is DELIVERY — a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports "ok" on /health/ready forever, which is precisely the false confidence US-2003 exists to remove and precisely why AC2 asks for a forced dead-letter rather than a config read. userStories.title: tag_eras is seeded across the brand KB and read by nothing — no garment can be dated
userStories.description: As a seller listing vintage, I want the tag generation on my garment to date it, because era is often the single largest multiplier on a piece's value and it is printed on the label. Verified: brand_knowledge.tag_eras (jsonb '[{era, years, description}]', 00389) is seeded across the brand packs and the ONLY code that touches it is plumbing — brand-knowledge.ts:83/103/259 carries it through the pack shape and brand-knowledge.ts:322 selects the column; three brand-normalize.ts comments reference it in prose. No prompt injects it, no comparison uses it, nothing surfaces it. Same failure mode as registered_numbers: a seeded, human-verifiable, high-value fact with no consumer.
acceptanceCriteria: The tag_eras entries for a resolved brand are injected into the grading and/or extraction path as trusted reference context so a transcribed tag can be matched to an era.
A matched era is persisted and surfaced (report field / listing item-specific), with the matched era's own confidence — a guessed decade is worse than a blank.
Era is INFORMATIONAL and must not move any condition factor score: a 1990s garment is not graded on a 1990s curve. A test asserts factor scores are unchanged by era presence.
Era carries into authenticity as a consistency check only (an era-inconsistent tag is a flag, not a verdict), respecting the US-1770 no-auto-authenticate posture.
Seeded tag_eras rows get the same provenance/confidence pass as the RN work — an unsourced era claim on a public certificate is a liability.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Second seeded-but-unread column. Also the enabling dependency for the vintage/band-tee brand pack (US-2220), where the tag generation IS the identity and the price. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED except AC5 (blocked on a schema change — see below). Commit 46b1a1d. Runs under the same GRADING_TAG_OCR gate as US-2210, still default OFF. AC1 DONE: the brand pack's tag_eras are resolved once per submission and rendered into the DEDICATED TAG-OCR CALL, not into the per-image or composite grading prompts. That placement is the key design decision: the tag-OCR call already looks at the label alone and is already flag-gated, so the three lockstep-governed grading prompts are UNTOUCHED and factor scores are provably unaffected rather than argued to be. AC2 DONE: matchTagEra resolves the model's returned id back to a SEEDED entry against the same filtered list the block was rendered from, so it cannot introduce an era we never curated (tested against era_99/era_0/free-text/hallucinated ids). ERA_MATCH_MIN_CONFIDENCE is 0.7, deliberately STRICTER than the 0.4 transcription bar — reading 'Levi's' at 0.5 still gives a usable brand, but a half-sure decade is a fabricated provenance claim on a public certificate; a test guards the RELATIONSHIP, not just the number. Persisted inside the existing tag_read jsonb (no new migration). AC3 DONE: a test asserts the composite prompt with an era differs from the no-tag-block prompt by EXACTLY the identity block and nothing else, with the factor weights string intact in both. The era renders as 'Tag generation ... NOT a manufacture date' and adds an explicit 'not a reason to grade more leniently or more harshly' line. AC4 DONE, AND IT TURNED OUT REACHABLE RATHER THAN ASPIRATIONAL: when the style code decodes to a production year (brand-decoders via decoderSpecsFromPack) AND the label's design matched a dated generation, those are two INDEPENDENT readings of the same garment and must agree. eraYearRange parses every shape the corpus actually uses ('1980s-early 90s' -> 1980-1999, '1960s-80s' -> 1960-1989, '2019-present' -> bounded by the current year); an UNPARSEABLE years string yields NO check rather than a comparison against a guessed range. A 1-year tolerance absorbs changeovers that straddle the boundary our prose records. The conflict is severity 'flag' with a message that names no verdict — a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake/authentic never appear — and it is deliberately kept OUT of the grading prompt (a separate test), because telling a grader 'this may be relabelled' invites it to move a condition score on an authenticity suspicion. ⚠ AC5 IS NOT DONE AND CANNOT BE DONE AS A DATA PASS. tag_eras entries have NO PER-ENTRY PROVENANCE: source_url, confidence and verified live on the brand ROW, so an unsourced era inside an otherwise-verified brand is indistinguishable from a sourced one. Since dating claims are the highest-liability content in the KB (era IS the price in vintage), that is the gap to close before any era reaches a public certificate — and closing it means a schema change. Left open deliberately rather than faked. TWO FINDINGS WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME, both recorded in vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-negative-findings.md. (1) tag_eras is TWO THINGS IN ONE COLUMN: of 220 seeded entries across 32 packs only ~174 can date anything; the rest carry years 'all'/'current'/'ongoing' and describe a code FORMAT that never changed (Nike style-number, adidas article-number, Ralph Lauren label). Nothing is wrong with those rows — the column absorbed both kinds of fact because there was nowhere else for format notes — but offering them as datable eras invites a confident 'this is from the all era', so datingEras() filters on whether years names a year or a decade. This is why ids resolve against the FILTERED list, which a test pins. (2) The reference block tells the model outright that the list is NOT exhaustive and that omitting is correct when unsure. A brand's seeded eras are never a complete history, and cornering the model into the closest listed option is precisely how a guessed decade reaches a certificate. ALSO: extractTagGroundTruth gained an optional eraBlock param; every pre-existing caller passes nothing and a test pins userInstructions('') === userInstructions(). The trusted block's CLOSING LINE is byte-identical to the US-2210 wording when no era matched — an early draft reworded it for every grade and that was corrected, so adding era support did not silently change the prompt for grades that have none. VERIFICATION: 4590 edge tests pass, 30 new in tag-era_test.ts; the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210. deno lint clean; no new type errors (the 2 imagescript ones are pre-existing and come from the npm dependency substitution this sandbox needs).

userStories.title: Grading never runs the tag-OCR ground-truth pass — the brand and size on a certificate are seller-typed, not read off the label
userStories.description: As a buyer trusting a GradeThread certificate, I want the brand, size, style code and fiber content on it to have been READ off the garment's own label, so that the certificate identifies the item rather than repeating what the seller claimed. Verified today: lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts exists and does exactly this job (a focused vision pass over ONLY the tag photos returning brand/size/fiber_content/style_code/rn_number verbatim with per-field confidence), but its only callers are lib/ai-listing.ts and lib/ai-size-estimate.ts — both FlipDesk AutoLister paths. The grading pipeline never imports it. Grading's own label handling is one line of the per-image prompt (ai-grading.ts:274) that transcribes fiber_content for the fabric-criteria block and nothing else; brand reaches the composite prompt only via ai-grading.ts:1589 as sanitized, fenced, explicitly-untrusted seller text. So the two halves of the same product read the same photograph to completely different depths, and the half that prints a public certificate is the shallow one.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline runs extractTagGroundTruth over the submission's label/label_2 images and persists the result (brand, size, fiber_content, style_code, rn_number, each with its confidence) on the submission or grade report.

Read fields enter the composite prompt as TRUSTED server-generated context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence; the seller's own typed brand/title stays inside the fence, and a test asserts the two channels are never merged.
The composite prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, with a distinct version suffix so accuracy-tracking can attribute the tag-grounded era.
A read below TAG_GROUND_TRUTH_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.4) is discarded rather than shown — an illegible tag must not produce a confident identity.
A read that CONTRADICTS the seller-declared brand or size is surfaced (report field or review flag) rather than silently overwritten in either direction.
Tag-OCR adds a vision call per grade: it is metered through the existing ai-usage/ai-budget path and gated so it cannot run on submissions with no label photo.
Disabled (flag off or no label photo) the composite prompt is byte-identical to today, test-guarded.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). THE HEADLINE FINDING of the review: the AutoLister reads a garment tag far more carefully than the certificate does. lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts is a finished, tested, metered module (249 lines, ai-tag-ocr_test.ts green) and grading does not call it. Highest value-per-unit-of-work item in the epic because the code already exists — this is wiring plus a prompt-version cycle, not new capability. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (flag-gated OFF, awaiting eval). Commit 5b4ea22. AC1 DONE: processSubmission runs extractTagGroundTruth over label/label_2 photos INSIDE the existing withImageBufferSlot closure, in parallel with the per-image pass, over base64 that is ALREADY RESIDENT — one extra vision call, zero extra downloads, no change to the memory gate that bounds grading concurrency. Persisted to new grade_reports.tag_read (migration 00496, nullable jsonb). AC2 DONE: new lib/tag-ground-truth.ts renders the read as TRUSTED context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence alongside baseline/fabric; seller text stays inside; two tests pin it, including one where a hostile title mimics the trusted block's own header and still lands inside the fence. AC3 PARTIAL BY DESIGN: the +tag prompt-version suffix and the composite-prompt wiring are in, but the feature is gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR (default OFF) exactly as US-1533 gated baselines — shadow/eval/canary REQUIRE live vision calls and cannot run in this sandbox, so activation stays a deliberate operator step. AC4 DONE (0.4 bar, tested at/below/above). AC5 DONE: a brand disagreement is REPORTED not resolved — neither value overwrites the other; formatting-only differences (Levi's/LEVIS/levi s) are deliberately not mismatches; emits grading.tag_discrepancy + a warn log. AC6 DONE: own recordAiUsage feature row 'tag_ocr' so the added cost is measurable on its own rather than buried in per_image; gated on the flag AND on a label photo existing. AC7 DONE: empty block => composite prompt byte-identical, asserted three ways including a full-string equality on the only-difference-is-the-block property. THREE THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) The grade_reports insert uses a CONDITIONAL SPREAD, not tag_read: tagRead — a null-VALUED key still NAMES the column in the PostgREST payload and would 42703 the whole insert, and with it the paid grade, anywhere 00496 has not been applied. That spread is what makes the commit safe to deploy ahead of the SQL; do not 'simplify' it. (2) KNOWN COST EDGE, accepted: the read runs before the image-quality gate (same as the authenticity add-on), so a submission that later abstains on an illegible label has already paid for it. Sequencing the gate first would serialize the hot path on every grade to save a call on the abstaining minority — the same trade fabric-criteria.ts already documents. (3) The escalation path forwards the SAME tag block and does NOT re-read the tag: a verbatim transcription does not get truer on a bigger model. ALSO: extractTagGroundTruth now accepts data URIs as well as URLs (tagImageSource), which is what let grading reuse resident bytes; the FlipDesk URL callers are unchanged. tag_read is deliberately NOT in the public certificate allowlist (content-public.ts CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS) — publishing a machine read of someone's tag as certified identity is a product call that waits for eval numbers. New vault note vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md records the trusted/untrusted channel contract and the test for which channel a NEW block belongs to (who can influence its content, not whether it is accurate). VERIFICATION: 4540 edge tests pass, 16 new in tag-ground-truth_test.ts; the 8 failures in this sandbox are imagescript-FFI and network-timeout artifacts of substituted deps (deno.land/esm.sh are blocked here) and fail IDENTICALLY on a stashed clean tree — confirmed, not assumed. deno lint clean; deno check reports zero errors in the changed files. verify:db and verify:security not run (no Docker); web lane not applicable (zero frontend files changed, node_modules absent).

userStories.title: 23 route groups touching multi-tenant tables have no tenant-isolation test case; /api/account is the priority
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the US-268 per-route test rule to actually hold. tenant-isolation_test.ts is strong — 118 cases making real HTTP foreign-tenant probes — but these mounts have ZERO coverage: /api/account (reaches submissions, grade_reports, inventory_items, listings, sales, item_photos, sources — it both exports AND deletes), /api/flipdesk/images, /api/flipdesk/equity, /api/flipdesk/scout, /api/flipdesk/shopify, /api/flipdesk/depop, /api/flipdesk/google, /api/guarantee, /api/drip, /api/webhooks, plus 13 /api/admin/* groups.
acceptanceCriteria: Add cases for the ordinary seller routes first: /api/account (highest — seven multi-tenant tables), then /api/flipdesk/images and /api/flipdesk/equity.
Treat the /api/admin/* groups as lower priority and document why: adminAuthMiddleware covers them at main.ts:730-731, so they are authorization-gated by design rather than tenant-gated.

ALSO from the same audit — invert the auth allowlist for /api/flipdesk/ebay. main.ts:401-543 enumerates ~90 individual paths while other modules use a /* wildcard. All 108 currently-unmatched paths were hand-verified as legitimately public or self-authenticating (OAuth callbacks, requireJobSecret crons, signature-verified webhooks, HMAC extension routes), so there is NO live gap — but adding one route to the 7600-line flipdesk-ebay.ts with a path outside the allowlist ships it UNAUTHENTICATED with no test failure. Use a /* wildcard with an explicit skip-list.
Add a rate limiter to /api/support/assistant/* (an LLM route with none) for consistency with every other AI surface.
userStories.notes: [P2][Security/Testing] Found 2026-07-18 by the security deep dive. CRITICAL CONTEXT so this is not misread as a breach: the audit traced all 740 .from() call sites on multi-tenant tables, taint-traced request-supplied ids into filters, and machine-diffed every mounted route against the middleware tables — and could NOT confirm a single cross-tenant data hole. Every unscoped-LOOKING query hand-verified as parent-verified (inventory_items!inner(user_id), loadListingOwned, loadReconcilePair, or a locally-minted id). The US-268 discipline is genuinely being followed. This story closes the TEST gap and inverts a default that currently makes unauthenticated exposure a silent one-line mistake. | 2026-07-18 THREE OF FOUR ACs (agent loop). AC4 DONE: /api/support/assistant/* now carries rateLimiter(20/min) — it was the only AI surface with none. Not an open faucet before (support-assistant.ts calls loadGateAndDecide before any token spend) but every other AI route is limited, and defence-in-depth belongs on the path where a loop costs money per iteration. AC1 PARTIAL, and the probe SHAPE had to change: /api/account/export and /delete take NO resource id — they act on the caller — so assertDenied is meaningless for them and there is nothing to point at tenant A. The property that a leak would actually trip is CONTAINMENT, so the new case asserts B's own export (200, must succeed) contains NONE of A's seeded ids across the seven tables it reads. Uses EXISTING required fixture ids, so it runs in CI immediately rather than waiting on a seed change. Also added an env-gated remove-bg probe (that route writes to the PUBLIC item-photos bucket, so a cross-tenant call would publish another seller's photo) — deliberately NOT added to REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS, because a case that hard-fails CI before the seed script provides TEST_USER_A_PHOTO_ID would simply get muted, which is worse than skipping loudly. Plus an unauthenticated-read probe on equity. ⚠ /api/account/delete is deliberately NOT probed and I want that recorded rather than looking like an oversight: the only cross-tenant shape is 'can B redirect the delete at A', and every way of asking risks destroying a fixture account if the answer is ever wrong — a test whose failure mode is data loss is not worth its signal. The route reads only c.get('userId') and accepts no target id; that is the property to preserve in review. AC2 DONE (documented: /api/admin/* is authorization-gated by adminAuthMiddleware at main.ts:730-731, so it is lower priority by design, not by neglect). AC3 — I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO WHAT THE AC ASKED, and this is the judgement call to review. The AC says invert to app.use('/api/flipdesk/ebay/*', authMiddleware) + skip-list. I first VERIFIED the premise myself rather than trusting the audit: of 81 declared eBay routes, exactly 6 fall outside the 33 allowlist patterns, and I read every one — 5 are requireJobSecret crons, 1 is the OAuth callback verified by its single-use state token. So there is NO live gap, confirming the audit independently. The inversion is probably the right end state, but it re-wires auth for 81 live routes including OAuth returns and five Coolify crons, and it CANNOT be verified from here: a wrong skip-list 401s every cron and the eBay OAuth return in production, silently, until someone tries to reconnect an account. So I shipped the property the inversion exists FOR, at zero deployment risk: ebay-auth-coverage_test.ts fails the build if any eBay route is neither auth-covered nor listed in SELF_AUTHENTICATING with its mechanism NAMED. A second test re-verifies each exemption against the handler, so an exemption that stops being true (mechanism removed) also fails — a stale exemption is a documented promise the code no longer keeps. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by injecting an unauthenticated GET /secret-seller-report: the guard names it and fails; removing it passes. The middleware inversion remains worth doing BEHIND A STAGING DEPLOY — it is not worth doing blind, and it is now safe to defer because the silent-exposure path is closed. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4169 edge tests pass. STILL passes:false: the new tenant cases only prove themselves when the tenant-isolation workflow runs with its two-tenant fixture (they skip locally by design), and AC3's inversion is deferred rather than done. | 2026-08-03 AC1 ADVANCED — the two route groups AC1 names after /api/account. No migration. /api/flipdesk/images: the group has one MUTATING route (/archive) and it is the one worth a case — it moves photos to R2 and REWRITES photo_url to an unauthenticated public URL, so a cross-tenant reach would republish As images at a new address and delete the Supabase originals. Like /export it takes no resource id (eligibility comes from .eq(inventory_items.user_id, userId) on the join), so assertDenied is meaningless and CONTAINMENT is the property: Bs own archive run must never mention a photo of As. Asserted on the RESPONSE BODY rather than the status, because the failure being guarded returns 200 — a scoping bug archives As photos and reports a healthy count. /api/flipdesk/equity: the existing case pinned only that the route is authenticated, with a stated reason that a containment check needs seeded values. It does not. TWO stronger properties, both fixture-light: (1) DIRECT CONTAINMENT — the payload carries items with per-item ids, so As item id appearing in Bs aggregate names the leak outright; (2) A and B must not receive byte-identical equity, which is the signature of a dropped user_id scope (every caller aggregating the whole platform, returned as a healthy 200). Guarded against a false alarm: two tenants legitimately match when both are empty, so the inequality only bites when a side is non-zero — silent on a bare fixture rather than flaky, which is the trade that keeps a probe alive. ⚠ MY FIRST VERSION OF THE EQUITY PROBE WAS VACUOUS and I caught it by checking the payload shape instead of trusting the field name: GET /equity/ returns computeEquityForOwner, whose field is totalEquityCents, while total_equity_cents exists only on the /trend snapshot rows. Matching snake_case alone meant the parse always returned 0, both sides looked empty, and the case exited before its assertion EVERY time. A probe that never reaches its assertion is precisely the failure this suite exists to catch, written into the suite itself. It now matches both spellings AND fails if neither key is present, because a payload-shape change must not read as an empty tenant. REMAINING: AC2 (document why the admin groups are lower priority) and AC3 (invert the /api/flipdesk/ebay auth allowlist, deferred as needing a staging deploy) are unchanged. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5410 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1347 files.

userStories.title: Counsel review gate + jurisdiction matrix for subscription disclosure and cancellation
userStories.description: This batch of stories encodes engineering work against auto-renewal law, but the copy, the consent wording and the retention period are legal determinations, not engineering ones. We also do not currently know which state regimes we are exposed to — we sell nationally through Stripe with no state-based logic anywhere, so the strictest applicable state law effectively governs every customer. Before any user-facing disclosure copy ships, it needs review, and the team needs a written answer on which jurisdictions we are designing for.
acceptanceCriteria: Obtain counsel review of: point-of-sale disclosure copy, the affirmative-consent wording and mechanism, the cancellation flow, the renewal-reminder cadence, and the consent-record retention period.

Produce a jurisdiction matrix: which state ARLs we are treating as in scope, and whether we design to a single strictest standard (recommended, given no state-based logic exists) or vary by billing address.

Get a written determination on whether our 14-day no-card trial is an 'automatic renewal or continuous service offer' under California AB 2863 — it expanded the definitions to cover free trials, and our trial lapses to Free rather than charging, which may or may not take it out of scope.
Record the outcome in a vault note under vault/50-business/ and link it from the pricing and legal notes.

Confirm the retention period for consent records (California requires verification of affirmative consent kept 3 years, or 1 year after termination, whichever is longer) before the retention story is implemented.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Legal] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the gate story: the P0 engineering work below can start, but no copy goes live without this. Do not let an agent invent legal language.

userStories.title: No auto-renewal disclosure exists on ANY web purchase surface
userStories.description: Audit finding, verified by exhaustive search of src/: the strings 'auto-renew', 'automatically renews', 'recurring', and 'until you cancel' appear ZERO times in any user-facing purchase surface. The only renewal-adjacent copy at a point of sale is the price unit ('/mo', '/yr') and a single phrase — 'Switch or cancel any time.' — in src/components/billing/flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx:111. Correct auto-renewal language exists ONLY in the legal pages (src/pages/legal/terms.tsx:69-71 'renew automatically until cancelled'; refund.tsx:22-24), which is precisely where it does not satisfy a clear-and-conspicuous, same-screen requirement. The weakest surface is the 402 paywall (src/components/billing/upgrade-required-dialog.tsx), which carries no cancellation or renewal language at all and is the surface users hit under friction, blocked mid-action.
acceptanceCriteria: Render a clear and conspicuous auto-renewal disclosure adjacent to the purchase CTA — visually, not behind a tooltip, modal, accordion or link — on ALL FOUR surfaces: the pricing page plan cards (src/pages/marketing/pricing.tsx), the plan picker (flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx), the 402 paywall (upgrade-required-dialog.tsx), and buyer billing (src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx:147-220).

The disclosure must state, in the user's own view: that the subscription continues until the user cancels; the recurring amount; the billing frequency in words (not just a '/mo' unit label); the date of the first charge and/or the renewal date; and how to cancel.
Build it as ONE shared component so the four surfaces cannot drift, and so a new purchase surface inherits it by default.
Add a test that fails if any component calling the subscribe mutation does not render the disclosure component.
Copy must come from the counsel review gate, not be drafted by an agent.

userStories.title: No affirmative consent to recurring billing is captured or retained at purchase
userStories.description: There is no checkbox, no separate consent step, and no consent artifact of any kind for the recurring charge — verified across payments.ts, billing.tsx and pricing.tsx (zero hits). Stripe's consent_collection parameter is not used on the Checkout Session (services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:395-422, 542-554), and no custom_text is set. A real consent system already exists but is scoped to signup only: legal_acceptances (00142_legal_acceptance.sql:39-49) captures tos_version, privacy_version, method, user_agent, ip_address, accepted_at — and its method enum (signup_clickwrap | oauth_clickwrap | reacceptance) has no purchase-time value. It is never written at subscribe time. Separately, the highest-volume path is the weakest evidence: the signup trigger insert (:121-126) omits ip_address and user_agent entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture express affirmative consent to the recurring charge at purchase, separate from and in addition to general ToS acceptance.
Record a durable consent artifact at subscribe time: user, timestamp, IP, user-agent, the plan/interval/amount consented to, and the version of the disclosure copy shown.

Extend the legal_acceptances method enum with a purchase-time value, or add a purpose-built table — reuse the existing versioning machinery (lib/legal-versions.ts) rather than inventing a second system.
Backfill ip_address and user_agent on the signup clickwrap path (00142:121-126).
Retain consent records per the period set by the counsel review gate (California: 3 years, or 1 year post-termination, whichever is longer) and ensure no data-retention job prunes them earlier.
Cover the iOS/App Store and future Google Play purchase paths too — consent there is collected by the platform, so record which platform captured it and when, rather than duplicating it.

LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Express informed consent plus retained proof is the core of both ROSCA and the California ARL. Today we could not demonstrate what any subscriber agreed to. Depends on the terms-snapshot story for the 'what was shown' half. | 2026-07-19 INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — and the scoping matters, so here is what the next pass needs. THIS STORY IS GENUINELY MORE COUNSEL-GATED THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS. US-2117, US-2119, US-2120 and US-2125 all turned out to be mechanism (I was wrong to call them gated, four times). This one is not the same: US-2114's AC1 explicitly puts 'the affirmative-consent WORDING AND MECHANISM' under review, so AC1 here is squarely gated, and AC5's retention period is gated by US-2114 AC5 by name. AC4 IS NOT GATED, and I traced it to a precise conclusion. THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS: POST /api/legal/accept (routes/legal.ts:109) records ip_address via clientIp(c) and user_agent from the request header, SERVER-SIDE, and it already accepts method='signup_clickwrap' in its allowlist. So nothing needs building — the strong-evidence path is there and is used today by the legal GATE (oauth_clickwrap / reacceptance). The gap is only that the EMAIL-signup path never calls it: handle_new_user's trigger (00142:121-126) writes the signup_clickwrap row itself, inside Postgres, where it has no request context — hence no IP, no user-agent. That is exactly why the highest-volume path carries the weakest evidence. ⚠ THE TRAP, and the reason I did not just 'fix' it: the obvious shortcut is to pass ip/user_agent through signUp()'s options.data so the trigger can read them. DO NOT. Those would be CLIENT-SUPPLIED and trivially forged, and a forged IP in a consent record is worse than an absent one — it looks authoritative in exactly the setting where the record's only value is that it can be trusted. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement and US-2119's refusal to send a dateless notice. THE ACTUAL SEAM, for whoever picks this up: email signup defers the session until confirmation (emailRedirectTo), so /api/legal/accept — which requires auth — cannot be called at signUp() time. The right hook is the FIRST AUTHENTICATED SESSION, in use-auth.ts's onAuthStateChange SIGNED_IN branch, which already runs exactly this shape of one-shot post-signup work (redeemStoredAffiliateRef, sendWelcomeEmailOnce gated on a user_metadata flag). Call /api/legal/accept with method='signup_clickwrap' there. ONE DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST: legal_acceptances is an append-only audit table, so this produces TWO rows for one signup — the trigger's (guaranteed, weak) and the endpoint's (best-effort, strong). I think that is the RIGHT outcome rather than a defect: you always have a record, and usually a provable one. But it should be a decision, and the endpoint needs an idempotency guard so a repeated SIGNED_IN does not append a third. AC6 is also unblocked and unstarted: recording WHICH PLATFORM captured consent for IAP/Play purchases (where the platform collects it) rather than duplicating it — subscription_agreements.source (US-2117, migration 00486) already has the appstore/google_play values for exactly this. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC6 DONE. Both platform purchase paths now record WHICH PLATFORM captured the consent — appstore verify and the Play RTDN reverify each write a subscription_agreements row via recordPlatformAgreement. This became cheap only because two other pieces landed first: US-2117's table (with the appstore/google_play values already in its source CHECK) and US-2124's platform-event work that made me read these routes. THE HONESTY CONSTRAINT IS THE DESIGN, and it is what AC6 actually asks for: Apple and Google COLLECT AND STORE the affirmative agreement natively, so duplicating it would be dishonest — we did not take that consent and cannot attest to its wording. The row therefore records THAT the platform took it, not a claim that we did. Concretely: amount_cents is 0 with an in-place comment saying it is NOT a real price, because the platform owns and localises the amount and inventing a figure would be the same error US-2117 refuses on the Stripe path — a partial record that reads as fact. A test asserts BOTH the zero and its explanation, because an unexplained 0 will eventually be read as 'this user agreed to pay nothing'. stripe_subscription_id is namespaced as <source>:<external_id> so an Apple transaction id cannot collide with a Stripe subscription id in the uniqueness index, and a 23505 is swallowed — a replayed IAP verify or a repeated RTDN must not report a failure, since the index firing IS the idempotency working. A test pins that both paths call it, so the gap cannot reopen on one platform while looking closed on the other. WHAT THIS CHANGES IN PRACTICE: before, 'what did this user agree to?' was answerable for a Stripe subscriber and unanswerable for an IAP or Play one — the two populations had different evidentiary standing for the same product. STILL OPEN and correctly gated: AC1 (express affirmative consent at web purchase) and AC5 (retention period) are US-2114 counsel items; AC4 (server-side IP/UA on the signup clickwrap) is scoped above with its trap named — the mechanism already exists in /api/legal/accept, the seam is the first authenticated session, and passing a CLIENT-SUPPLIED ip through signUp() would be worse than the current absence. Verified: edge 4319 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: No record of what price or terms any user actually agreed to — pricing_plans is mutated in place
userStories.description: The users table stores flipdesk_plan and flipdesk_interval but NO amount column; price is resolved live on every read via getFlipdeskPriceIds() against pricing_plans. pricing_plans (00166:69-80) is mutated in place with only an updated_at trigger — no history table, no versioning. flipdesk_subscription_events records from_plan/to_plan and the raw payload but, per the note already in 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:20, not even the billing interval. Combined, there is no way to reconstruct what price any user was shown or agreed to on any past date. If a price changes, the historical record changes with it.
acceptanceCriteria: Snapshot the agreed terms onto the subscription record at purchase: amount, currency, interval, plan, trial terms, and the disclosure-copy version — immutable once written.
Version pricing_plans (history table or append-only revisions) so a past price is reconstructable.
Record the billing interval on flipdesk_subscription_events.
Make cancellation_reason append-only per-event rather than a single mutable text column overwritten on each cancel.
Follow the migrations skill: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in the same commit, self-record footer.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Data] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the evidentiary half of the consent story — consent to WHAT is unanswerable without it. Also unblocks honest revenue reporting. | 2026-07-19 ALL FOUR SCHEMA ACs DONE (migration 00486) + the write path. ⚠ I FIRST ASSERTED THIS WHOLE COMPLIANCE BATCH WAS GATED ON US-2114 (counsel) AND THAT WAS WRONG — recording it because the error was mine and would have left a P0 sitting untouched. US-2114 gates what the disclosure copy SAYS; this story is about whether we can still PROVE what it said. Those are different questions, and only the first needs a lawyer. Testing the assertion instead of repeating it is what surfaced the work. AC1 subscription_agreements — immutable snapshot at purchase (plan, interval, amount, currency, trial terms, disclosure_version pointer). IMMUTABILITY IS TRIGGER-ENFORCED, not merely intended: UPDATE and DELETE both RAISE. A comment asking people not to edit a compliance record is not a control, and this table's entire value is that its contents cannot drift. disclosure_version is nullable because the copy versioning (US-2114/US-2115) has not landed — recording the POINTER now means no second migration later. AC2 pricing_plan_revisions — append-only history written BY TRIGGER on pricing_plans, deliberately not by the application: a history table that depends on the writer remembering is a history table with gaps. Stores a full jsonb row snapshot too, so a column added to pricing_plans later is captured historically without another migration here. Seeded with current rows as revision zero so the history has a floor rather than implying prices did not exist before today. AC3 flipdesk_subscription_events.billing_interval — the gap 00215's OWN comment recorded; from_plan/to_plan alone cannot distinguish a monthly→yearly switch from a no-op. AC4 subscription_cancellations — append-only; users.cancellation_reason was a single mutable column each cancel overwrote, so a repeat canceller left one reason and no trace it happened twice. Backfilled from that column (timestamped updated_at, the best available approximation — the true cancel time was never recorded, which IS the defect) and the old column is KEPT since readers still use it. WRITE PATH: lib/agreed-terms.ts, pure extraction + a thin IO half, wired into handleSubscriptionChange — chosen over checkout.session because the subscription object carries what Stripe ACTUALLY applied (amount, interval, trial) whereas checkout carries what was requested. THE DESIGN POINT WORTH REVIEWING: it DECLINES TO WRITE rather than writing a partial row when the subscription cannot support a truthful record (no price, no unit_amount, or an interval we do not sell — Stripe also emits day/week). A compliance record containing a plausible guess is worse than a visible gap, because it will be read as fact. The refusal is reported, so the gap is not silent. Best-effort throughout: a compliance record must never be why a paying customer fails to get entitlement. Idempotent via a unique index, so a webhook redelivery cannot mint a second agreement for one purchase. 9 tests. The one that matters most: a MISSING amount must yield NO record while a REAL zero is kept — 0 is a legitimate agreed price (comped/fully-discounted), so defaulting absence to 0 would be indistinguishable from a genuine free agreement on the record. Negative-verified by making absence default to 0; that test goes red. ⚠ THE RLS GUARD CAUGHT MY OWN TABLES, which is the system working: three new tables with owner columns, RLS enabled and no policies is exactly the case US-2008's widened guard exists to catch, and the full suite went red until I classified them. All three are now in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY with the reasoning — they are evidentiary, read only by admin/support tooling, and the failure mode of a permissive policy (a user reading, or influencing, the record of what they agreed to) is precisely what they exist to rule out. STILL OPEN: nothing schema-side. What remains is US-2114's counsel review before any disclosure COPY ships, and wiring disclosure_version once that copy is versioned. Migration 00486 is HELD (7th) — see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md for the two backfills and the deploy-order note. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00215, 00486) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping.

userStories.title: Authenticity prompt activation must fail closed — the eval gate has never run
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-authenticity.ts (530 lines) is LIVE with three callers: the paid grading add-on (grading-pipeline.ts:1239), the buyer credit-metered check (routes/buyer-authenticity.ts:53), and an UNAUTHENTICATED public endpoint (routes/public-grading.ts:998). Results surface on public certificates. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts (268 lines) — the accuracy gate — has zero non-self callers. Its own header states: '⚠ THIS GATE DOES NOT RUN... Do not read this module's green tests as evidence the gate exists.' So an authenticity prompt version can ship today with no accuracy bar at all. The condition-grading engine has exactly this gate and enforces it; authenticity was built to the same design and never wired.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path, mirroring how the grading engine gates prompt versions (shadow -> eval gate -> canary).
Activation must FAIL CLOSED: an authenticity prompt version that has not passed the gate cannot be activated, and if no golden set exists yet, activation is blocked rather than defaulted open.
Add the admin route/surface needed to run the eval and view results.
Emit a startup or health warning while any live authenticity prompt version is ungated, so this cannot silently regress again.
Test that activation is refused when the gate has not passed, and that the refusal is visible rather than silent.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Safety][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. This is the single most urgent item in the epic: we are already making authenticity claims in production with no accuracy bar, including on an unauthenticated public endpoint. Same risk class as the FTC Section 5 substantiation work (US-2114..2128). Load the grading-engine skill first — it owns the prompt-version lifecycle this must mirror. Related: US-1996 tracks the backlog-integrity side of the same gap. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: shipped authenticityGateStatus + gateStatusFromRun (pure, fail-closed on BOTH no-run and query-error) + assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (the fail-closed guard a future activation path must call) + warnAuthenticityGate wired into main.ts as backgrounded non-throwing boot work (NOT a boot guard — US-778 crash-loop precedent). Model is part of the gate key, mirroring US-2036. Guard test extended: accepts either runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable, and now pins the boot check. 4348 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: (a) no authenticity prompt-ACTIVATION path exists to block — authenticity prompts are code constants, not ai_prompt_versions rows; building that lifecycle needs a migration and was deliberately NOT invented here (see the reasoning in authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, which argues against speculative lifecycles); (b) the gate will report ungated for every version until US-2131 seeds real labeled cases. Next: admin route to RUN the eval. ITER2 2026-07-19: added GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/gate (reports whether each live version has a passing run on the serving model; all_gated headline) and POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/eval (step-up gated — costs one vision call per case; surfaces the empty-golden-set case as a 400 setup state, not a 500). Reused the existing admin group so guards/audit are inherited. authenticity_eval_* already carry admin RLS policies, so no rls-guard registration needed. 4348 edge tests pass. | 2026-08-02 VERIFICATION — THE WORK SHIPPED AND THE RECORD NEVER SAID SO. This is a P0 safety story whose notes contained nothing but the founding audit, so anyone reading the backlog would conclude the authenticity gate is entirely unbuilt. It is not: commit 0e5afb89 "US-2130: make the authenticity eval gate runnable and its absence visible" landed it, and the note was written onto US-1996 instead. I walked all five ACs against the code. AC2 MET — assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (lib/authenticity-eval.ts:291) calls authenticityGateStatus and returns {ok:false} unless gated, so it REFUSES BY DEFAULT; with no golden set the status is not gated and activation is blocked rather than defaulted open, which is exactly what the AC asks. AC3 MET — an admin route runs the eval against a chosen prompt version, defaulting to AUTHENTICITY_PROMPT_VERSION_GROUNDED because that is what the live pass uses when brand tells are available, and it writes an audit log with the version, model and pass/fail. AC4 MET — warnAuthenticityGate() logs "[BOOT] authenticity: prompt X is serving UNGATED" for each live version, and it IS called, at main.ts:1685. It is deliberately best-effort and non-throwing, and the reason is recorded in its own header: a boot guard that can fail is how the schema-version check once crash-looped the whole edge service (US-778). AC5 MET — authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, and it asserts the boot call itself (/warnAuthenticityGate\(\)/ against main.ts), not just the function's existence. AC1 IS MET BY A DIFFERENT MECHANISM THAN IT NAMES, and the substitution is the interesting part. The AC says "wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path". THERE IS NO SUCH PATH: authenticity prompts are code constants, not rows in ai_prompt_versions. The previous pass declined to invent an activation lifecycle to satisfy the wording, and said why in the code — inventing a flow to satisfy a checkbox is how authenticity-eval.ts became dead code in the first place. Instead it shipped the property the AC exists FOR: a source-scan test that FAILS THE BUILD if an authenticity prompt-activation path ever appears without calling runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable. That is arguably stronger than the literal wiring, because it cannot be forgotten by omission — the wiring protects one call site that exists, the guard protects every call site that does not exist yet. RECOMMENDATION: close on all five, and let the fact that the gate has never actually RUN sit where it belongs — that is a golden-set problem (US-2131 built the curation surface for exactly this) and not a defect in the gate. I am not closing a P0 safety story myself on a substituted AC; the substitution is defensible and documented, but it is the owner's call whether "no activation path exists, and a guard fails the build if one appears" satisfies "wire it into the activation path". WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND WORTH NOT LOSING: the epic's framing stands — the scaffolding is built and the evidence base is not. The gate is runnable, visible and fail-closed; it has no golden set to run against, so nothing has been certified. That is the honest state, and it is a much better state than the notes implied.

userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Data][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction).
