Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy. So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (in my own iteration-4 work): withdrawAssessment cleared only verdict/verdict_confidence, but the PUBLIC certificate view (00172, carried through 00307) does NOT read verdict — it derives what a buyer sees from authenticity_confidence (-> confidence band), counterfeit_risk (-> risk label) and summary (rendered verbatim). So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Also confirmed: the edge-SSR cert page renders no authenticity at all (SPA-only), and authenticity_checked in the public view derives from image_authenticity (PHOTO-EDIT, 00061), which is a different signal from the brand add-on and must not be conflated. 4412 edge tests pass. SELLER ROUTE 2026-07-19: POST /api/grade/authenticity-appeal shipped, implementing the approved §1a/§1b decisions. Files as disputes.kind=authenticity (00489) rather than a parallel table. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). Rate limited to 5 open appeals per seller, which exists BECAUSE hiding is free otherwise: unlimited appeals would suppress every verdict indefinitely at no cost. CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the first version called the reseal before the update landed, so it would have hashed the OLD verdict and written a signature verifying against nothing — resealAfterAuthenticityChange now takes the NEXT assessment explicitly, which makes that mistake impossible rather than merely fixed. If hiding fails the appeal is still recorded (better a visible verdict with a filed appeal than a silent appeal nobody actions). 4431 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: the admin resolve route, seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (needs the SLA number + counsel). ADMIN RESOLVE 2026-07-19: GET /authenticity/appeals (open queue, OLDEST FIRST — while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty) + POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve. Step-up gated: upholding withdraws a published verdict and reseals a certificate, rejecting republishes one. Upheld -> withdrawAssessment (permanent, clears every publicly-projected field); rejected -> restoreAssessmentAfterAppeal (exactly what was hidden, since the reviewer finding the appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item). Both reseal with the NEXT assessment. An upheld appeal also records an authentic reviewer verdict through the US-2140 path, because a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE is the most valuable label available and the error direction nothing else measures — the model_verdict snapshot reads from appeal_hidden_original, since the live field was nulled when the appeal was filed. Already-resolved appeals 409 rather than double-applying. 4431 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (SLA number + counsel). | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172, 00307, 00489) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. NOTIFICATION 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-notify.ts, fired from the pipeline at finalize. Implements the approved §1a decision — red_flags ONLY, never on inconclusive (not a finding; telling a seller invites appeals against nothing) and never on likely_authentic. SLA of 5 business days is stated in the notice, per the decision: an appeal with no stated turnaround cannot be planned around, and while it is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade. COPY IS DELIBERATELY NON-ACCUSATORY and tested to stay that way — it says the check flagged details it COULD NOT CONFIRM, calls itself an automated photo estimate and not a determination, and a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake never appear, because the pass has no measured error rate and must not assert what it cannot support. Rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a type the users notification preferences do not know about, which would have made it unsuppressable. Best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. ⚠ COPY STILL NEEDS COUNSEL REVIEW under US-2133 — flagged in the module header; it should be reviewed alongside the certificate copy, not separately. 4453 edge tests pass (+22). | 2026-08-02 THE APPEAL PIPELINE IS BUILT AT BOTH ENDS AND HAS NO SELLER-FACING BUTTON. Verified by grep, not inferred. The SELLER endpoint exists and is complete: POST /authenticity-appeal at routes/grade.ts:1301 — it verifies the caller owns the submission, 422s when the grade has no authenticity assessment to contest, and rate-limits deliberately (the comment says why: hiding the verdict while an appeal is open means an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict indefinitely — that is a well-reasoned control, not boilerplate). The ADMIN side exists too: GET /authenticity/appeals is the open queue oldest-first and POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve closes them, and the queue's ordering carries its own reasoning (while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty). AND NOTHING IN src/ CALLS THE SELLER ENDPOINT. A grep for "authenticity-appeal" across every .ts and .tsx under src returns ZERO hits. So an operator opening the appeals queue sees a list that can only ever be empty, and a seller whose genuine item was flagged still has exactly what the story title says: no way to contest it. THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS SESSION KEPT FINDING, and it is the third instance today — the waitlist backend with no public capture form, the grade-card switch writing columns nothing read, and now this. Each time the expensive half was built and the cheap half was not, and each time the missing half is the one a USER touches. Worth naming explicitly on a story about a seller being unable to defend a genuine item: the backend being done makes this look further along than it is, and anyone reading the route file would conclude the feature ships. WHAT REMAINS FOR AC1 is therefore smaller than the AC implies but not trivial: the surfaces where a seller SEES the verdict (the certificate view and the submission detail) need a contest action that POSTs to the existing endpoint, plus the open-appeal state AC2 asks about — and AC2 is a real design question, not wiring, because the passport is append-only so a withdrawal is a superseding entry rather than an edit. AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published) is also still open and is arguably prior to AC1: they cannot contest what they were never told about. AC6 needs counsel. I did not build the UI — the certificate and passport display rules in AC2 have to be settled first, and shipping a contest button before deciding what the certificate shows while an appeal is open would put a seller in a state nobody has defined. | 2026-08-02 AC1 AND AC2 DONE — the seller can now contest a verdict. MY EARLIER BLOCKER DISSOLVED ON INSPECTION, and that is worth recording because I nearly left this unbuilt on it: I said AC2 (what the certificate shows while an appeal is open) had to be settled first. It already was, server-side, and I had not read far enough. hideAssessmentForAppeal (lib/authenticity-appeal.ts:106) NULLS verdict, verdict_confidence, authenticity_confidence, counterfeit_risk and summary, sets under_appeal + appeal_opened_at, and stashes the original in appeal_hidden_original — guarded against stashing a stash on a second appeal, which would make the original unrecoverable. The endpoint then RESEALS (AC4) because integrity v4 covers the verdict, and its own comment explains why the reseal passes the HIDDEN assessment rather than the stored one. So AC2 and AC4 were shipped; only the button was missing. SHIPPED: NEW src/components/grade/authenticity-appeal-dialog.tsx and a "This is genuine — contest this result" action on submission-detail.tsx, the surface where the seller actually sees the verdict. THREE DETAILS THAT ARE NOT DECORATION. (1) The page now renders an UNDER-REVIEW card when under_appeal is set, instead of the normal card. Without it the seller sees a row of blanks where the verdict was — which reads as a bug, and is worse than not shipping the button at all, because it makes them think their appeal broke something. (2) The dialog is mounted at the PAGE root, not inside the authenticity card, so it is not unmounted the instant the card swaps to its under-review state on a successful file. (3) MIN_REASON = 20 mirrors the server's validateAppeal floor deliberately, and the client copy spends it telling the seller what a reviewer needs before they type: being rejected after writing is how someone abandons an appeal they were entitled to. The 429 path surfaces the SERVER's message rather than a generic retry, because that cap is a deliberate control (an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict) and a retry prompt would send the seller round the same loop. GUARD: NEW src/test/authenticity-appeal-wired.test.ts — something must POST to the endpoint, the dialog must be RENDERED somewhere rather than merely defined, the seller surface must handle under_appeal, and the client minimum must match the server's. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to every test that exercises the route directly, so only a scan catches it. STILL OPEN: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path), AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is PUBLISHED — arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told), AC6 (counsel, folded into US-2133). VERIFIED: full web suite 248 files / 3154 tests 0 failed, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors. | 2026-08-02 CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, and a better outcome than expected. I wrote that AC5 was "still open" and "arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told". THAT IS WRONG. AC5 IS DONE. notifyAuthenticityFlagged (lib/authenticity-notify.ts:71) is called from grading-pipeline.ts:2785, fires only on a red_flags verdict, and is best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. It had reached the same design conclusion I was about to: it rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a notification type the user's preferences do not know about — an appeal IS a dispute. Its copy is careful in a way worth preserving: "our authenticity check flagged details it could not confirm ... an automated estimate from photos, not a determination", because saying the item IS counterfeit would assert something an ungated photo-only estimate cannot support. THE FLOW IS NOW END-TO-END, which is the actual news: the notice links to /dashboard/submissions/{id}, and that is exactly the page where the contest button I added this session lives. So the loop closes — red_flags verdict fires a notification, the seller clicks through, and the button is there. Before today the notification landed on a page with nothing to do. That is the same defect one level up from the one I fixed: the notice was built, the endpoint was built, and the two were never joined. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I asserted AC5 was open from the AC text plus the absence of any UI, without grepping the pipeline for a notify call. The lesson is the one this session kept re-learning in the other direction — I checked whether the ENDPOINT had a caller and correctly found none, then failed to run the same check on the NOTIFICATION and assumed. Absence of a caller is a thing you verify, not infer, in both directions. REMAINING ON THIS STORY: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path so a withdrawal produces a reviewer verdict) and AC6 (counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133). AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5 all stand. | 2026-08-02 AC3 IS ALSO ALREADY DONE — checked rather than assumed this time, having just been wrong about AC5. POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve takes an outcome of upheld or rejected, refuses to re-resolve an already-closed appeal, and splits correctly: UPHELD withdraws the verdict permanently, REJECTED restores exactly what was hidden — with the reasoning stated inline that a reviewer finding an appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item, so the original stands rather than being re-derived. It reseals, updates the dispute status, and when plan.reviewerVerdict is set it feeds the outcome through the same review path so it counts toward accuracy and can be promoted, which is precisely what AC3 asked for. SO US-2145 STANDS AT: AC1 done (the contest button, this session — the only piece that was actually missing), AC2 done, AC3 done, AC4 done, AC5 done, AC6 outstanding and needing counsel on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133 per the AC itself. THE SHAPE OF THIS STORY IS WORTH KEEPING, because it is the clearest example of the pattern this whole session kept hitting: FIVE of six criteria were fully implemented — endpoint, hiding, reseal, reviewer path, notification — and the story read as untouched because the one missing piece was a button. Every file a reader would open to check suggested the feature shipped, and the seller still could not contest anything. The expensive halves were all built; the cheap half, the one a user touches, was not. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to any test that exercises the route directly, which is why it survived. RECOMMENDATION: close on AC1-AC5 and let AC6 travel with US-2133, or leave open pointing there — an owner call, and specifically not one I should make by writing a note that sounds like agreement on a story with a legal-review criterion.

userStories.title: DeleteReconciler has no production caller — server-side deletions never reach Android
userStories.description: As a seller, an item I delete on the web or on iOS also disappears from my Android device.
acceptanceCriteria: DeleteReconciler.reconcile is invoked from the sync path (after a drained pull), not only from DeleteReconcilerTest
Locally-created rows whose CREATE is still queued, and local-only photo captures, are protected from pruning (the protections the class already implements)
A test asserts the production call site exists, so this cannot silently regress to being uncalled again
userStories.notes: [P1][Android/Sync] Found 2026-07-27 while fixing the mutation-queue drain. Same class as US-2151 and the drain gap: DeleteReconciler is complete and unit-tested (create-before-edit protection, local-only photo protection, dirty-row protection) but grep finds NO production caller — only DeleteReconcilerTest. So a pull only ever ADDS and UPDATES rows: anything deleted on another client stays on the Android device forever, and the seller works from an inventory containing items they already got rid of. Deliberately NOT bundled into the replay fix: reconciliation PRUNES local rows, so it wants its own change with its own review rather than riding along with an unrelated one.

userStories.title: EPIC: Grading depth — identity, sizing, brand knowledge and product coverage
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the grading pipeline to identify WHAT it is grading as rigorously as it grades CONDITION, and to cover the product categories sellers actually list, because today the two halves of the product are lopsided: the condition engine is deep (5 weighted factors, defect taxonomy with mm tolerances, fabric-aware criteria, confidence caps, shadow/eval/canary lifecycle) while identity is thin (brand and size on a certificate are whatever the seller typed) and coverage is clothing-only (a hat, a tie, a belt and a handbag all have a garment_category and no way to be graded).
acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic names the exact module, table or enum it changes — no story in this epic may be closed on prose alone.
Identity work does not weaken US-346: label-read fields are server-derived and TRUSTED; seller-typed brand/size stay fenced and untrusted, and neither channel may move a factor score.
Any change to a grading prompt in this epic goes through the mandated lifecycle (new version name -> shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary), never a silent edit.

Any new rubric added by this epic keeps the three weighted-overall rounding sites in lockstep (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, admin/reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) in the same commit.
Epic closes only when its children close; it carries no implementation of its own.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Epic] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Parent for US-2210..US-2225. Scope split six ways: tag identification (2210-2212), sizing (2213-2215), brand styles/models (2216-2217), authenticity evidence + coverage priority (2218-2219), brand breadth (2220-2221), product coverage beyond clothing (2222-2225). DELIBERATELY NOT DUPLICATED: US-2130..2148 already own the visual-authenticity epic (eval gate, golden set, capture quality, decoder cross-checks, tell depth/counterfeit modelling, appeals, accuracy tracking); US-1997 owns non-clothing rubric ACTIVATION for the three rubrics that already exist (sports_cards/watches/shoes) and its Phase-2 notes already scope the factor-set generalization every new rubric here depends on; US-2107 owns publishing measurable tolerances.

userStories.title: Android is a plumbing skeleton, but its README and 19 passing stories claim near-parity
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the Android backlog to reflect reality. Android has genuinely good infrastructure — auth, a Room sync engine, mutation queue, delete reconciliation, telemetry, app-lock, CameraX capture, ~70 Kotlin files. It has no product: every navigation destination except one is a literal placeholder (ui/shell/AppShell.kt:162-175 — Home, Inventory, Money, Marketplaces, Settings, Details intake, AutoLister all render SectionPlaceholder; only capture/photos is real). Corroborating: Android calls exactly ONE edge endpoint in the entire codebase (/api/flipdesk/photo-profiles) versus iOS's 77 and web's ~530 — no grading submit, no inventory read, no eBay, no payments. Two documentation problems compound it: android/README.md:31-39 presents a package map for grading / inventory / marketplaces / money / billing whose directories contain ZERO .kt files, and :3 calls it 'at iOS parity'. And 19 stories are marked passes:true with no implementing code — verified: US-1380 Glance widgets (zero 'glance' references anywhere, no AppWidgetProvider in the manifest), US-1378 FCM push (no FirebaseMessaging reference), US-1383 Settings (routes to a placeholder), US-1384/1385/1387/1388/1389, US-1393 localization (no values-* locale dirs). The pattern is clean: US-1300-1328 (infrastructure) are genuinely done; US-1378-1396 is a contiguous block marked done without code.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-open the falsely-passing Android stories (start with the verified list: US-1380, US-1378, US-1383, US-1384, US-1385, US-1387, US-1388, US-1389, US-1393) and audit the rest of the US-1378-1396 block the same way.
Correct android/README.md — remove the 'at iOS parity' claim and the package map for directories that contain no code. This is the first document a new engineer or a diligence reviewer reads.
Re-baseline the Android estimate: real completion is closer to 29/98 than the 48/98 the backlog implies, and ALL remaining work is the expensive UI/feature half rather than a polish pass.
Decide explicitly whether Android is on the launch plan. If it is, the remaining work is essentially the whole app.
userStories.notes: [P1][Android/Backlog-integrity] Found 2026-07-18 by the cross-platform parity deep dive. This is the same class as US-1996 (archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED) but larger and on a platform nobody is looking at. The state is more misleading than a plain stub would be: sophisticated offline-sync infrastructure attached to zero features reads as 'nearly done' to anyone who opens the project and sees the hard parts solved. NOT verified: whether the 50 OPEN Android stories are correctly open — only the passing ones were falsified. | [2026-07-27] AC1 DONE: audited the whole US-1378..1396 block, not just the verified subset — 14 stories re-opened as never-implemented (1378/1379/1380/1381/1382/1384/1385/1386/1387/1388/1389/1390/1392/1393) and 2 re-opened as partial (1391 has no signing config; 1395 has no androidTest/E2E). userStories.title: In-place plan upgrade charges a prorated amount on a single click with no confirmation
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:326-380: if a user already has a subscription, clicking a higher tier calls stripe.subscriptions.update with proration_behavior: 'create_prorations' — charging immediately with NO Stripe Checkout page, no price confirmation, no interstitial and no disclosure. The click IS the purchase. Every other purchase path at least passes through Stripe's hosted checkout, which renders the recurring price; this one renders nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Show an explicit confirmation step before an in-place upgrade that states the prorated amount charged today, the new recurring amount, the new billing frequency, and the next renewal date.
Capture the same affirmative consent artifact as a new subscription.
Apply the same treatment to downgrades and interval switches if they charge or change terms.
Test asserting the upgrade mutation cannot fire without the confirmation step.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). A charge with no disclosure and no confirmation is the clearest Section 5 / ROSCA exposure in the codebase after the missing disclosures themselves. | 2026-07-19 SCOPED, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT — and the reason is the story's own logic, not capacity. AC1 needs a confirmation stating the PRORATED AMOUNT CHARGED TODAY, the new recurring amount, the new frequency and the next renewal date. Those numbers do not exist anywhere yet: payments.ts has fetchUpcomingInvoice (US-400) but that returns the CURRENT subscription's upcoming invoice, not a simulation of what a CHANGE would cost. Getting the real figure needs Stripe's proration preview — invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the PROPOSED subscription_items plus a subscription_proration_date — which is a new endpoint, and one whose output I cannot verify from this sandbox (the Stripe MCP connector is unauthorized; see US-2033, blocked the same way). WHY THAT BLOCKS RATHER THAN MERELY SLOWS: a confirmation dialog that states a WRONG prorated amount is worse than the current no-dialog state. Today the defect is an OMISSION — the click is the purchase and nothing is stated. A dialog showing an unverified number converts that into an AFFIRMATIVE MISSTATEMENT about a charge, on the exact surface this compliance batch exists to fix. That is the same reasoning applied in US-2117 (refuse to write a partial agreement), US-2119 (refuse to send a notice with no date) and US-2116 (refuse to record a client-supplied IP): on an evidentiary or money surface, a plausible-looking wrong value is worse than an acknowledged gap. WHAT THE NEXT PASS NEEDS, so it is short: (1) a preview endpoint wrapping invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the target plan's price id, returning prorated-now / new-recurring / interval / next-renewal; (2) a confirmation dialog — DowngradePreviewDialog is the established pattern to mirror, and AC3's 'apply the same treatment to downgrades' is already satisfied by it, which is why upgrades being bare is the anomaly rather than the norm; (3) route the upgrade mutation through it; (4) AC4's test that the mutation cannot fire without confirmation. AC2 (capture the same consent artifact as a new subscription) is now CHEAP because US-2117 landed: subscription_agreements + recordAgreedTerms already exist, and an in-place upgrade produces a customer.subscription.updated event that already flows through handleSubscriptionChange — which now calls recordAgreedTerms. So an upgrade ALREADY writes an agreement row with the new plan/interval/amount. Worth verifying rather than assuming, but the plumbing is in place. userStories.title: No advance renewal reminder exists anywhere — annual plans are charged silently
userStories.description: Confirmed absence, verified three ways: invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch (services/edge-functions/src/routes/webhooks.ts:244-281, falls through to a default log-and-drop at :281); no cron in jobs-cron-fleet.ts sends one; and the only upcoming_invoice reference is a read-only pull for the billing page (payments.ts:1142). The first notice a user receives about a renewal is sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail (email.ts:1183), sent AFTER the money is taken. Yearly price IDs exist for all five paid tiers (src/lib/constants.ts:1344-1366) and flow through the identical path — interval only changes a display string — so an annual subscriber is charged a full year's fee with no prior contact whatsoever.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.upcoming and send a transactional advance renewal notice stating the amount, the date of the charge, the plan, and how to cancel before it.
Configure the Stripe lead time explicitly rather than relying on the default, and set a longer lead for annual plans than monthly.
Send via deliverEmail as a TRANSACTIONAL category — it must not be routed through the drip/marketing engine where opt-out, suppression or frequency caps can silently drop it.
Also handle customer.subscription.trial_will_end.
Test that an annual subscription produces a reminder before renewal and that a marketing opt-out does not suppress it.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Comms] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Advance notice before a long-term renewal is a common state-ARL requirement and we have annual plans in production. Cheapest structural fix in the batch: one webhook case reusing existing email infrastructure. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 + AC4 + AC5 DONE (mechanism, not copy — the fourth compliance story that did not need counsel). invoice.upcoming is now HANDLED and sends sendRenewalReminderEmail, a NEW template deliberately separate from sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail: a receipt confirms something that happened, this warns about something that has not, and the only action that matters — cancel before the date — is meaningless on a receipt. It states the plan, the amount, the exact charge date and how to cancel. AC3: category subscription_renewal_reminder is registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES, so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional even if marketing:true is explicitly requested — pinned by a test, because if that ever flips, an opt-out silently drops the only advance warning of a charge and the exact defect returns. AC4 customer.subscription.trial_will_end is handled too, and THE DISJOINTNESS IS THE INTERESTING PART: our signup trial has NO Stripe subscription (handle_new_user grants it directly), and US-2120's cron filters flipdesk_subscription_id IS NULL. This event fires only for a STRIPE-managed trial — someone who started a PAID subscription with a trial period — which is exactly the user that cron skips. The two populations cannot overlap, so neither path double-sends. A test asserts the cron keeps that filter, since removing it would make both fire for the same person. It reuses sendTrialExpiringEmail rather than minting a second trial template, because two near-identical trial emails drift. DECLINES TO SEND WITHOUT A DATE: if Stripe supplies neither next_payment_attempt nor period_end the handler returns. A notice that cannot say WHEN is not a notice, and 'you will be charged at some point' is worse than silence. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement. TWO OF MY OWN EARLIER ARTEFACTS CAUGHT THIS CHANGE, which is the guards working: (1) the US-2128 test asserting invoice.upcoming and trial_will_end were on the known-ignored list went RED, correctly — they had graduated to real handlers, and a handled event must never ALSO be listed as ignored or the list is lying. Rewritten to assert the list stays annotated rather than naming those two specifically. (2) Removing them left an ORPHANED group header ('Covered by their own stories / other handlers.') heading an empty group — deleted. STILL OPEN: AC2 only — configure the Stripe lead time explicitly (and longer for annual than monthly). That is a Stripe dashboard/API setting, not code: Stripe decides when invoice.upcoming fires, and the default is 3 days. Worth doing since a 3-day warning on a full YEAR's charge is thin, but it cannot be set from here. Verified: edge 4306 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 VERIFIED ALREADY DONE (US-2089-style stale box). This story's premise — 'invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch' — is no longer true: webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to handleInvoiceUpcoming (:284) AND customer.subscription.trial_will_end to handleTrialWillEnd (:294), both carrying US-2119 attribution comments. Closed by that work; the story was simply never flipped. Found while triaging the P1 Compliance/Comms cluster for US-2122. NOT marking passes:true from here, because I did not verify AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time configuration, which is a dashboard setting) or AC5's live test — someone with Stripe access should confirm those two before closing. | 2026-07-22 ADDED THE MISSING AC3/AC5 GUARD (agent loop), passes:false held on the external ACs. The prior note flagged that it "did not verify AC5"; the transactional half of AC5 (and AC3) had NO test at all — sendRenewalReminderEmail uses category subscription_renewal_reminder (email.ts:2936) which IS in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts:49), so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional and a marketing opt-out cannot suppress it — but nothing pinned that. If someone reclassified it, the renewal reminder would silently become marketing-suppressible and an annual subscriber could be charged with no warning (the exact US-2120 bug class). New services/edge-functions/src/tests/renewal-reminder_test.ts (2 tests, mirrors trial-notice_test.ts): asserts the category is transactional + resolveIsMarketing===false, and structurally that webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to sendRenewalReminderEmail (not the drip). Verified: deno check+lint clean, 2 tests pass. STILL passes:false: AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time is a Dashboard billing setting — Settings->Billing->Upcoming renewal reminders — not code) and AC5's live half (an annual sub actually producing a reminder before renewal needs a Stripe run). AC1/AC3/AC4 are done (handleInvoiceUpcoming + handleTrialWillEnd wired, transactional category, now guarded).

userStories.title: iOS paywall advertises 1,000 AI actions for Pro; the server grants 750
userStories.description: ios/GradeThread/Billing/IAPProduct.swift:88,93 advertises Pro as '1,000 listings · 1,000 AI actions · 30 grades · AutoLister'. Both the server catalog (services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/products.ts:75,80) and web (src/lib/constants.ts:243, aiActionsPerMonth: 750) say 750. iOS buyers are sold 1,000 AI actions and will be plan-gated at 750 — a paid-for entitlement that does not exist. The drift test that should catch this (iap-catalog-drift_test.ts:69-106) compares ids, credits, plan/interval and fallbackPrice but NOT blurb or title, so the guard has a hole exactly where the misleading copy lives.
acceptanceCriteria: Correct the iOS copy to match the entitlement actually granted (or change the entitlement — but the two must agree).
Extend iap-catalog-drift_test.ts to compare user-facing blurb and title against the server catalog, so advertised entitlements cannot drift from granted ones.
Audit every other advertised number on the paywall against the server catalog.
Check whether any user purchased Pro on iOS under the 1,000 copy and determine remediation with the review gate.

userStories.title: Substantiation review of every public authenticity claim and its framing
userStories.description: Authenticity verdicts (likely_authentic / inconclusive / red_flags) are shown on public certificates and returned from an unauthenticated public endpoint, currently with no accuracy gate behind them. Separately, the seeded brand KB was written to REFUSE authentication — 00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql:14 reads 'NEVER auto-authenticate... A creed/serial proves NOTHING about authenticity on its own' — so our own knowledge base contradicts the product's public posture. That contradiction needs resolving deliberately, not by drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Review every user-facing authenticity string against what the evidence can actually support, with counsel — fold into the US-2114 review gate rather than running a separate process.

Decide and document the claim posture: assessment/opinion with stated limitations vs verification. The pipeline is built for the former (confidence ceilinged at 0.9, hard-capped to 0.5 on contradiction, limitations set from a constant the model cannot override) — keep that discipline in the copy.
Reconcile the brand-KB 'never auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture.

Check eBay policy exposure: grade-badge.ts is already dead because eBay bans grade overlays on listing imagery, and eBay runs its own Authenticity Guarantee — determine what may be stated on a listing before building listing-facing surfaces.
Confirm the unauthenticated public endpoint should expose verdicts at all.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Legal][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Pairs with the FTC Section 5 batch (US-2114..2128) — same substantiation problem, different claim. Do not let an agent draft the claim language. ACCURACY GATE 2026-07-19 (decided: adopt the conservative posture ahead of counsel): the public /tools/authenticity-check endpoint now requires a PASSING eval run in addition to PUBLIC_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_ENABLED. CORRECTION to an earlier characterisation of the exposure: that endpoint was ALREADY fail-closed behind the env flag (default off) and documented as awaiting legal review of the limitations copy — so the risk was lower than described. What was missing is that the env flag is the LEGAL gate (a human read the copy) and says nothing about whether the model is any good; enabling it after a legal review should not be sufficient to publish verdicts from a prompt version that has never cleared the golden set. The two gates are now separate and both required. Authenticated surfaces (paid add-on, buyer check) deliberately still run ungated — they carry the limitations disclaimer and a named account, a different posture from an anonymous public claim. Returns 503 + Retry-After rather than 404 so a crawler does not deindex the tool page behind it. 4431 edge tests pass.

userStories.title: Garment sellers are never asked for a serial or date-code photo
userStories.description: photo-profiles.ts:31-45 defines serial and marking slots but surfaces them ONLY for non-clothing profiles. A garment seller is never prompted for a date code, interior stamp, or hardware close-up — while ai-authenticity.ts:142-151 asks the model for stitch-per-inch, embroidery backing, screen-print registration and rivet engraving. The prompt requests evidence the capture flow never collects. This is the cheapest single improvement to authenticity signal quality.
acceptanceCriteria: Add serial/date-code and hardware/stamp macro slots to the clothing photo profile, surfaced when the authenticity add-on is active.
Make them optional-but-encouraged rather than blocking a condition grade — a grade must never fail because an authenticity slot was skipped.
Feed slot presence into the authenticity confidence: absent macro evidence should lower confidence and widen limitations, not be silently ignored.
Mirror across web and iOS (photo required-set and order surfaces change together — see the photo-required-and-order-surfaces memory; ~7 spots).
Update the prompt so it asks only for what the available slots can actually support.

Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Highest-leverage unblocked item in Phase 1 — everything downstream depends on capturing the right pixels. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: added optional serial (Serial / Date code) + marking (Brand stamp / Hardware) roles to the CLOTHING photo profile with macro-specific hints. Pure config — both storage types already existed in the enum (migration 00230) and were merely never surfaced for clothing, so NO migration and NO client release: photo-profiles.ts is server-authoritative and both clients fetch it (iOS already maps both, PhotoSlotType.swift:46-47). PRODUCT DECISION LEFT OPEN: 0.7 was chosen because it sits exactly on both thresholds — deriveVerdict needs >=0.7 for likely_authentic and authenticityNeedsReview forces review BELOW 0.7 — so it removes high confidence without flipping every existing no-macro verdict to inconclusive or flooding the review queue. Going stricter is defensible but changes the headline verdict on past assessments; that is a product call, not a refactor call. The authenticity eval cannot pass until US-2131 seeds a golden set, so the prompt narrowing is GATED ON US-2131 — it is not independently shippable. Deliberately NOT edited silently. When unblocked, the sanctioned route is the additive/flag-gated pattern the skill describes: a macro-awareness block that suffixes prompt_version (mirroring authenticity_v1+tells) and is byte-identical when disabled, test-guarded.

userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). The server does no further resize, and Claude's own ~1568px normalization is the effective ceiling. A label filling a third of the frame yields roughly 500px of label: enough to OCR a size, nowhere near enough for stitch density, kerning, weave or engraving fidelity. The only real magnification path today is the Forensic add-on's defect zoom (grading-pipeline.ts:130-172), which crops the retained original and upscales to a 320px minimum — but it is keyed to defect bboxes only, never to tags or hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.
Generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching) rather than defect bboxes only — this is the most reusable existing asset.
Measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it, so confidence can be conditioned on real evidence quality rather than assumed.
Respect the existing storage/upload hardening path (validateImageUpload -> stripImageMetadata -> upload) and the Vision budget ceiling.
Do not raise resolution globally — the upload-speed tradeoff that motivated the iOS reduction is real; scope the increase to authenticity slots.

Without this the prompt is asking for evidence the pixels cannot carry, which is precisely how an ungated model produces confident nonsense. | 2026-07-31 AC1+AC5 DONE (web). Authenticity slots (serial/marking/surface/corner/sole) now compress to 3600px, tag/label/detail/defect/interior/certificate to 3000, everything else keeps the unchanged 2400 default -- uploadMaxWidthFor() in src/lib/macro-photo-quality.ts, applied at both upload paths (submission photo-upload.tsx and FlipDesk photo-uploader.tsx). userStories.title: Deepen brand-decoders cross-checks — the strongest deterministic signal we have
userStories.description: brand-decoders.ts is a data-driven regex decoder engine whose crossCheck produces DecodeInconsistency on impossible dates (date_in_future, date_before_brand at :236-245), fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence (ai-authenticity.ts:346-353). This is deterministic contradiction detection — it does not depend on model judgment, cannot be talked out of a finding, and is already built and underused. It is the highest-confidence authenticity signal available today and the one most worth extending. CORRECTION 2026-07-19 (after reading vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-decoder-bar.md, which the grading-engine skill instructs be read BEFORE adding any decoder): this story as originally filed invites the exact failure that note forbids. Decoders must clear tag-printed AND regular AND BRAND-UNIQUE IN FORMAT, plus a fourth question added 2026-07-19 — WHICH ENTITY does the identifier name? Reebok, PUMA, Chanel/Moncler/Balenciaga serials, the Canada Goose hologram and URBN OB###### are all deliberately decoder-less; they look like coverage gaps and are not. Decoder authority OUTRANKS the AI on conflict, so a false decoder does not merely add a wrong guess — it overrides a correct one. Expanding coverage by submission volume, as originally written, would mint false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: Treat CROSS-CHECKS and DECODERS as different risk classes. A cross-check detects a contradiction (impossible date, mismatched era) and cannot mis-attribute a brand — that is the safe expansion path and where effort should go. A decoder RECOVERS a brand from a code and can override a correct read.
Any new decoder must clear all three bar tests AND the which-entity question, with the reasoning recorded in the vault note alongside the existing table.
Do NOT seed a decoder for any code listed as a deliberate refusal — extend the refusal table instead if a new one is evaluated and rejected.

A parent-wide or shared identifier (URBN OB######, shared RN 66170) can never attribute a sibling brand. Any RN/CA cross-check must handle shared RNs explicitly rather than treating RN -> brand as one-to-one.
Codes that fail the bar get transcribed into tag_eras or authentication_tells, never wired to brand recovery.
A contradiction from a deterministic decoder must dominate model optimism — verify applyVerdictCap composition holds (caps compose as a min and never raise).
Surface which decoders fired in the operator view so a verdict is explainable.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Signal][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Deterministic signal is also the most defensible claim: 'the date code is impossible for this brand' is a fact, not an opinion. Prioritize this over model-side tuning. The safe, high-value work here is CROSS-CHECK expansion (contradiction detection), not decoder expansion (brand attribution) — the vault note is unambiguous that a false decoder is worse than no decoder. Read vault/20-domain/brands/{brand-kb-decoder-bar,brand-kb-alias-refusals,brand-kb-negative-findings}.md before touching this. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ THIS STORY'S FOUNDING PREMISE IS FALSE — READ BEFORE STARTING. The description states the cross-checks are 'fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence'. THEY ARE NOT. Traced end to end: buildTellsBlock (ai-authenticity.ts:386) accepts a crossChecks array and renders the DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS block, and assessAuthenticity reads it as `context.crossChecks ?? []` (:543) — but NOTHING IN THE CODEBASE EVER SUPPLIES IT. All four production callers (grading-pipeline.ts:1243, buyer-authenticity.ts:50, public-grading.ts:1106, authenticity-eval.ts:484) pass `{ tells }` only. So the array is always empty, the block never renders, and crossCheckDecodeResult — the only producer — has ZERO callers (found by audit-unwired-exports.mjs). THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS STORY: every AC is about DEEPENING a signal that is not connected. Adding decoders and cross-checks as written would extend a pure function whose output still reaches nothing, and the work would test green throughout — the deepened signal simply never reaches the model. WIRE IT FIRST, and note the plumbing already exists on the consuming side, so this is genuinely small: ai-extract.ts already computes decoderHits: DecodeResult[] (:946,:981) in production. The missing step is running crossCheckDecodeResult over those hits and passing the result as context.crossChecks. BUT IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER, and this is the part worth flagging: this ADDS DYNAMIC PER-ITEM CONTEXT TO AN AUTHENTICITY PROMPT, which the grading-engine skill requires be flag-gated and to SUFFIX prompt_version so accuracy tracking can attribute eras (the same rule that governs +baseline/+fabric/+visual). Shipping it unflagged would silently change verdicts under an unchanged version string and make every before/after accuracy comparison meaningless. AC6 (applyVerdictCap composition) also cannot be verified today, because a contradiction can never currently reach the model to dominate its optimism. RECOMMEND: split the wiring (+ flag + version suffix + eval) out as its own story ahead of this one; the decoder-bar discipline in AC2-AC5 is unaffected and still correct.

userStories.description: As a consumer grading on iOS, I want the same journey the web offers. acceptanceCriteria: Decide explicitly whether the consumer grading path belongs on iOS. Nothing in IOS_PARITY_AUDIT.md or the Android plan mentions this omission either way, which is weak evidence it is accidental rather than a product decision — settle it in writing.

If it does not: document why, and confirm the dispute obligation is discharged some other way — a 14-day dispute window that only one client can exercise is a support and chargeback liability regardless of intent.

userStories.title: iOS: bulk photo import is strictly serial though a bounded-concurrency helper already exists
userStories.description: Both PHPicker import paths — AutoListerReviewModel.swift:218-243 and PhotoIntakeView.swift:907-923 — are plain serial for loops awaiting per photo: result.loadImage() (I/O; for iCloud-backed photos a NETWORK round trip each), then PhotoCompressor.compressOffMain (CPU), then a detached DHash.compute (CPU, :238-240). Meanwhile PhotoCompressor.compressBatch(_:maxConcurrent:) (PhotoCompressor.swift:64-91) exists for exactly this — bounded concurrency, per-item autoreleasepool, order-preserving — and a grep of the whole ios/ tree shows its ONLY caller is Inventory/PhotosDropHandler.swift:20. Neither high-volume import path uses it.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrap the whole per-photo unit (load + compress + dHash) in the chunked withTaskGroup shape already used correctly three times in this codebase: PhotoCompressor.compressBatch, DisclosureStore.renderAll (Disclosure/DisclosureStore.swift:88-115) and ReconciliationService (:215-242).

Keep concurrency modest (3-4) so only a few full-resolution UIImages are resident — that memory property is why compressBatch was written, and parallelising without it trades a latency win for a jetsam risk.
Preserve input order via the enumerate-and-sort approach at DisclosureStore.swift:106.
userStories.notes:
[P2][iOS/Performance] Found 2026-07-18 by the iOS audit. The dominant cost is loadImage(), not compression: for iCloud-backed photos that is a serialized network fetch per photo, so a 200-photo import is 200 sequential round trips. Symptom: bulk import sits on the spinner for minutes rather than tens of seconds when photos are not local, and it widens the window for the 'still downloading from iCloud' partial-failure path the code already anticipates (:255-259). NOT FIXED HERE — Swift is unbuildable on Windows.

VERIFIED 2026-07-18 — REAL, still open, deliberately NOT fixed blind.

Confirmed at PhotoIntakeView.ingestLibraryPicks (:907): a plain `for result in results` loop awaiting result.loadImage() then compressOffMain per item. Strictly serial, so 200 iCloud-backed photos are 200 sequential network round trips.

Refinement to the story premise: the existing helper CANNOT be applied directly. PhotoCompressor.compressBatch takes [UIImage] — images already in memory — while the bottleneck is loadImage() upstream of it. What compressBatch does provide is the exact PATTERN to copy: a windowed `withTaskGroup(of: (Int, T).self)` writing into a pre-sized results array, which preserves picker order (the loop comment notes order matters for the tray) and bounds residency.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT worth recording, because the obvious implementation is wrong: do NOT load all images first and then call compressBatch. compressBatch own header explains why — it keeps only a few full-resolution UIImages resident so a large drop does not spike memory into a jetsam kill. Loading 200 full-res UIImages up front reintroduces exactly that risk. The correct shape is ONE windowed TaskGroup where each task does loadImage + compress together, so at most maxConcurrent full-res images exist at any moment.

Why not fixed here: this is ~25 lines of NEW concurrent Swift on the bulk-import path, with ordering and memory-residency invariants, and it cannot be compiled or tested on this Windows checkout. That is a different risk class from the one-word LazyHStack change — needs a macOS session.

userStories.title: No price-change notice or consent path on any platform
userStories.description: No code path notifies a user of a price increase before it takes effect. Stripe's price.updated and customer.subscription.updated-with-price-delta are not inspected (webhooks.ts:244-281). On Apple, the ASSN router (lib/appstore/notifications.ts:18-32) does not handle PRICE_INCREASE or DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF — Apple collects price-increase consent natively so this is not a rejection risk, but the server never learns a price change occurred, and an unconsented lapse arrives only as a generic EXPIRED. On Google Play, PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is explicitly a no-op (lib/google-play/rtdn.ts:11,107).
acceptanceCriteria: Notify subscribers in advance of any price increase, stating the old price, new price, effective date and how to cancel first.
Handle Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF so server state reflects platform-side changes.
Decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web (it commonly does under state ARLs) and implement accordingly.
Do not implement a price change of any kind until this exists.
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Billing] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Currently latent — no price change has been attempted. It becomes a live exposure the moment pricing moves, which makes it cheap to fix now and expensive to fix under deadline. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (mechanism — no counsel). Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF now reach server state. routeNotification gained a THIRD kind of verdict, record_only, distinct from both an entitlement action and 'ignore'. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Apple owns price-increase consent natively, so ACTING on these would be wrong — if the customer refuses, Apple lapses the subscription and we hear EXPIRED. But ignoring them meant that later EXPIRED was uninterpretable: indistinguishable from an ordinary cancellation, with no way to tell that a price change preceded it. Recording without acting is exactly the right posture, and it is the same 'known-ignored vs unexamined' distinction I built for the Stripe switch in US-2128 — the two surfaces had the identical defect. REUSED recordAppstoreEvent rather than hand-rolling the insert: it already namespaces stripe_event_id as appstore:<id> and swallows 23505, so an Apple retry cannot double-record. (My first attempt DID hand-roll it — the helper was 180 lines above and I had not looked. Worth noting because writing the second copy is always easier than finding the first.) 4 tests, including the two that matter: record_only must NOT be an entitlement action (not sub_active, not sub_expired, not revoke), and an unknown type must STILL fail closed to ignore — widening a router is exactly when a permissive default sneaks in. REMAINING, and correctly split: AC1 (notify subscribers in advance of an increase) needs the COPY, which is US-2114's gate — but note the DETECTION half is now free: US-2117's migration 00486 added pricing_plan_revisions, an append-only price history written BY TRIGGER, so 'a price changed' is already a queryable fact rather than something needing new plumbing. AC3 is explicitly a decision ('decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web') and belongs to counsel. AC4 is a CONSTRAINT rather than work — do not ship a price change until AC1/AC3 exist — and is worth keeping visible: the pricing_plans trigger will now record any change, so an accidental one leaves evidence. Google Play PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is still a no-op (rtdn.ts) and is the same shape as the Apple fix if someone wants symmetry. Verified: edge 4310 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC2 EXTENDED TO GOOGLE PLAY — the symmetry I flagged last pass, and it turned out to be the SHARPER of the two platforms. Apple's PRICE_INCREASE is a notification that a price WILL change; Google's PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is the user ACCEPTING one. That makes it a consent artifact — exactly what subscription_agreements (US-2117) exists to hold — and dropping it meant the only server-side evidence of the acceptance was the eventual renewal amount, which is an INFERENCE rather than a record. classifyRtdn now returns record_only for type 8, and the reconciler writes an audit row via the existing recordEvent dep (idempotent on the event id) while touching no entitlement: Google owns the consent UI, so acting would pre-empt it, and the next renewal RTDN settles the amount. ADDED A DISTINCT OUTCOME VALUE rather than reusing 'ignored': both leave entitlement untouched, but one wrote an audit row and the other did not. Collapsing them would leave the RTDN log unable to answer 'did we ever learn the user accepted a price change?' — which is the entire point of the branch. TWO THINGS THE TYPE SYSTEM AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT, both of them the system working: (1) adding the union variant broke the route glue's narrowing at `action.productType`, which is TypeScript correctly refusing to let a new action fall through unhandled; (2) an existing test asserted type 8 → ignore and went RED, correctly — it was encoding the old behaviour, and it was right to fail rather than let the change pass silently. Updated it to state WHY 8 left that group, so the next reader sees the reasoning rather than an unexplained gap in [9,10,11]. PROCESS NOTE: this took four attempts because bash ate template literals and regex escapes in inline node -e scripts (the fifth such incident today). Anything containing backticks or regex now goes through the Edit tool, not a shell string. Verified: edge 4312 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). California AB 2863 requires cancellation through the same medium used for the original transaction. Web is fine; the divergent path is the risk, not the flow itself. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC2 DONE (no counsel needed — this half is a code defect, not copy). AC1: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker now routes to the REVIEWED cancellation dialog instead of opening the Stripe billing portal. The portal path skipped everything the reviewed flow was designed for: the period-end statement on every screen, the required acknowledgement checkbox, the reason capture, and the undo banner. A divergent second route is how an audited flow stops being the one users actually hit. THE DESIGN POINT: it is a CALLBACK (onRequestCancel), not a self-rendered dialog, because CancelSubscriptionDialog ALREADY opens this picker as its 'switch to a cheaper plan' off-ramp — rendering the cancel dialog inside the picker would have made the two mutually recursive. The parent owns the flow; the picker only reports intent. When the prop is omitted (i.e. the picker was opened FROM the cancel dialog) the Free tile simply closes the picker, returning the user to the cancel flow they are already in rather than stacking a second copy of it. AC2 AUDITED: after the fix, every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation — the plan picker's own non-cancel branch (same-tier interval change) and past-due-banner's 'update payment method'. Using the portal is fine; routing a CANCELLATION through it is not, because cancellation is the flow carrying the review requirements. 4 guard tests pin that distinction explicitly, including one asserting past-due-banner may keep its portal call, so a future reader does not 'fix' it by mistake. The strongest assertion is ordering: the isCancelToFree branch must come BEFORE portal.mutate() AND must return — a guard that merely EXISTS while falling through would leave the bug intact while looking fixed. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by deleting the guard: that test goes red. STILL OPEN: AC3 (have the review gate assess whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations) is explicitly a US-2114 counsel-review item, not an engineering call — the story itself routes it there. AC4 (cancellation available in the same medium as signup) is stated in the story as already satisfied — web-purchased cancels on web, IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet — and I did not re-derive it. Verified: tsc clean, lint 0 errors, web 2293 passed. | 2026-08-03 AC4 VERIFIED — and it was NOT satisfied. No migration. The note said AC4 was 'stated in the story as already satisfied', i.e. taken on the audit's word and never checked. Checking it found a real defect on the server. THE WEB AND iOS HALVES DID HOLD: src/pages/billing.tsx computes isAppstoreManaged and hides every Stripe subscription CTA behind it, showing 'Manage this plan in the GradeThread iOS app' instead; iOS presents .manageSubscriptionsSheet in PaywallView and PlanSection and never calls the web cancel endpoint. THE SERVER HALF DID NOT. appstoreSubscriptionBlocksStripe guarded the SUBSCRIBE and CHANGE-PLAN endpoints and not CANCEL. An App Store subscriber has no flipdesk_subscription_id, so POST /flipdesk/cancel fell straight through to 'No subscription to cancel' — a 400 telling a paying customer they have nothing while Apple carried on billing them monthly. Someone who believes that message reasonably concludes they are not subscribed, and the next thing they hear is a renewal receipt. That is worse than an error: it is a confident wrong answer on a billing question. HIDING A BUTTON IS NOT ENFORCEMENT, which is why the UI half passing did not make AC4 true. The endpoint is reachable from any client holding a token, and the iOS app talks to the same API. FIXED: cancel now returns the same 409 + `action` contract the purchase paths already use (manage_in_app / manage_in_play), which the clients already branch on. Apple and Google both REQUIRE cancellation on-platform, so the honest answer is not an error at all — it is where to go. ORDERING IS THE DEFECT, NOT PRESENCE, and the guard says so: both checks can exist and the wrong one still win, because an in-app subscriber has no Stripe subscription id. A case pins that the medium check runs BEFORE the no-subscription check. 6 new cases in cancel-medium-parity_test.ts: the precedence helpers still recognise active/trialing/past_due on both stores AND still return false for Stripe (or web cancellation breaks for the people it is for), the cancel route refuses and names where to go, the ordering, the purchase paths keep their own guards (cancel and purchase have to agree about who is in-app managed — this story is about them drifting apart once), the billing page still hides the CTAs, and iOS still defers to the platform sheet without calling the web endpoint. ⚠ MY OWN GUARD MATCHED ITS OWN COMMENT, fourth time this session: the ordering case searched for the string 'No subscription to cancel', which the comment above the fix QUOTES to explain the bug — and that comment sits before the guard, so the scan reported the ordering as still broken. Comments are stripped now. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS: the cancel guard removed, the guard moved after the no-subscription check, the refusal losing its action, a trialing in-app subscriber no longer recognised, and the billing page showing Stripe CTAs. Each reddened. (One mutation initially reported a false pass because .replace hit the SUBSCRIBE handler's occurrence first — re-run scoped to the cancel handler, where it reddens correctly.) REMAINING: AC3 only — whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations. That is explicitly a US-2114 counsel item, not an engineering call. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5400 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1345 files.

THE EVIDENCE, gathered before asking so the question was cheap: no 14-day money-back guarantee exists anywhere in the codebase — not in constants, not in the Stripe setup, not in the webhook handlers.
