Both public pages say the opposite of the vault (refund.tsx section 3 and terms.tsx: subscription fees non-refundable once a billing period has begun, except where required by law or expressly granted in writing). What DOES exist is a 14-day free TRIAL, which is real, advertised on the landing page and in the plan picker, and is a completely different thing. Two features sharing a number is the most likely origin of a policy nobody agreed to. WHY THIS MATTERED IN A DIRECTION, and it is the part worth keeping: an internal note promising a refund the public pages deny is a promise support might honour case by case. That produces an UNDISCLOSED policy applied inconsistently, which is worse than either answer on its own — worse than not offering it, and worse than offering it openly. AC2 does not apply: there is no guarantee to disclose at the point of sale. The vault section is rewritten to state the three real rules (subscriptions non-refundable, credit packs non-refundable once a grade is generated but credits never expire, billing errors refunded within 60 days), each pointing at the page or constant that owns it, with a callout recording what the claim was and why it was wrong. refund.tsx and terms.tsx are added to the note's code_refs so a change to either now drifts the note. A SECOND CONTRADICTION FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: terms.tsx says "Unused grading credits DO NOT ROLL OVER and are not refundable". That conflates two different things. Purchased credit packs never expire — constants.ts:384, migration 00037 and 00415 all say so explicitly. The MONTHLY PLAN ALLOWANCE (users.grades_used_this_month) does reset each cycle and genuinely does not roll over. The word "credits" is used for both, so the sentence is true of one and false of the other. It UNDERSTATES what a paying customer gets, so it costs conversion rather than creating legal exposure — but it is still a false statement in the Terms. I did not edit it: AC4 puts these pages under counsel review, and rewriting Terms copy ahead of that trades one unreviewed statement for another. Recorded in the vault note under its own heading so it is not lost, and carried on this story. NOTE ON MY OWN FIRST READING: I initially thought refund.tsx contradicted the vault on credit expiry too. It does not — "credits do not expire INTO A CASH BALANCE" is about cash redemption, and I had read a truncated line. Checked the full sentence before acting. STILL OPEN: AC3 (reconcile the point-of-sale copy with the legal pages — nothing to reconcile now that there is no guarantee, but the credits sentence above is in scope) and AC4 (the EU/UK right-of-withdrawal waiver in refund.tsx section 4 and the chargeback clause in section 5, both needing counsel).

userStories.title: Generalize the iOS tag-quality gate to web and to every macro slot
userStories.description: iOS already has the right pattern: TagPhotoQuality.swift:24-47 enforces a 700px floor plus on-device OCR requiring at least 4 characters before accepting a tag photo. Web has no tag-quality gate at all, and neither platform applies a quality gate to any other macro slot. A blurry or too-distant macro shot currently reaches the model looking exactly like a good one.
acceptanceCriteria: Port the tag-quality gate to web.
Apply a quality gate to every authenticity macro slot, with per-slot thresholds.
Reject or warn in-capture with actionable guidance ('move closer', 'hold steady') rather than failing silently after upload.
Feed the measured quality into authenticity confidence rather than treating accepted/rejected as binary.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Capture][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. The pattern exists and is proven on iOS — this is generalization, not invention. | 2026-07-31 AC1+AC2+AC3 DONE; AC4 recorded as deferred, not half-built. New src/lib/macro-photo-quality.ts is the web port: per-slot long-edge floors + a sharpness floor, pure assessment separated from the browser measurement so the logic is testable without a canvas. THE ONE THING NOT PORTED, deliberately: the iOS on-device OCR check. The browser has no built-in recognizer and bundling Tesseract's ~2MB wasm on every page load to replicate a check whose PURPOSE is 'is there enough detail here to read' is the wrong trade -- normalized Laplacian variance answers that directly instead of by proxy, costs a few hundred bytes, and catches what OCR was standing in for (blur, shake, glare, too far). AC2 is real per-slot thresholds, not one number renamed: 700px keeps the iOS tag baseline; serial/marking get 900 because a struck code is physically smaller than tag print and resolves less at the same pixel count; surface/corner/sole get 800. Full-garment slots are deliberately EXCLUDED -- photo-standards.ts already governs those at eBay's 500px floor, and the two gates answer different questions ('will eBay accept it' vs 'can the model read it'). WIRED INTO BOTH CAPTURE SURFACES, which mattered more than it looks: the submission flow only has tag/label/detail slots, so wiring it alone would have left the authenticity slots (serial, marking, surface, corner, sole) ungated -- those live in the FlipDesk photo-uploader. Submission renders an amber per-slot line; the uploader raises a warning toast post-upload. Both assess the COMPRESSED bytes rather than the camera original, because compressImage caps at 2400/1600px and the model only ever sees what was stored. LENIENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, matching iOS: warns and offers a retake, never blocks, and every uncertain input (unknown dimension, decode failure, NaN) fails OPEN -- a gate that blocks on its own inability to measure blames the seller for our bug, and a false 'retake this' is exactly what trains sellers to ignore the nudge. 27 tests asserting BOTH halves (fires on bad, silent on good, passes exactly AT the floor), plus the metric's own property -- zero on a flat image, large on a hard-edged one, and strictly lower on a blurred copy of the same image, which is what matters rather than any absolute number. AC4 DEFERRED WITH THE GROUNDWORK IN PLACE: the assessment already carries a continuous 0..1 `score` on both pass and fail precisely so authenticity confidence can read a measure instead of a pass/fail bit, but delivering it to the grading pass means persisting it per photo -- a schema change, and the held-migration rule means a migration commit cannot be pushed without the operator applying the SQL first. Verified: tsc -b clean, lint 0 errors, 2898 tests pass, build green.

userStories.title: Guided macro capture — framing, distance and lighting for authenticity shots
userStories.description: There is no guided capture for authenticity evidence: no framing overlay, no distance guide, no lighting instruction. iOS uses .builtInWideAngleCamera with no zoom or focus tuning (CameraSession.swift:238), so macro shots depend entirely on the seller's instinct. The existing photo-profiles hints said WHAT to shoot and nothing about distance or light, which is where macro shots actually fail. LIGHTING ADVICE IS SLOT-SPECIFIC ON PURPOSE, and this is the substantive part: the failure modes are OPPOSITE. A struck serial is visible only by its shadow and needs single-side low-angle light; a glossy care label needs even indirect light or the print blows out. One reusable 'use good light' sentence would have been easier and would not have changed a single photo -- a test asserts the lighting lines are not all identical, because boilerplate would pass every other assertion in the file. THE OVERLAY IS SIZED TO BE SATISFIABLE, which is the reviewable judgement: a guide box you can fill and still be told 'move closer' is worse than no box, so the fill fractions are chosen against the US-2136 floors at the US-2135 caps, and a test walks every slot asserting that filling the box delivers more pixels than that slot's own floor -- so raising a floor without revisiting the overlay fails in CI rather than in a seller's hands. The box is decorative only; the capture is still the full frame, so it constrains composition and never the saved pixels. THE COVERAGE TEST IS WHY THIS PAIRS WITH US-2136: every slot the quality gate can reject now has guidance for getting it right, because a gate without guidance is just blame. STILL OPEN: AC2 (closer-focus camera configuration) is iOS and cannot be built in this environment; AC3 (worked good-vs-unusable examples per slot) needs real example imagery, which is design work rather than code; AC4 (gate the rollout on measured pixel-density improvement) needs the per-photo measurement persisted first, which is US-2135 AC3 and blocked on a migration. Verified: tsc -b clean, lint 0 errors, 2912 tests pass, build green.

Reconcile the seeded 'NEVER auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture (see US-2133) rather than leaving the KB and the product in contradiction.

userStories.title: Legal ToS/privacy versions are hardcoded in both clients while the server derives them from the DB — and iOS has no re-acceptance gate
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want consent records to name the version the user actually saw. The edge derives current legal versions DYNAMICALLY from DB rows (lib/legal-versions.ts:66, consumed at routes/legal.ts:73,105,162). Both clients HARDCODE them: ios/GradeThread/Auth/AuthStore.swift:19-20 (legalTosVersion / legalPrivacyVersion = '2026-04-01') and src/lib/constants.ts:1491-1494 (LEGAL_VERSIONS). The only sync mechanism is a code comment (AuthStore.swift:17-18, 'Keep IN SYNC with the web ... and the edge mirror') with no automated guard. Worse, iOS has NO re-acceptance gate at all: web has src/components/auth/legal-gate.tsx; iOS never calls /api/legal (0 matches).
acceptanceCriteria: Clients must READ the current version from the server rather than hardcoding it, or a build-time guard must fail when the constants disagree with the DB-backed source.
Implement a re-acceptance gate on iOS equivalent to legal-gate.tsx.
Add a test/guard covering the three-way agreement (edge DB, web constants, iOS constants) — a comment is not a mechanism.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Legal] Found 2026-07-18 by the cross-platform parity deep dive. The failure mode is silent and legally material: the moment an operator publishes a new ToS row via admin-legal.ts, web and iOS signups keep recording 2026-04-01 — users are attested to a version they were never shown, and iOS users are never re-prompted at all. That is a defensible-consent failure, and exactly what an enterprise or legal review looks for. | 2026-07-18 SCOPED DOWN + GUARD ADDED (agent loop). ⚠ THIS STORY OVERSTATED THE RISK and the correction matters more than the fix. It claims users are 'attested to a version they were never shown'. For the WEB that is not what happens: legal-gate.tsx does NOT trust the hardcoded constant — it asks /api/legal/status (its own comment says so at :29) — and /api/legal/accept stamps the SERVER's current versions (legal.ts:103-106), never a client-supplied value. So after a FORCING republish the system SELF-CORRECTS: the gate fires and an immutable legal_acceptances row is written with the real version. The genuine residual hole is narrower and does NOT self-correct: on a MINOR republish (requires_reacceptance:false) requiredSince deliberately does not advance, so the gate correctly stays quiet — while handle_new_user (00142:79) still records the CLIENT-SUPPLIED constant into users.tos_accepted_version. The new user was shown the live document (/terms serves current) but their record names an older version, and nothing later corrects it. Moderate, not the defensible-consent failure described. FIXED WHAT IS FIXABLE HERE: added src/lib/__tests__/legal-versions-lockstep.test.ts pinning the baseline across all THREE projects that hold it — web LEGAL_VERSIONS, edge FALLBACK_TOS/PRIVACY_VERSION, and iOS AuthStore.legalTosVersion/legalPrivacyVersion — plus a shape check so a placeholder value cannot silently disable the gate. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED from every direction: drifting the web constant fails 2 assertions, drifting the iOS constant fails 1. That iOS assertion is the valuable one — Swift cannot be compiled on a Windows checkout, so a source-level check is the ONLY cross-project verification available for it. STILL passing:false on the two real ACs: (1) the durable fix is for the server to stamp the version at signup rather than trusting client metadata — that is a migration to handle_new_user and I did not want to stack a third held one; (2) iOS still has NO re-acceptance gate at all (grep for api/legal across ios/ returns nothing), which remains the largest genuine gap in this story and needs a macOS session. [2026-07-19 AC3 DONE + AC1 GUARD HALF. AC2 NEEDS macOS — story stays open] AC3 was the whole point of the story (a comment is not a mechanism) and is now real: src/test/legal-version-parity.test.ts asserts the THREE-WAY agreement between the edge fallbacks (FALLBACK_TOS_VERSION / FALLBACK_PRIVACY_VERSION), web LEGAL_VERSIONS, and the iOS AuthStore.swift static lets, by parsing each source. Negative-verified by bumping the iOS constant to 2026-09-01 — the guard fails naming all three values. AC1: took the guard option the AC explicitly allows rather than making clients read /api/legal at runtime. A build-time comparison against the live DB is not possible (no DB at build), and the edge FALLBACK constants are the DB-backed sources checked-in form, so this pins what CAN be pinned. Making the clients dynamic remains the stronger fix and is still open. Also asserted the versions are ISO dates: the edge ORDERS versions to decide whether re-acceptance is required, so a free-form string would break that comparison silently. And the parse-succeeded guard is explicit, because comparing null to null would have passed vacuously — it caught a real bug immediately when a heredoc ate the backslashes in my regex and both parsers returned null. AC2 NOT DONE and deliberately not faked: iOS has no re-acceptance gate (never calls /api/legal) while web has legal-gate.tsx. I cannot build or test Swift on Windows, and writing a compliance gate blind is precisely the wrong place for that. A test asserts the gap STILL EXISTS so it flips the moment someone implements it, rather than the story looking complete because the parity guard is green. AuthStore.swift now documents the gap in place. Seventh prose-matching guard failure this session: my new Swift comment names /api/legal, which the absence assertion matched. Comments are stripped now. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00142) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. userStories.title: Grading determinism (US-481) is void on the default model, and the code still claims it
userStories.description: ai-config.ts:157-179 documents that grading ALWAYS uses a low temperature, defaulting to 0 (fully greedy decoding), because a certified score backs a public 'standardized' value prop. But gradingSamplingParams() returns output_config.effort — not temperature — for effort-based models, and the default grading model (DEFAULTS.model = claude-sonnet-5) is effort-based. So getGradingTemperature() is never called on the shipping path, GRADING_MAX_TEMPERATURE and the whole clamping apparatus are dead code, and grading runs at the model's own non-greedy decoding. A regrade of the same photos can return a different score with no explanation.
acceptanceCriteria: DECIDE the product position: is a regrade of identical photos allowed to return a different score? That is a trust question, not an engineering one.
If determinism is still the promise: add a self-consistency check (grade twice, compare, flag divergence) or pin a decoding mode that guarantees it.

If it is NOT the promise: correct the ai-config.ts comment block, which currently asserts a property the code does not have, and disclose run-to-run variance wherever the 'standardized grade' claim is made.
Either way the comment must stop describing temperature clamping as though it governs grading.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Trust] Found 2026-07-18 by the grading-engine deep dive. I VERIFIED the mechanism myself: DEFAULTS.model is claude-sonnet-5 (ai-config.ts:12), modelUsesEffort() matches it (:189-192), and gradingSamplingParams() returns the effort branch with no temperature (:228-233). This is NOT a code bug — effort-based models do not accept temperature, so the US-1033 migration was a correct API fix. The defect is that it silently removed a DOCUMENTED GUARANTEE and nobody updated the guarantee. Code that claims a property it no longer has is the most dangerous state for a trust product, because everyone downstream reasons from the claim rather than the behaviour. I deliberately did not 'fix' it: the right answer is a product decision — restore determinism (costly, possibly not available on this model family) or stop promising it (cheap, but it changes what a certificate means). [2026-07-19 PARTIAL — AC3(a)+AC4 DONE, AC1/AC2/AC3(b) BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT DECISION] Verified the technical claim in full: getDefaultModel()=claude-sonnet-5 is effort-based, so gradingSamplingParams() returns output_config.effort and NO temperature; getGradingTemperature()/GRADING_MAX_TEMPERATURE are dead on the shipping path. Found a THIRD layer the story did not name: grading-reliability.ts implements the self-consistency math AC2 asks for, is pure and tested, but has ZERO non-test callers — the env-gated live-sampling job it describes was never built. So the determinism promise is unenforced at every level: no greedy decoding, no measurement, no gate. Done: both false comment blocks (ai-config.ts, grading-reliability.ts) now describe reality and name the open decision; new src/tests/grading-determinism_test.ts pins the actual behaviour (4 tests) so the claim cannot silently drift back. BLOCKED: AC1 is explicitly a trust/product call — is a regrade of identical photos allowed to return a different score? AC2 depends on that answer (wire grading-reliability.ts as a live self-consistency gate vs accept variance); AC3(b) public-copy disclosure depends on it too. NOTE: do NOT remedy by pinning a temperature — effort-based models 400 on it (US-1033).

NOTE the story cites src/lib/seo/marketing-jsonld.ts; the file is at src/pages/marketing/marketing-jsonld.ts. What was wrong: the brand was re-declared as ANONYMOUS INLINE NODES ({"@type":"Organization", name:"GradeThread"}) at 8 sites, so every publisher/provider/isPartOf edge landed on a fresh unnamed entity and none of it accrued to the site-wide Organization — plus 4 hardcoded copies of the ORG_ID string. ORG_ID/WEBSITE_ID are now exported from json-ld.ts and referenced. THE FIX IS DELIBERATELY NOT UNIFORM, which is the whole judgement here: a bare {"@id"} reference is only valid where the target node is actually ON the page. organizationLd() is emitted by marketing-layout, legal-layout and every prerender head, so publisher/provider became bare refs. webSiteLd() is emitted ONLY on the home route (verified) — so isPartOf stays an INLINE node that additionally CARRIES @id: WEBSITE_ID. Converting it to a bare ref would have been the tidier-looking edit and would have produced a DANGLING pointer to a node the document never defines, which is strictly worse than the anonymous node it replaced. AC5 (certificate Products orphaned) got the same treatment for the same reason: US-425 documented the cert Review author as deliberately inline because the cert page emits only Product + Breadcrumb, and that reasoning still holds — so the node keeps its name/url AND gains @id: ORG_ID. Self-contained for a consumer reading the page alone, merged for one that has also seen the Organization. Mirrored in the SSR (blog-render.ts certificateProductLd + passportProductLd) for both cert and passport; the existing SPA/SSR byte-equality test passed unmodified, which is what confirms the mirrors moved together. THE TEST IS THE PART WORTH READING: the first version listed five builders by hand, and when I reintroduced an anonymous node to check it, IT PASSED — none of the five happened to contain a fixed site. Rewrote it to DERIVE its coverage from every zero-arg *JsonLd export plus every FLIPDESK_LANDINGS entry (53 assertions), so a new builder is covered the day it is added. Re-negative-verified both failure directions: an anonymous provider node reddens 2 tests, a bare dangling WebSite ref reddens 1, restoring returns to green. Verified: 2449 web tests pass, tsc -b clean, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Content engine is built and cold — 4 finished drafts unpublished, flags off, webhooks unset
userStories.description: The content pipeline is complete and deliberately switched off. content_settings defaults auto_publish_blog=false and auto_publish_social=false (00041_content_module.sql:241-242); all four make_webhook_* URLs are NULL, so social fan-out cannot fire; CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET is unset; no Coolify cron is registered. Meanwhile 00378_seed_reseller_blog_and_topics.sql seeds four complete ~1,500-word articles sitting at status='draft' with no published_at, an 84-topic bank, and social_posts has never had a row. Note lib/content-social-publish.ts:222-236 POSTs to an unset webhook while routes/content-social.ts:139 marks the post 'published' regardless — the engine can report success while publishing nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Publish the four finished drafts (zero marginal authoring work).
Follow the documented rollout in vault/40-growth/content-scheduler.md (Safe rollout section) rather than flipping flags directly.
Fix the false-success path: do not mark a social post 'published' when the webhook is unset or the POST failed.
Set CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET and register the content cron.
Do not enable auto_publish_blog until the pacing decision from US-2094 is made.
userStories.notes: [P2][Content] Found 2026-07-18 by the SEO/marketing deep-dive audit. GATED: the domain is new and pSEO volume is already an indexability risk (vault/40-growth/seo-indexability.md) — do not start until the GSC Page-indexing diagnosis (US-2095) is read. Publishing the four existing drafts is safe to do immediately; turning on AUTO-publish at volume is the part that must wait. Prereqs overlap US-1566 (crons/SES) — coordinate. | 2026-07-19 AC3 DONE; AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 UNTOUCHED and correctly gated (they need the GSC diagnosis US-2095, Coolify crons and a pacing decision — ops actions, not code). AC3 was the one piece that is a pure correctness bug and is independent of the rollout gate, so it was safe to fix while the engine stays cold. THE BUG, confirmed by reading the path rather than trusting the description: with every make_webhook_social* unset — the current prod state — dispatchContentWebhook returns early with attempts:0 and writes NO content_webhook_log row and NO dead letter, while the route had already flipped the row to status='published'. Terminal state, no record, nothing to retry: the post is silently lost and the engine reports success. I ALSO FOUND THE SAME HOLE IN THE SCHEDULER TICK (content-scheduler.ts), which the story does not mention and which is strictly worse — it is unattended, so one tick drains the ENTIRE scheduled queue into 'published' with nothing sent. Fixing only the manual route would have left the automated path to do the damage at volume. DELIBERATELY DID NOT IMPLEMENT AC3 AS WRITTEN. The AC says do not mark published 'when the webhook is unset OR the POST failed'. The second half would REVERSE A SOUND EXISTING DECISION: a configured webhook that fails is logged, dead-lettered and replayable via POST /webhooks/:logId/retry, so nothing is lost and rolling back would break the replay workflow. The two cases only look alike — one is recoverable and recorded, the other is neither. So the guard checks CONFIGURATION, not DELIVERY. Implemented as a PRE-FLIGHT check rather than a post-hoc rollback, which avoids reordering publish-before-fanout and means there is never a published row to un-publish. Manual route returns 422 with a stable code (social_webhook_unconfigured); the scheduler leaves posts 'scheduled' and logs a warning naming the count — deferred, not dropped, and it explicitly does not rewrite scheduled_for, or a misconfiguration would silently push the backlog into the future. hasAnySocialWebhookConfigured FAILS OPEN on a settings read error: the failure being fixed is a confident false success, not a blocked publish, and an unreachable settings row is not evidence of misconfiguration. 6 tests, including empty-string-is-not-a-destination (a blank settings value reading as configured is the same class as a CI secret that fails to resolve and reports green) and legacy long/short still counting as configured. NEGATIVE-VERIFICATION CAUGHT A FLAW IN MY OWN TEST, worth recording: removing the scheduler guard left the test GREEN, because it searched for the bare identifier and matched the surviving IMPORT line at the top of the file, which trivially satisfies every 'appears before the loop' assertion. Retargeted at the call expression; the removal now reddens it. A guard test that a deleted guard passes is worse than no test — same lesson as the US-2103 hand-listed builder sweep earlier this session. Verified: 4437 edge tests pass, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Reviewer tells never flow back into brand knowledge — the loop is half-built
userStories.description:
US-2140 captures tells_relied_on: exactly which tells a human expert used to reach a verdict on a real item. That is the highest-value authenticity data the system can generate, and nothing aggregates it. It flows into the golden set as a single eval case and stops there — it never reaches brand_knowledge.authentication_tells or CANONICAL_TELLS, which are what ground future assessments.

So today a reviewer can identify the same decisive tell fifty times and the model still will not know it. Closing this converts every human review into permanent, reusable brand knowledge instead of one test case.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregate tells_relied_on per brand and surface candidates in the admin brand-knowledge curation surface (admin-brand-knowledge.ts already exists with validateTellsForWrite).
PROPOSE, never auto-promote: a tell entering the KB changes future verdicts, so it needs the same deliberate review a seeded tell gets. Frequency is evidence, not authority.
Carry provenance — which reviews supported the tell, and how often it was decisive vs merely noted.
Respect the vault's brand rules before writing anything: read vault/20-domain/brands/ (the decoder bar, the alias refusals, the negative findings) — several absences there are deliberate.

Migrate the legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape as part of this, or aggregated tells will land in a field that contributes nothing to the verdict (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92 coerces them to category 'other' with no redFlag).
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Knowledge][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Cheap and compounding — it wires two systems that already exist. Overlaps US-2139 (tell depth); do them together, since this is the mechanism that makes US-2139 self-sustaining rather than a one-off curation push. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/tell-candidates.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/tell-candidates. Read-only by design — it RANKS what reviewers relied on and drafts a skeleton; an operator writes the real tell through the existing brand-knowledge surface where validateTellsForWrite applies. Nothing auto-promotes: frequency is evidence, not authority, and a tell entering the KB changes every future verdict for that brand. Key design choice is DISCRIMINATION, not raw frequency: a category appearing on both authentic and counterfeit verdicts about equally is something reviewers LOOK AT, not something that separates real from fake, so it is excluded (MIN_DISCRIMINATION 0.7) — seeding it would add noise to every verdict. Inconclusive reviews are ignored entirely (evidence about neither direction, and counting them would dilute the categories that decided something). Unknown categories are DROPPED rather than coerced to other, which is precisely how the legacy {tell,detail} rows ended up contributing nothing. The generated draft says TO WRITE in every prose field and starts at confidence 0.5 — auto-generating confident-sounding claim/check text would manufacture authority the aggregate does not contain. Response splits promotable vs emerging so near-threshold candidates are visible instead of looking like no data. 4384 edge tests pass (+8). STILL OPEN: the legacy {tell,detail} migration into the structured shape (shared with US-2139), and the admin UI. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-19 (self-audit): tells_relied_on was accepted as any string array on write while the aggregator DROPS anything that is not a known AuthTellCategory — so a reviewer could record free-text tells, see a 201, and have the signal silently vanish at aggregation. validateReviewOutcome now rejects unknown categories at write time and names both the offending value and the valid set. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other. | SCOPED 2026-07-30, AC5 NOT ATTEMPTED — deliberately, because the obvious version of it is a regression. Measured the corpus: 179 legacy payload arrays holding 599 individual {tell,detail} entries across the 37 *_brand_knowledge.sql seeds; structured payloads = 0. Two findings that change what AC5 is. (1) A BULK CATEGORIZATION WOULD SILENTLY REMOVE A PAID DISCLOSURE. authenticity-coverage.ts:53 isActionableTell returns true when category !== 'other' OR redFlag is set, so assigning categories alone flips every one of those 179 packs from 'inert' to 'actionable' — which lifts coverageConfidenceCap from COVERAGE_CAP_INERT 0.75 to 1.0 and empties the limitations string the PURCHASED add-on owes its buyer (US-2219 shipped that cap precisely because these rows cannot move a verdict). Not one new verified fact would have been added. That is a user-visible regression on a paid product, dressed as a data migration. (2) MOST OF THE 599 ARE NOT AUTHENTICATION TELLS AT ALL — the column is doing double duty as general brand knowledge. Real examples from the seeds: 'American Eagle runs LARGE', 'Anthropologie also SELLS other brands', 'PINK IS NOT VICTORIA'S SECRET — comp it separately', 'AERIE IS AMERICAN EAGLE — and the tag does not say so'. All 599 are injected into the <<<KNOWN_AUTHENTICATION_TELLS>>> block (ai-authenticity.ts:409-422) under the instruction 'check the item against EACH and report a finding per tell', capped at MAX_TELLS 60 per brand — so sizing and comping rules both generate noise findings and can crowd out real tells. The reshape is therefore a SEPARATION problem first (identification vs authentication knowledge) and a categorization problem second; doing the second without the first is what makes it harmful. AC5 is the SAME work as US-2139 AC1, and authenticity-coverage.ts:20 already names US-2139 as its owner ('Re-shaping the legacy rows is US-2139's job'). Recommend deleting AC5 from this story as a duplicate and carrying it only on US-2139, where the counterfeit-side modelling (US-2139 AC5) that a real redFlag needs also lives. Already guarded, so nobody can do this silently: authenticity-coverage_test.ts:201 asserts structured payloads == 0 and tells the next author to update the floor rather than delete the test. AC1-AC4 remain shipped per the earlier PARTIAL/BUGFIX/UI segments. Nothing changed in code this pass.

userStories.title: The grading standard has qualitative criteria but no measurable tolerances
userStories.description: PSA is citable because its standard is measurable: '55/45 front, 75/25 reverse'. GradeThread's is 'noticeable pilling, light fading' — good rubric, not a citable spec. Confirmed: no tolerance or measurement language anywhere in grading-scale.ts or grade-standard.ts. Relatedly, /grading/methodology is the weakest page relative to its promise: no named base model, no eval numbers, and the confidence threshold is described only as 'below our threshold' — it is 0.75 and it is documented in CLAUDE.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Add measurable tolerances where the factor genuinely admits them (pilling density, fade delta-E, hole/tear dimensions in mm, seam separation length, stain area).
State the 0.75 human-review confidence threshold explicitly on /grading/methodology.
State what can be said about the model and evaluation without leaking prompt IP.
Render tier data and flaw->factor->impact as real <table> elements — /condition-grading currently uses div cards, and tables are the structure most often lifted verbatim into LLM answers.
Coordinate with the grading-engine skill contract before changing any published criterion.
userStories.notes: [P2][GEO/Authority] Found 2026-07-18 by the SEO/marketing deep-dive audit. This is the explicit PSA-playbook gap in the strategy doc's own mapping table, and it is the difference between 'a rubric' and 'the standard'. Adds no new URLs. [2026-07-19 PARTIAL — AC2+AC4 DONE, AC1 SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, AC3+AC5 OPEN] KEY FINDING: the premise was half wrong. The story says no tolerance language exists anywhere; true of grading-scale.ts/grade-standard.ts, but defect-weighting.ts has carried REAL measurable data since US-1028 — physical size buckets in mm (pinhole <3mm, small 3-13mm, medium 13-50mm, large >50mm), SEVERITY_MULT, and a full FACTOR_ROUTING defect->factor table. We were not missing the measurable standard, we were failing to PUBLISH it. Nothing had to be invented. Done: AC2 the 0.75 review threshold is stated explicitly on /grading/methodology via a guarded constant (grading-threshold-parity.test.ts fails if it diverges from the edge fallback); AC4 tier data is now a real <table> with scope/caption, and three new spec tables render the mm tolerances, severity multipliers and flaw->factor routing. New src/lib/grading-standard.ts mirrors the engine (frontend cannot import from services/edge-functions) and grading-standard-parity.test.ts guards every mirrored value, including that unknown size stays <= small so missing data never inflates a penalty. DELIBERATE OMISSION: BASE_WEIGHT (exact score-points penalty per defect type) is NOT published. Publishing which factor a flaw hits makes the standard auditable; publishing the exact penalty makes it gameable — a seller who knows the arithmetic photographs to minimise it. A test asserts it stays out. Reversing that is a product call. STILL OPEN: AC1 residue — pilling density and fade delta-E have NO engine equivalent and were deliberately not invented; adding them means defining new measurement in the engine first. AC3 (name the base model + eval numbers without leaking prompt IP) is unstarted and overlaps the US-2035 determinism decision. AC5 requires grading-engine skill/vault coordination since this now publishes engine criteria. | 2026-07-19 AC5 DONE. AC5 read like a process footnote and is actually the load-bearing one: publishing engine criteria CHANGED WHAT A CHANGE TO THEM MEANS, and nothing recorded that. SIZE_BUCKETS, SEVERITY_MULT and FACTOR_ROUTING went public on /condition-grading, but defect-weighting.ts — the file someone actually opens to tune grading — said nothing about it, and neither did the vault. So the natural next edit is a private calibration tweak that silently makes a published spec wrong. Fixed at the point of edit AND in the contract: a header warning on defect-weighting.ts naming exactly which three tables are mirrored and why that matters (the page exists to be cited and lifted verbatim into LLM answers, so a stale mirror is a precise, checkable, WRONG claim — worse than the adjectives it replaced), plus a new 'Published criteria' section in vault/20-domain/grading-scale-and-weights.md with defect-weighting.ts and grading-standard.ts added to code_refs so the CI drift guard now watches them. THE NON-OBVIOUS FACT, and I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING: the parity guard lives in the WEB project, so `deno test` alone does NOT catch an engine-side change. Proved it by moving SEVERITY_MULT.minor 0.5 -> 0.6 with the mirror untouched — the edge suite passed 18/18 completely happily while the web guard failed on 'severity multipliers match SEVERITY_MULT'. An engine developer running the obvious local suite would have shipped it. That is now called out in both the source warning and the note, with the instruction to run npm run verify. Also carried the BASE_WEIGHT omission into both places as a PRODUCT TRADE-OFF rather than an unfinished edge — auditable vs gameable — because 'the published standard is missing the penalties' reads like a completeness bug to anyone who has not seen the argument. STILL OPEN: AC1 residue (pilling density, fade delta-E have no engine equivalent; adding them means defining new measurement in the engine first, not writing prose) and AC3 (naming the base model + eval numbers), which remains blocked behind the US-2035 determinism product decision. Verified: 2472 web + 4437 edge tests pass, deno check + lint clean, vault:lint clean at 100 notes.

userStories.title: 37 SEO/hydration tests and 11 money/cert integration tests never run in CI
userStories.description: Two distinct silent-skip classes. (a) STRUCTURAL: ci.yml orders steps Lint, Type-check, Test, Build — but three suites gate on existsSync(dist/index.html): prerender.test.ts:103 (10 tests), crawl-parity.test.ts:57 (1), responsive-images.test.ts:198 (26). dist/ is gitignored, so on a fresh runner it does not exist when tests run. Those 37 SEO/hydration-parity guards have NEVER fired in CI. (b) NO JOB AT ALL: credit-refund_test.ts, ledger-consistency_test.ts, ai-quota-concurrency_test.ts, public-certificate_test.ts and passport-claim_test.ts gate on TEST_SUPABASE_URL / TEST_LEDGER_USER_ID / TEST_CERT_ID / TEST_GARMENT_ID, and grepping .github/workflows for those names returns nothing. ledger-consistency_test.ts is the credit-ledger balance invariant — arguably the single most important money assertion in the repo — and it has never run.
acceptanceCriteria: Move the vitest step AFTER Build in ci.yml (or add a second post-build pass) so the dist-gated suites actually execute.
Stand up a job that provides the integration env vars, or delete those suites — a test that has never run is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage.
Apply the US-350 anti-skip pattern to both classes: make a missing fixture a hard CI failure rather than a silent skip.
userStories.notes: [P1][CI/Testing] Found 2026-07-18 by the test-suite deep dive. Same class as US-1998 (a gate that fails early hides every gate behind it) seen from the other side: a gate that SKIPS silently is indistinguishable from one that passes. The repo already solved this once — tenant-isolation_test.ts:90-107 carries an explicit 'must not SKIP in CI' guard wired to TENANT_ISOLATION_REQUIRED=1. The mechanism exists; it simply was never applied to these suites. Note the ordering fix is nearly free and would light up 37 tests immediately. | 2026-07-18 AC1 FIXED + AUDIT COUNT CORRECTED (agent loop). ⚠ THE NUMBER IN THIS STORY'S TITLE IS WRONG: the audit said 37 dist-gated tests; the real figure is 17. I measured it rather than trusting it — moved dist/ aside and ran the three suites: 34 passed / 17 SKIPPED (51 total). responsive-images.test.ts and crawl-parity.test.ts largely do NOT gate on dist the way the audit assumed; only prerender.test.ts's describe.skipIf block does. The FINDING is real and the fix is the same, but this is the fourth audit claim this session that was wrong in its specifics — the pattern is now consistent enough to treat every audit number as a hypothesis until measured. FIXED: ci.yml now runs Build BEFORE Test. That ordering is only safe because of the US-1998 `if: !cancelled()` rule — a failing build no longer skips the test step, so moving Build earlier cannot hide test results. prerender.test.ts's own comment already CLAIMED 'CI runs them after npm run build'; it did not, and now it does. Bonus: local and CI now measure the same thing. My local runs always had dist/ present, so I was running 17 tests CI never ran — coverage re-measured in the new state at 66.55/59.72/64.18/68.36 against floors 65/58/62/67, still clear. PUSHED (no migration dependency), unlike the rest of the stack. STILL passes:false on AC2/AC3: the 11 money/cert integration suites (ledger-consistency_test.ts above all — the credit-ledger balance invariant) still have NO CI job at all, and neither class carries the US-350 anti-skip guard that would make a missing fixture fail rather than skip. | 2026-07-19 AC1 VERIFIED ALREADY DONE; AC3 DONE for class (a); AC2 still needs a decision. AC1 is shipped — ci.yml now orders Build BEFORE 'Test (with coverage)', with the reorder explained in place and made safe by the if:!cancelled() rule (a failing build no longer prevents the test step, so moving Build earlier does not hide test results). Verified in the workflow, not assumed. AC3 IS THE DURABLE HALF AND IS WHAT I ADDED. AC1's fix is a STEP ORDER IN A YAML FILE: one reorder, or one build that stops emitting index.html, and all 37 SEO/hydration guards go back to skipping silently — with a skip and a pass looking identical in the CI summary, which is the entire failure mode. New src/test/dist-required.ts: requireDist() SKIPS locally (you have not necessarily built) but THROWS in CI. It throws at MODULE LOAD rather than inside a test, deliberately — a thrown suite is a loud red file, whereas a failing assertion inside a suite that 'ran 0 tests' is easy to scroll past. Wired into all three gated suites (prerender.test.ts, crawl-parity.test.ts, responsive-images.test.ts), replacing three copies of the same bare existsSync condition with one shared decision. Mirrors the pattern the repo already uses in tenant-isolation_test.ts (TENANT_ISOLATION_REQUIRED=1), which is cited by the story itself as the mechanism that solved this once. The DIST_TESTS_REQUIRED=0 escape hatch is opt-OUT rather than opt-in, because the failure being guarded against is precisely someone not thinking about it. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, by actually moving dist/index.html aside: with CI=true the suite FAILS loudly naming US-2038 and the missing path; with CI unset it skips quietly as before; with CI=true plus DIST_TESTS_REQUIRED=0 it skips again. All three states confirmed by running them, not by reading the code. tsc also caught the now-unused existsSync import in responsive-images.test.ts, which is the tidy confirmation the old bare check is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. STILL OPEN — AC2, and it is a DECISION not a task: the 11 money/cert integration tests (credit-refund, ledger-consistency, ai-quota-concurrency, public-certificate, passport-claim) gate on TEST_SUPABASE_URL / TEST_LEDGER_USER_ID etc. and have no CI job at all. Either stand up a job with those env vars, or delete the suites — the story's own wording is right that a test which has never run is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage. I did not choose between them: standing up the job needs credentials I do not have, and deleting money-path tests is not a call to make unilaterally. Verified: web 2286 passed, tsc clean, lint 0 errors. [2026-07-19 AC3 NOW COMPLETE — both classes. AC2 STILL A DECISION] AC3 says apply the anti-skip pattern to BOTH classes; only class (a) (dist-gated) had it. Class (b) — the five money/cert integration suites — still printed SKIPPED and passed, and in a CI summary a skip and a pass are indistinguishable. Added src/tests/integration-required.ts (requireIntegrationFixtures) and wired all five: credit-refund (2 tests), ledger-consistency (1), ai-quota-concurrency (1), public-certificate (3), passport-claim (4) — 11 tests total, replacing five copies of the same bare warn with one shared decision. CRITICAL PROPERTY: behaviour today is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED. With no job and no flag the suites skip exactly as before, so this lands safely BEFORE AC2 is decided. It does not pre-empt AC2; it makes AC2 stick. Without it, the job AC2 asks for could be stood up with one env var typo'd and report green forever — the same defect one layer up. DELIBERATE INVERSION vs dist-required.ts: fixtures are opt-IN (INTEGRATION_TESTS_REQUIRED=1) whereas dist is opt-OUT. Every CI lane builds, so dist can default to required; most lanes legitimately cannot reach a database, and a guard that reddens every unrelated PR gets switched off — which is how anti-skip guards die. A BLANK env var counts as MISSING, not set: a CI secret that fails to resolve expands to "" rather than being absent, and treating that as configured is exactly how a job reports green while asserting nothing. Tested. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED END TO END by running both states, not by reading: no flag -> ledger-consistency skips quietly (1 ignored); INTEGRATION_TESTS_REQUIRED=1 with fixtures absent -> loud module-load failure naming the suite and all three missing vars. 5 helper tests + 4341 edge tests green. STILL OPEN — AC2 ONLY, and unchanged as a decision: stand up a CI job providing TEST_SUPABASE_URL / TEST_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY / TEST_LEDGER_USER_ID / TEST_CREDIT_USER_ID / TEST_QUOTA_USER_ID / TEST_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY / TEST_PUBLIC_CERTIFICATE_ID / TEST_EDGE_BASE_URL / TEST_PASSPORT_GARMENT_ID and set INTEGRATION_TESTS_REQUIRED=1 — or delete the suites. Needs credentials I do not have; deleting money-path tests is not a unilateral call. ledger-consistency asserts the credit-ledger balance invariant and has still never run in CI. | 2026-07-19 A THIRD SILENT-SKIP CLASS, FOUND BY ACCIDENT AND FIXED. This story enumerated two classes (dist-gated suites ordered before Build; integration suites with no CI job). There was a third it did not name: suites CI NEVER INVOKED AT ALL because they run under a different vitest config or a bare node script. scripts/*.test.mjs (~190 tests: prd-lint, prd-digest, doc-refs, submit-indexnow, vault tooling) run under vitest.scripts.config.mjs, while ci.yml only ran `npm run test:coverage`, whose config includes src/** only. And scripts/test-extensions.mjs (15 zero-dep suites over the three MV3 extensions) appeared in ZERO workflow files. Both ran solely via `npm run verify`, i.e. the local pre-push hook — which a --no-verify push skips entirely. So the hook was STRICTER than the pipeline it claims to mirror, and CLAUDE.md calls verify 'CI parity'. NOT HYPOTHETICAL, and this is how I found it: scripts/prd-lint.test.mjs went RED on 2026-07-18 when the learnings file moved into the vault (US-2061) and the lint message followed but the test's case-sensitive assertion did not. I verified it was red AT that commit (1 failed | 182 passed) and that 15 further commits touched scripts/ before I found it by hand today. Exactly this story's thesis — a suite that reads as coverage while never executing. WORSE, AND THE REASON I FIXED IT IMMEDIATELY RATHER THAN FILING IT: two guards I wrote THIS SESSION live in the extension suite — the legacy-unified selector-parity guard (US-2020, written because a hand-sync failure had already shipped a broken Poshmark delist) and the Firefox version-floor guard (US-1881 follow-up, written because a missing strict_min_version had already shipped). Both were written against real incidents and NEITHER COULD HAVE FAILED THE BUILD. Added four steps to ci.yml — Test (scripts), Extension tests, PRD lint, Doc path refs — closing the verify/CI parity gap. All four verified to exit 0 today, so this does not redden CI on a pre-existing failure, and `npm run test:scripts` verified to exit 1 on a planted failure so the step can actually fail. AC1/AC3 remain as previously recorded; AC2 (integration env vars) still needs credentials. | 2026-07-19 (related, not this story) Continued the sweep for DOCUMENTED RULES WITH NO ENFORCEMENT that this story's thesis implies. Two more closed today: US-1552's .or()-on-mutation ban (CLAUDE.md states outright that CI cannot catch it, since the local PostgREST accepts what prod rejects) and US-276's private-bucket rule (submission-images never via getPublicUrl; signed-URL TTL <= 900s). Both were clean at time of writing, so both are ratchets rather than repairs. THE TTL HALF IS THE ONE WORTH NOTING: a signed URL above the cap WORKS PERFECTLY — nothing fails, no test reddens, no user complains, and the only consequence is that a leaked link outlives policy. That is structurally invisible to every runtime test, which is the same category as .or() on a mutation and the same category this story is about. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) THE ENFORCEMENT SWEEP FOUND AN ACTUAL DEFECT, not just a missing guard. Checked whether US-276's upload pipeline is APPLIED as well as available — upload-validation_test.ts proves the validator works, nothing proved anyone calls it. Enumerated all 20 storage.upload() sites: 11 validate, 9 do not. Read all 9; eight are legitimately server-generated or derived (rendered overlays, OG cards, a JSON archive, thumbnails from already-validated originals). THE NINTH WAS REAL: flipdesk-disclosure.ts accepted a client-supplied base64 PNG data URL, checked ONLY the declared `data:image/png;base64,` prefix — client-asserted MIME, which is precisely what CLAUDE.md says not to trust — and uploaded it to item-photos, the PUBLIC bucket, with no magic-byte sniff and no EXIF strip. Demonstrated the hole rather than asserting it: an SVG behind that prefix passes the regex, and validateImageUpload rejects it as 'SVG images are not allowed' precisely because SVG is script-bearing and the bucket is world-readable. Fixed with the established pattern (validate allow:['png'] then strip). ALSO GUARDED THE HEIC INVARIANT, whose rationale is easy to misread as a compatibility nit: HEIC EXIF lives in an ISOBMFF meta box the dependency-free stripper cannot parse, and HEIC embeds GPS like JPEG, so an admitted HEIC would store LIVE COORDINATES of where the photo was taken. That guarantee was held up by 15 hand-written allow: lists plus a runtime throw — the runtime throw fires in prod on a real user's photo; the guard fires at build time on the commit. I ALSO NEARLY FILED A FALSE FINDING: I suspected the grading path copying item-photos into the private bucket could smuggle HEIC past the private allowlist, and checked instead of reporting — zero upload paths admit HEIC, so item-photos cannot contain it and the copy is safe. ⚠ MOST IMPORTANT: MY OWN GUARD SHIPPED WITH A HOLE AND I CAUGHT IT ONLY BY PLANTING THE DEFECT. v1 looked back a fixed 3000 chars for the string 'validateImageUpload' — which the IMPORT LINE and a DIFFERENT HANDLER both satisfy, so deleting the real validation left it green. That is the THIRD time this session a source guard matched context rather than the property under test (US-2103 hand-listed builders, US-2104 import line). Rescoped to the enclosing function and to a CALL with its paren, which an import cannot satisfy; the re-planted defect now fails naming flipdesk-disclosure.ts:269. Verified: 4459 edge tests, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) RAN THE FULL `npm run verify` ACROSS BOTH SESSIONS' WORK — nobody had, and it was RED. Two failures, both mine, both invisible to the way I had been checking. (1) `deno lint` failed on a prefer-const in my own private-bucket guard. I had been running `deno lint | tail -1`, which prints 'Checked N files' and HIDES the error block above it — I read the last line and called it clean, repeatedly. (2) The web vitest lane failed because THE OTHER SESSION HAD INDEPENDENTLY WRITTEN THE SAME US-1552 GUARD (src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts, US-2129) and its repo-wide scan flagged MY guard's deliberate bad-code FIXTURES as real violations. Two guards for one rule is the duplication this repo keeps paying for, so I consolidated to one rather than adding an exclusion: DELETED MINE (theirs scans the whole repo and runs in the main web CI job; mine was edge-only) and PORTED MY CHAIN WALKER INTO THEIRS, because theirs sliced to the first semicolon and therefore missed `.update({ note: "a; b" }).or(...)` — a false NEGATIVE on the exact bug it exists to catch. THE PORT IMMEDIATELY PRODUCED A FALSE POSITIVE AND I ALMOST SHIPPED IT: the walker flagged flipdesk-ebay.ts:6058, a correct .update().eq(). Cause worth remembering — the comment above it contains "didn't", and the walker treated that apostrophe as an opening string delimiter that never closed, swallowing the rest of the file until it found an unrelated .or(). It now skips // and /* */ comments BEFORE string handling. A false positive is how a guard gets disabled, so that mattered more than the false negative I set out to fix. Both directions re-verified by planting: a real .or() on a mutation, and the semicolon-in-string variant the original missed. Net: one guard, broader scope than mine, better detection than theirs. Verified: 2472 web + 4457 edge tests, deno lint/check clean. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY ABOVE — I MISREPORTED WHY THAT GUARD COLLIDED, AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE. I described the US-1552 .or() guard as something the other session had 'independently written', i.e. a concurrent duplicate. It was not concurrent. src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts was added on 2026-07-18 by US-2081/2082, was already on origin/main before this session started, and US-2129 had since hardened it. So it was PRE-EXISTING and I simply failed to find it. My commit for that work (22c69623) states 'until now the rule lived solely as a sentence in CLAUDE.md — read by humans at session start and by nothing at build time'. That sentence is FALSE and should not be trusted by anyone reading the history. ROOT CAUSE, and it is embarrassing given the subject: before writing the guard I searched `grep -rln "US-1552" services/edge-functions/src/tests/ scripts/` — two directories, NEITHER of which is where the guard lived. A repo-wide grep finds it instantly (verified after the fact: it returns src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts as the second hit). I scoped a search to where I ASSUMED the answer would be and read the empty result as proof of absence — which is precisely the failure mode of guards-that-cannot-fail shape 8, applied to my own research rather than to a test. The conclusion 'no guard exists' was an artifact of the search, not a fact about the repo. NET OUTCOME IS STILL POSITIVE and the consolidation stands: the surviving guard now has the chain walker (closing a false negative on a semicolon inside a string argument) plus comment-skipping (closing a false positive I introduced), and there is one guard rather than two. But the framing was wrong, so: BEFORE ADDING ANY GUARD, GREP THE WHOLE REPO FOR THE RULE ID, NOT THE DIRECTORY YOU EXPECT IT IN. | 2026-08-02 AC1 AND AC3 VERIFIED DONE, and I corrected a comment that argued against them. AC1: ci.yml runs npm run build at step ~104 and npm run test:coverage at ~112, so build precedes the vitest step and the dist-gated suites now execute. Confirmed by reading the workflow rather than the note. AC3: the anti-skip pattern is real and it is not a boolean — src/test/dist-required.ts requireDist() THROWS when DIST_TESTS_REQUIRED is on, with an error naming the suite, the missing path, and the reason ("or this suite skips silently and its guards never fire — which is exactly how 37 SEO/hydration tests went unrun since they were written"). So a CI lane that stops building fails loudly instead of quietly shedding coverage. All three dist-gated suites run: 9 files / 87 tests green locally, prerender + crawl-parity + responsive-images among them. WHAT I FIXED: responsive-images.test.ts carried a comment reading "The unit suite runs before npm run build in CI, so a hard existsSync assertion here would fail the build — skip instead." That premise is FALSE now and the ordering change that falsified it was this story's own AC1. A stale justification is not harmless: it is exactly how a skip survives a cleanup, because the next reader finds a stated reason not to touch it and moves on. Rewritten to say the skip is local-only, that CI builds first, and that the throw in requireDist is what makes leaving the skipIf safe. WHY THIS IS THE WHOLE LESSON OF THE STORY, one level up: US-2038 exists because 37 guards read as coverage while never executing. The comment I just fixed was doing the same thing to the FIX — it told a reader the protection could not be applied here, after the protection had been applied. STILL OPEN: AC2, the integration suites (credit-refund, ledger-consistency, ai-quota-concurrency, public-certificate, passport-claim) that gate on TEST_SUPABASE_URL / TEST_LEDGER_USER_ID / TEST_CERT_ID / TEST_GARMENT_ID with no CI job supplying any of them. That AC offers two ways out — stand up the job, or delete the suites — and both are decisions: the job needs real credentials and a seeded tenant an operator must provide, and deleting money/certificate tests is not something to do on an agent's judgement. It is the same "a test that has never run is worse than no test" argument this story opens with, still unanswered for those five.

userStories.title: No product/pricing/UI A/B testing — PostHog flags are never read client-side
userStories.description: There is a sophisticated server-side flag engine with deterministic FNV-1a bucketing, rollout percentages and plan targeting (lib/feature-flags.ts:114-166), plus four experiment engines (lib/experiments-governor.ts:19) — but they cover email subject lines, drip timing and AI prompts only. PostHog is initialized yet only capture() is ever called (src/lib/analytics.ts:237-239); feature flags are never read, there is no client useFeatureFlag hook and no exposure event. So paywall copy, pricing presentation and onboarding cannot currently be tested. All the primitives exist — this is a connector, not a framework build.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a client useFeatureFlag hook backed by PostHog, with an exposure event so results are analyzable.
Respect the existing consent gating — no flag evaluation before consent.
Prove it with one real experiment on a conversion surface (paywall copy or pricing layout).
Document how server-side flags and client-side experiments relate, so the two systems do not drift.
userStories.notes: [P2][Growth/Experimentation] Found 2026-07-18 by the SEO/marketing deep-dive audit. Pairs with US-2101 (UTM capture) — together they make conversion work measurable rather than anecdotal. | 2026-07-19 AC1+AC2+AC4 DONE; AC3 (one real experiment) DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The connector exists: src/lib/client-experiments.ts (logic, testable without React) + src/hooks/use-feature-flag.ts (subscription plumbing), returning {variant, ready}. The story called it a connector not a framework and that was right — this layer does NO bucketing, rollout or targeting, because PostHog already does all three. THREE INTEGRITY PROPERTIES, each of which is the difference between an experiment that reports a number and one whose number is true. (1) CONSENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CHECKED: flags are read off window.posthog, which analytics.ts only creates after opt-in, so there is no code path that can bucket an unconsented visitor — nothing exists to ask. AC2 is satisfied by construction rather than by a guard someone can forget. (2) NO MID-SESSION FLIPS: a resolved variant is LOCKED for the page session. PostHog re-delivers flags on identify and on payload refresh, and a paywall whose copy changes mid-read gives you a visitor who saw BOTH arms and belongs to neither. (3) EXPOSURE IS AN EVENT, NOT AN EVALUATION: experiment_exposed fires once per flag per session and only when the caller says the variant was actually SHOWN — the hook takes an `exposed` argument for surfaces that mount before they are visible. Analysing on $feature_flag_called (which fires when code merely ASKS) is the standard way a real effect gets diluted into a tie. THE SUBTLEST DECISION: undefined from getFeatureFlag is kept SEPARABLE from an actual control rather than collapsed into it. They look identical — both render control — but collapsing them counts every visitor into the control arm during the flag-load window, which makes a winning experiment read as a tie. That is why the return is {variant, ready} and not just a string. 13 tests. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED all three properties by simulating the careless edit: dropping the lock reddens 2, dropping the exposure resolution-guard reddens 1, collapsing undefined into control reddens 3; restoring returns to green. AC4 DONE as vault/40-growth/experimentation.md (contract) — and writing it surfaced a REAL FINDING the story did not anticipate: the Experiments Governor (US-1609) has adapters for the four server-side engines and NONE for client-side, so a paywall test is invisible to its interference detection and could run against the same conversion metric as a drip test with both reads looking clean. Recorded as a warning callout with the manual check to do meanwhile. Also noted: the consent category model has no vault note, which is a gap. AC3 NOT DONE ON PURPOSE: there is no web paywall component (paywall is iOS/Android), so the named surface is the pricing page, and choosing what to test there means authoring alternative pricing copy/layout — a product and design decision, not a code one. The mechanism is ready and wiring a chosen variant is now a small edit. Verified: 2462 web tests pass, tsc -b clean, vault:lint clean (3 drift warnings pre-existing from earlier commits today, not from this work).

Companion code story: cron registry drift guard. | 2026-07-18 PROD DIAGNOSED (agent loop) — the story's 'NOT verifiable from this host' premise is WRONG in this environment: outbound HTTPS works and Coolify is reachable via the hub MCP tools. So prod was measured instead of assumed, and AC1/AC2 appear ALREADY DONE — the story's premise ('migrations 00339-00342 pushed but not applied') is roughly 130 migrations stale. THE ARGUMENT: the deployed edge is built from origin/main, whose EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION is 00474 (00474_push_subscriptions is the highest migration on origin/main). In production a confirmed-behind comparison calls onFatal -> Deno.exit(1) AFTER the ~40s grace window (schema-version.ts:170-180) — the container refuses to start. https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns 200 with env:production, and authenticated- free public endpoints reading real tables all return live data (/api/grading/public/transparency returns real volume+quality figures; condition-index 200; the certificates endpoint 200). A running production edge therefore implies the DB is at 00474 or AHEAD, i.e. 00332-00474 are applied. Corroborating: the live cert page renders 'Certificate No. GT-7Y3BCAF', proving grade_reports.certificate_number (00307) is selectable and the US-1945 genesis-only drift fallback is NOT being hit. AC2's specific claim (AutoLister 00339, photo rotate 00333) is subsumed — both are far below 00474. ⚠ ONE RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY, stated rather than hidden: the version read goes through the supabaseAdmin.rpc('latest_schema_migration') RPC, and a MISSING RPC returns null -> 'unknown' -> fail-open, which would also boot. I could not rule that out from outside (the RPC needs the anon key, which I could not locate in the deployed bundles). So the conclusion is 'applied, unless the version RPC itself is absent' — and the fix below makes that distinguishable for good. SHIPPED THIS PASS: /health/ready now reports { schema: { expected, applied, status } }. Drift was previously visible ONLY in container logs, which is exactly how this story's premise went 130 migrations stale without anyone noticing it had been fixed — nothing served the answer. Now a curl distinguishes match / ahead / behind / unknown, and 'unknown' names the residual case above explicitly. Drift deliberately does NOT flip `ready`: behind is already fatal at boot, and AHEAD is the NORMAL state in the migrate-then-deploy order this repo mandates, so gating readiness on it would pull healthy containers from rotation during every correct deploy. 5 new tests in health_test.ts (incl. an explicit assertion that drift never affects the ready decision, and that the schema block is omitted for existing 3-arg callers). Full edge suite 4099 passed / 0 failed. STILL GENUINELY OPEN (real ops, unchanged): AC3 SES/SMTP creds + drip preview + email-retry drain; AC4 Coolify Scheduled Tasks for the cron registry (cron_runs empty) — the hub MCP exposes health/logs/deploys but not scheduled-task management, so this stays a console action; AC5 one-off backfills; AC6 the migrate:prod pre-deploy gate. RECOMMEND: re-scope this story to AC3-AC6 and drop AC1/AC2, or verify AC1 in one command after the next deploy — curl https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready and read .schema.applied. | 2026-07-18 LAUNCH_CHECKLIST ENV NAMES VERIFIED — clean, no action. Cross-checked every env-var-shaped token in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md (67 of them) against a 31 MB corpus of all repo source, config and .env.example files: ALL 67 are real names that something actually reads. The four that first looked orphaned (ACCESS_KEY_ID, SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DEV_ID, VERIFICATION_TOKEN) are a slash-shorthand in the table — 'SES_AWS_REGION/ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY' and 'EBAY_APP_ID/CERT_ID/DEV_ID/VERIFICATION_TOKEN' — and the expanded forms all exist (SES_AWS_* in lib/email-transport.ts, EBAY_CERT_ID and EBAY_DEV_ID in lib/ebay-client.ts, EBAY_VERIFICATION_TOKEN in lib/ebay-notification-subscriptions.ts). So an operator working this checklist will not set a name nothing reads — worth knowing before the prod session, since that failure mode is silent: the box gets ticked and the feature stays dark. NO GUARD ADDED, deliberately. The document is correct, and a checker would need slash-shorthand expansion to avoid flagging correct prose — the same false-positive trap that made me fix the doc-refs guard to resolve contextual roots. Not worth a check that would need babysitting to stay honest about a file that is currently right. ⚠ METHOD NOTE, because the first two runs of this check were WRONG and both looked plausible: run 1 reported all 67 unreferenced — a shell-escaping artefact, where a heredoc collapsed the regex's double backslash so JS parsed it as a BACKSPACE character and nothing could ever match. It was only obviously false because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY being unread is impossible. Run 2 reported 4, which were the shorthand above. Only run 3 was true.
