userStories.title: Returns and Disputes: refunds are all-or-nothing and there is no closed/history view
userStories.description: As a reseller handling returns, I want to issue a partial refund and review resolved cases, so I can offer keep-it discounts and audit past outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: refundReturn in src/pages/flipdesk/post-sale.tsx accepts a refund amount and issues a partial refund through the existing eBay post-order refund edge route, not only a full refund
A partial refund amount is validated to be greater than 0 and no more than the order total
Each of the three cards (disputes, returns, cancellations) gains a closed/resolved view showing past outcomes, not only open items
A test asserts a partial-refund request sends the entered amount to the edge route
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC3 DONE for Returns, and it turned out to be a DEFECT rather than a missing view. The card fetched every return eBay returned, applied NO filter, rendered them all with Approve / Decline / Refund buttons, and said "No open returns." when the list was empty. So a case eBay had already closed was indistinguishable from one waiting on the seller — with a destructive action attached whose own confirm text reads "This issues a refund to the buyer on eBay immediately. This can't be undone." The edge degrades gracefully (isAlreadyResolved swallows eBay's rejection) so this was not losing money; it was showing a seller work that did not exist and hiding the work that did among it. SHIPPED: NEW src/pages/flipdesk/post-sale-state.ts with isClosedCase / splitByOpenState, the returns card split into open/closed with a toggle that only appears when there IS history, and the action row hidden on closed cases. THE CLASSIFIER IS A SUBSTRING MATCH, NOT AN ENUM, and that is deliberate: eBay's Post-Order state vocabulary is not published anywhere in this repo — the only values recorded are three examples in an ebay-postorder.ts comment — so an exhaustive enum would be guessing, and a guessed enum fails SILENTLY the first time eBay sends something unanticipated. THE DEFAULT IS OPEN, and the asymmetry is the whole design: mis-classifying an open case as closed HIDES work the seller must do before an eBay deadline with no way to discover it; mis-classifying a closed case as open shows one extra row whose buttons become a no-op. The first costs a case, the second costs a glance. THE ONE TRAP IN THE WORD LIST, pinned by its own test: REFUND is deliberately NOT a terminal marker on its own, because REFUND_OVERDUE is an OPEN case and the most urgent kind there is — a refund the seller owes and has not issued. Matching the bare word would bury exactly the row that most needs action. AC1/AC2/AC4 NOT DONE, and the reason is a finding rather than effort. AC1 says refundReturn should issue a partial refund "through the existing eBay post-order refund edge route". There are TWO routes and they are different eBay flows: /returns/:returnId/refund calls issueReturnRefund(ownerId, returnId, comments) and takes NO amount — eBay's return-refund closes the return in full — while /orders/:orderId/refund is the partial/proactive one (US-1978) and already accepts amount and line_items. So the capability exists, but on the ORDER, and US-1978's own header says it is for refunds "outside any return case", written for the seller who wanted to make it right without pushing the buyer into opening a return. Using it to settle an OPEN return is outside its designed use, and whether eBay permits an order-level partial refund while a return case is open is not knowable from this checkout. Getting that wrong moves money incorrectly, possibly twice. That needs an answer about eBay's semantics before it is a UI change, and I did not guess it. AC3 for cancellations and payment disputes is left too — the helper reads `status` as well as `state` precisely so one rule covers all three cards, so wiring them is small, but each needs its own look at which actions must disappear on a closed case. VERIFIED: 8 new classifier tests, 108 flipdesk tests pass, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors. | 2026-08-02 AC3 NOW COMPLETE — all three cards. Disputes and cancellations had the IDENTICAL defect to Returns, which is the part worth recording: this was not one card someone forgot to filter, it was the same mistake made three times independently, because each card was written to answer "what needs my attention" and each one shipped the raw list instead. On Payment disputes it was the worst of the three: Accept & refund and Contest rendered against a respond-by deadline that had already passed, on a dispute eBay had already decided — Accept refunds the buyer, and Contest is meaningless once a decision exists. On Cancellations, Approve & cancel and Reject on a request already settled. Both now split open/closed with the same toggle, both hide their action rows on closed cases, and both empty states say which view is empty. The classifier needed no change to cover them, which is why it reads `status` as well as `state` — disputes carry the former, returns and cancellations the latter, and one rule across all three is the only way they stay consistent as eBay's vocabulary shifts. THE TOGGLE ONLY APPEARS WHEN THERE IS HISTORY, on all three: a "Show closed (0)" button teaches nothing and adds a control to a card whose whole job is to be scannable. STILL OPEN ON THIS STORY: AC1, AC2 and AC4, all three about partial refunds, and blocked on the eBay-semantics question recorded in the previous note rather than on effort — the return-refund route takes no amount, and the order-refund route that does is documented as being for refunds outside any return case. VERIFIED: full web suite 247 files / 3150 tests 0 failed, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors.

userStories.title: Expenses: no edit, no receipt upload, no recurring entries
userStories.description: As a reseller doing bookkeeping, I want to edit an expense, attach a receipt, and mark an expense recurring, so I can fix mistakes and keep an audit trail without re-logging monthly costs by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/flipdesk/expenses.tsx gains an edit action for an existing expense (today it is only add plus delete, lines 101-123)
An expense can attach a receipt image or PDF stored per-user via the hardened upload path (validateImageUpload then stripImageMetadata) and the row shows it
An expense can be marked recurring monthly and the system auto-creates the next entry
The list gains category and date-range filters
If a column or table is added for receipts or recurrence, the migration follows the US-1108 triple (idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer)
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC1 AND AC4 DONE, no migration needed. AC5 therefore does not apply yet. AC1: AddExpenseDialog becomes ExpenseDialog with an optional `expense` prop — null adds, non-null edits. ONE dialog rather than two, deliberately: a second would have duplicated the amount validation and the manage_inventory permission check, and bookkeeping is precisely where those must not drift. An edit path that skipped the permission check would let a workspace member rewrite the owner's numbers; one that skipped the amount check would accept a typo the add path rejects. The update sends only category/amount/description/spent_on and NOT user_id — the row's owner never changes and RLS scopes the update by it, so including it would create a way to move a row between workspaces that nothing here should have. The seeding effect keys on the dialog OPENING rather than on `expense` alone, because reopening the add form after an edit has to clear the previous row's values and `expense` going null is not on its own distinguishable from a re-render. AC4: category select plus inclusive from/to date inputs. The comparison is STRING comparison on purpose — spent_on is a plain yyyy-mm-dd date column and the date inputs emit the same format, so no parsing and no timezone to get wrong. Both bounds inclusive, which is what "the 1st to the 31st" means to someone doing a month's books. THREE DECISIONS THE AC DID NOT SPECIFY, each recorded in the code: (1) the monthly summary and the all-time card now compute over the FILTERED rows, because a summary showing the all-time figure beside a filtered table WILL be read as the filtered total — the card relabels to "Filtered total" so the two readings cannot be confused. (2) CSV export follows the filter, since exporting a narrowed view is the main reason to narrow it. (3) the empty state SPLITS: "no expenses match these filters" offers Clear, "no expenses logged" offers Add. Showing the log-an-expense state to someone whose filter matched nothing answers a question they did not ask, and worse, reads as though their existing expenses are gone. AC2 (receipt upload) and AC3 (recurring) both need schema — flipdesk_expenses (00019) has category, description, amount, spent_on and nothing else — plus, for AC2, a storage bucket decision: receipts are FINANCIAL documents with names and addresses on them, so they belong in a private bucket behind signed URLs, not in item-photos, and the hardened server path the AC names (validateImageUpload then stripImageMetadata) is the edge upload route, which expenses do not currently use at all — the page talks to supabase directly. That is a real piece of work, not a column. A MISTAKE I MADE AND CAUGHT: I typed a stray non-ASCII character into the empty-state edit ("țicon"). The build caught it immediately; noting it because a scripted multi-line edit is exactly where that kind of thing survives review. VERIFIED: build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 836 tests pass across the flipdesk and lib suites.

userStories.description: As a reseller reading the MeasureCard page, I want a button into the measure tool and a sample of the finished result, so the page leads to the capability it describes instead of dead-ending.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/flipdesk/measure-card.tsx adds a primary CTA linking into the item measure surface
The page shows a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo
The mailed-card status surfaces an ETA and, once shipped, a tracking number (today only a date, lines 199-206)
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC1 DONE; AC2 and AC3 recorded as blocked with the reason, not attempted. AC1: measure-card.tsx gains a "Measure an item" card with a primary CTA into /dashboard/flipdesk/inventory?status=cataloged. THE DIAGNOSIS BEHIND THE FIX, because the story's title undersells it: every control on that page produced an ARTEFACT — a PDF to print, a card to be mailed — and not one of them led to the thing the artefact is FOR. A seller who read the whole page still had to already know that measuring happens on an item, and where to find one. That is the specific shape of "brochure": not missing content, missing a next step. TWO CHOICES IN THE LINK WORTH STATING. It points at ?status=cataloged rather than the inventory root, so the seller lands on pre-listed items — the set that actually needs measuring — instead of their entire catalog; statusParamToTab folds cataloged / measured / photographed into the To-list tab, so one status param reaches the right view. And it uses ?status= rather than ?tab= deliberately: status is the documented EXTERNAL entry point that the Overview pipeline grid and the Kanban "+N more" links already use, tab is the table's internal view key, and the mapping function exists precisely so external links survive a tab rename. AC2 NOT DONE — it asks for a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo. That is an image asset. Producing it needs the measure pipeline run against a real garment with a real card in frame, and a judgement about whose item is safe to show publicly. Same class as US-1949 AC1: a human with the product open, not a code change. AC3 NOT DONE, and it splits. The TRACKING NUMBER half needs a schema change: measure_card_requests (00351) has status, requested_at, shipped_at and card_version, and NO tracking column — so there is nothing to render, and adding one is a migration plus a fulfilment-side write that nothing currently produces. The ETA half could be rendered without a migration from status + requested_at, but only if a real fulfilment SLA exists to quote; inventing "ships in 3-5 days" on a page a paying seller reads is a promise the system does not make. Both need an answer about the fulfilment process before they are code. VERIFIED: build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 100 flipdesk tests pass.

userStories.title: iOS: the item's own columns don't own their eBay specifics, so changing Size edits nothing the listing will publish
userStories.description: As a seller on iPhone, I want changing Size or Color on the item to update the eBay item specific too, so that I don't have to open Category & Specifics and type the same value a second time.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a structured column (brand/size/color/material/style) on the iOS item editor updates that column's eBay aspect even when the aspect's provenance is ai_extracted or manual. Today InventoryAspectSync.reassertDerivedAspects builds a 'preserve' map of every manual/aiExtracted aspect and passes it as 'known', so the AI-filled Size survives and the seller's new Size is discarded - the opposite of the documented contract that the columns OWN those five aspects (see the web helper projectColumnAspects in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts and its tests).

The save writes BOTH aspect stores, not just one: inventory_items.ebay_aspects (+ebay_aspect_sources) AND listings.item_specifics_override (+item_specifics_sources) for this item's listing row. Today the save-time path writes only the inventory_items pair; item_specifics_override is written ONLY by SpecificsEditorModel (the Category & Specifics editor), which is exactly why the seller has to go there for the change to stick - it is the copy publish/revise reads FIRST.

The projection runs even when the item has no eBay category selected yet. Today reassertDerivedAspects returns early on a blank ebay_category_id, so column values set before a category is picked never reach the aspect stores.

The projection is a PURE local function (a Swift mirror of projectColumnAspects: non-empty column overwrites its aspect and stamps provenance inventory_derived; a blanked column clears it), not a server round trip. Today every save calls EbayAspectsService.deriveAspects, so a save costs a network call and a transient failure silently no-ops via try?.

An XCTest asserts the three rules directly: an ai_extracted Size aspect IS overwritten by a changed Size column; a non-column aspect (e.g. Department, Pattern) is left untouched; and a cleared column clears its aspect.

A deno or vitest drift guard asserts the iOS column-to-aspect name mapping matches the web/edge registry (services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-registry.ts, vendored to src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json), so the two platforms cannot disagree on which aspect a column owns.

Publish still re-normalizes against the real category spec server-side (forceColumnAspects / COLUMN_ASPECT_FALLBACK in flipdesk-ebay.ts), so a raw column value outside eBay's allowed list is still corrected at publish - this story does not change that.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-03 WARNING, READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: AC4 and AC5 as written would re-open a bug fixed on 2026-08-02 (commit ea9e27a2). AC4 says to mirror projectColumnAspects, which was DELETED on 2026-08-01. Its replacement, projectColumnAspectsForSpec in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts, is deliberately OVERWRITE-ONLY: a blank column no longer clears its aspect, because a blank column cannot be told apart from a never-populated one. Clearing is allowed ONLY on a surface that owns the column inputs, which the iOS item editor does, so clear-on-blank inside the iOS EDITOR is fine. What is NOT fine is AC2 combined with AC4: writing a clear-on-blank projection straight into listings.item_specifics_override, the store the publish check reads FIRST. A blank Brand column carrying an AI- or hand-typed Brand aspect is the ordinary state of an iOS-created item, and deleting it there is exactly the reported failure: Brand plainly visible in the specifics editor while publish refuses with "Fill required eBay specifics in the composer: Brand". Also add the reverse pass (reverseProjectAspectColumns) BEFORE the forward one, or a specifics edit typed on iOS is clobbered by the stale column. Read vault/20-domain/sync-source-of-truth.md first; it is the contract.

userStories.title: Lock down SECURITY DEFINER functions: revoke EXECUTE from PUBLIC across public schema
userStories.description: Postgres grants EXECUTE on every new function to PUBLIC by default. No migration in supabase/migrations/ ever revokes it, and no `REVOKE ... ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC` exists anywhere. Because these functions are SECURITY DEFINER they run as the owner and bypass RLS, so any holder of the anon key can call them directly through PostgREST. grant_grade_credits and debit_grade_credits carry no GRANT/REVOKE statements at all; the revenue-dashboard functions (00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:273-274) grant to authenticated and service_role but never revoke the implicit PUBLIC grant. Impact: mint yourself unlimited grade credits, drain another user's credit balance, and read the full revenue and customer roster anonymously.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration revokes EXECUTE on all existing public-schema functions from PUBLIC, then re-grants explicitly to the roles each function actually needs.
`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC` so future functions are closed by default.
Every SECURITY DEFINER function is inventoried with its intended caller role; credit-mutating functions (grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, refund/reserve variants) are service_role only.
A test or CI check fails if a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships without an explicit grant block.
Migration triple honoured: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer.
Run `SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND prosecdef;` against prod before and after and record both in the story.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. Pairs with the guard_users_protected_columns gap — either one alone gives free grading. Fix both together. | 2026-08-04 BLOCKED on US-2403, with the migration WRITTEN AND VERIFIED. Two findings, and the first one means the fix as the story describes it would have done NOTHING. (1) THE STORY'S DIAGNOSIS IS HALF WRONG. It says Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default and no migration revokes it. Reading pg_proc.proacl on a live stack says otherwise: grant_grade_credits carries {postgres=X/postgres, anon=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres} — DIRECT grants to anon and authenticated, granted by postgres, from Supabase's own ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES bootstrap (confirmed in pg_default_acl for both postgres and supabase_admin on schema public, objtype 'f'). PUBLIC does not appear in the ACL at all. So 'REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC' is a NO-OP on exactly the functions the story names. I wrote that version first, applied it, and measured: grant_grade_credits/debit_grade_credits/revenue_dashboard still showed anon_can=t. A migration that looks like a security fix and changes nothing is worse than none, and the only reason I caught it is that I queried the ACLs instead of trusting the revoke. (2) THE CORRECTED MIGRATION IS WRITTEN AND PASSES EVERY CHECK, and is parked at supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED (the suffix is deliberate — apply-prod-migrations.sh globs *.sql, so the rename is what stops an accidental apply). It revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon AND authenticated on every non-extension function in public, closes the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES that keeps re-granting them, grants service_role everything (the edge calls 48), and then REPLAYS the grants migrations actually made — 43 names for authenticated, 4 for anon, PARSED out of every GRANT EXECUTE statement in the corpus minus any later explicit REVOKE, not authored by judgement. Plus is_admin/is_super_admin/is_reviewer_or_admin explicitly, because a function called inside an RLS policy runs as the QUERYING role and is_admin appears in 29 migrations' policies while having NEVER had a grant — it worked only on the default this removes. Extension functions are excluded via pg_depend deptype 'e' so pg_trgm (installed into public by 00224) keeps its operators. MEASURED AFTER APPLYING, on a fresh stack: all 527 apply from zero; ZERO of the 28 client-callable RPCs (parsed from src/ + ios/ call sites) lost authenticated EXECUTE; grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, grant_api_credits, admin_adjust_credits, revoke_grade_credits and reserve_ai_action are now f/f/t (anon no, authenticated no, service_role yes); revenue_dashboard and system_health keep authenticated because their own migrations explicitly granted it, and lose anon; similarity/show_trgm still callable by PUBLIC. (3) WHY IT IS NOT SHIPPING: verifying the behaviour crashed the database. On this image any function-permission denial for a role in supautils.hint_roles (anon, authenticated, service_role) segfaults the backend. Filed as US-2403 with the isolation. 00527 does not cause it — refund_grade has been revoked since 00048 and crashes identically — but it would take the crashable surface from a handful of RPCs to ~80. REMAINING ACs when unblocked: AC4 (a CI check that a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships with an explicit grant block) is NOT written; AC6 (proname/proacl before and after against PROD) is an operator read.

userStories.title: extension.pem private key is committed to the repository
userStories.description: git ls-files confirms extension.pem and extension.crx are tracked. extension.pem begins with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. .gitignore has no .pem or .crx rule. The key was added 2026-07-13 in commit e1dbc4da; gitleaks failed that commit and every run since has been green because push-mode only scans new commits. This is the Chrome Web Store signing identity for the extension. Anyone with repo read access can publish an update that every installed user auto-receives. Also tracked and probably unwanted: ios-screenshots/Payment/ios.zip, ios-screenshots/screenshots-appstore.zip, ios-screenshots/screenshots-raw.zip.
acceptanceCriteria: Rotate the Chrome Web Store extension key first. Removing the file does not un-leak it.
git rm --cached extension.pem extension.crx; add *.pem, *.crx and ios-screenshots/*.zip to .gitignore.
Decide and record whether git history is rewritten (BFG / filter-repo) or the key is simply treated as burned. Rewriting rewrites every open PR.
gitleaks runs in full-history mode at least once in CI (scheduled, not per-push) so an existing leak is not permanently invisible.
The rotated key is stored where the team's other signing secrets live; the location is named in the runbook, never the value.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/Secrets] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. via git ls-files + file header + .gitignore read. Rotation is a human action, not a code change. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the code half is done; AC1 (rotate) and AC3 (the rewrite-or-burn decision) are HUMAN actions and are now written down where the person doing them will find them. AC2 DONE: extension.pem, extension.crx and the three ios-screenshots zips are untracked via git rm --cached, and .gitignore refuses *.pem, *.crx, *.p12, *.keystore, *.jks and ios-screenshots/**/*.zip — broader than the story asked because the next leak will not be another .pem. Verified with git check-ignore. AC4 DONE: NEW .github/workflows/secret-scan-history.yml runs gitleaks over the FULL history weekly (Mondays 06:00 UTC, plus workflow_dispatch), with fetch-depth:0 and the gitleaks BINARY rather than gitleaks-action — the action derives its scan scope from the triggering event and on a schedule there is no diff, so `detect` over the checked-out repo is the unambiguous form. The report uploads on failure, because a bare red X names nothing. WHY THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT and worth stating plainly: there WAS a secret scanner, it WAS working, and it could not have caught this. secret-scan.yml runs in push/PR mode, which scans the commits in the triggering event; it failed the commit that added the key on 2026-07-13 and every run after that was green while the key sat in history. Per-push asks 'is this change clean?'; only a history sweep asks 'is the repository clean?'. AC5 DONE (structurally): vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md gains a section for this key — what it grants (publish an update EVERY installed user auto-receives, i.e. code execution in their browsers, not read access to something), the rotation steps, and an explicit blank line for the storage location, left blank rather than guessed at because naming the wrong vault entry is worse than naming none. AC3 is RECORDED not decided: both options are written out with their real costs — treat-as-burned (rotation makes the leaked copy inert; no rewrite; usually right for a signing key) versus rewrite (BFG/filter-repo; rewrites every open PR and invalidates every clone). .gitleaks.toml carries a COMMENTED-OUT allowlist stanza to uncomment AFTER rotation, with an explicit 'DO NOT uncomment before rotation — silencing a live key is worse than the leak, because it also removes the reminder.' EXPECT THE SCHEDULED SCAN TO BE RED until one of those two happens: the key IS still in history, so a finding is the job working, not a broken job. ALSO ADDED: src/test/no-committed-keys.test.ts refuses any tracked .pem/.crx/.p12/.pfx/.keystore/.jks/.key/.ppk at the point a developer notices — their own test run, before the push. It reads git ls-files rather than the filesystem, because an ignored file on disk is fine and a TRACKED one is the bug, and it skips (not fails) without a git binary, since a false red on a P0 guard trains people to ignore it. Negative-verified by force-adding a .pem to the index (reddened naming the file, reverted). REMAINING FOR THE OWNER: (1) rotate the Chrome Web Store signing key and revoke the old one; (2) fill in the storage-location line in key-rotation.md; (3) choose burn-vs-rewrite and, if burning, uncomment the gitleaks stanza. VERIFIED: 3079 tests pass (239 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green, vault-lint 108 notes clean. | SEVERITY RE-ASSESSED 2026-08-03, in BOTH directions, because the original framing is wrong in a way that changes what the owner should do. WORSE THAN RECORDED: the repository is PUBLIC (gh repo view reports visibility PUBLIC) and commit e1dbc4da is on origin, and reading that path out of history still returns a PRIVATE KEY header today. So this is not 'anyone with repo read access' — it is anyone at all, with no access, right now. Untracking the file (AC2) did nothing about that and was never going to; only rotation does. BETTER THAN RECORDED, and this is the part that should stop anyone panicking: the claim that 'anyone can publish an update that every installed user auto-receives' is NOT true today. Checked: no manifest in extension/, extension-condition/ or extension-unified/ declares an update_url or a key field, so there is no self-hosted auto-update channel; and US-1757 (publish to the Chrome Web Store and AMO) is still OPEN and operator-gated, so the extension has never been published and has no installed users. Uploading to the Web Store needs the developer ACCOUNT, which this key is not. WHAT THE KEY ACTUALLY GRANTS: the ability to package a CRX carrying the SAME extension ID as the real one — which matters for sideloading, for enterprise-policy deployment, and for any future self-hosted update channel, and which would let a lookalike be presented as genuine. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR SEQUENCING, which is the practical finding and was recorded nowhere: rotation is CHEAP right now and gets expensive the moment the extension is published, because after publication that ID is the installed identity. So AC1 must be done BEFORE US-1757, and US-1757 should not proceed until it is. RE-VERIFIED the code half rather than trusting the note: git ls-files finds no .pem, .gitignore lines 155-156 refuse *.pem and *.crx (git check-ignore confirms both files), .github/workflows/secret-scan-history.yml exists, and src/test/no-committed-keys.test.ts passes 3/3.

userStories.title: Apple sandbox purchases grant production plans
userStories.description: lib/appstore/verify.ts:89-96 retries a failed production receipt check against Apple's sandbox endpoint (Apple's documented pattern) but nothing downstream records or checks WHICH environment answered. Any TestFlight or sandbox tester gets a real Business Yearly entitlement for zero dollars. The Stripe path already blocks the equivalent case, so this is an iOS-path-only gap.
acceptanceCriteria: The verify result carries the environment (Production vs Sandbox) that actually answered.
A sandbox-verified receipt grants nothing in production, or grants only in a non-production environment.
Same check applied to the Google Play path: reject purchases flagged as test purchases (purchaseType / testPurchase).
Regression test for both stores.
Audit existing appstore-sourced entitlements for sandbox-originated grants.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/iOS+Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Covers both the Apple sandbox fallback and the Google Play test-purchase flag; they are the same class of bug. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED — and the premise is CONTESTED BY THE CODE, so this needs re-triage before anyone 'fixes' it. services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/verify.ts lines 38-44 already argue the opposite case, in a comment written when the fallback was added: App Review ALWAYS exercises IAP in the sandbox, even against a Production build, so a Production deploy that refuses Sandbox JWS fails App Review. verify-config.ts:91-93 implements it as primary-then-fallback (configured environment first, the other second), mirroring the legacy 21007 receipt rule Apple documents. The comment's defence is that a valid Sandbox JWS can only be produced by a sandbox tester Apple provisioned on the developer account, so it is not an open abuse vector. THAT DEFENCE IS PROBABLY RIGHT AND STILL LEAVES A REAL GAP, which is what this story should be rewritten to cover: the grant is recorded with NO MARKER of which environment produced it. Nothing on the users row or in the appstore audit rows says 'this Pro plan came from a Sandbox JWS'. So a sandbox-granted entitlement is indistinguishable from a paid one in every downstream query — revenue reporting, the expiry sweep, plan-distribution metrics, and any manual 'why is this account on Pro' investigation. RECOMMEND: reframe from 'stop accepting sandbox' (which would break App Review) to 'stamp the environment on the grant and exclude sandbox grants from revenue reporting', and say in the story that the acceptance itself is deliberate.

userStories.title: users_billing_source_chk rejects 'googleplay' — Play subscriptions may be failing outright
userStories.description: 00104_appstore_billing.sql:25 defines users_billing_source_chk allowing only 'stripe' and 'appstore'. The Google Play verification path writes 'googleplay'. If the constraint is live in prod as written, every Play subscription write fails: the customer is charged by Google and receives no entitlement.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm against prod whether the constraint still excludes 'googleplay' and whether any Play purchase has ever succeeded.
Migration extends the allowed set to include every billing source the code actually writes.
A test asserts the constraint's allowed set matches the set of literals the code writes.
If any customer was charged by Google without receiving entitlement, reconcile and grant retroactively.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Verify against prod before assuming customers were affected — the constraint may have been altered outside migrations. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED, and it is worse than 'may be failing' — it fails, deterministically. users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE, in 00104_appstore_billing.sql line 25: CHECK (billing_source IS NULL OR billing_source IN ('stripe','appstore')). grep across every file in supabase/migrations returns exactly two hits for the constraint name, both in 00104 (the IF NOT EXISTS probe and the ADD CONSTRAINT). NO migration ever drops or re-adds it. 00321_google_play_billing.sql touches public.users but only to add columns — its own header comment says "billing_source already carries 'stripe'/'appstore'; Play sets 'googleplay'", which reads as if the constraint had been widened, and it never was. Meanwhile the Play grant path genuinely stamps it: services/edge-functions/src/lib/google-play/products.ts declares billing_source: 'googleplay' as a literal type on the users update, and the expiry sweep queries .eq('billing_source','googleplay'). So every Play subscription grant UPDATE violates the check and returns 23514, and the sweep can never match a row because no row can hold that value. WHAT MAKES THIS EASY TO MISS: three OTHER constraints were correctly widened for Play — 00354 added 'googleplay' to the dead-letter provider check, 00414 allows it on buyer_billing_source, 00486 allows 'google_play' on the agreed-terms source. Only the seller-side users constraint was left behind, so a targeted grep for 'googleplay' in migrations returns four confident-looking hits and none of them is the one that matters. THE FIX is a one-line ALTER (drop + re-add with the third value), needing the US-1108 triple. Worth checking prod for stuck Play purchasers before shipping it: they paid Google and were never entitled here.

userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Abuse] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. userStories.title: Batch grading re-charges on every retry, up to 5 times for one garment
userStories.description: lib/grading-batch-worker.ts:59-124 and :155-176: gradeBatchItem unconditionally INSERTs a new submission (:66-79) and calls runPaymentPrecedence (:97) on every invocation. runJob reclaims a stale job (:167) and calls it again with no reference to the submission a prior attempt already created and paid for. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS is 240s but a single image's worst case is already 3 attempts x 120s = 360s, so a job can be marked stale while the original pipeline is still running and may still write a valid grade. After GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS (15 min) the reclaim cron starts a second paid attempt. MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS is 5. Result: up to 5 credits debited for one payload, plus duplicate certificates.
acceptanceCriteria: The created submission_id is persisted on the job row BEFORE the charge, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission rather than creating a new one.

Payment is charged at most once per job row, enforced by an idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions (the column and partial unique index already exist at 00216_credit_ledger_admin.sql:35-42 and the grading path never sets it).
Item lease duration exceeds the true worst-case runtime (3 AI attempts x timeout + composite), or the work is made cancellable.
Regression test: a job forced through 3 reclaims debits exactly one credit and produces exactly one certificate.
Audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id, and refund affected customers.
userStories.notes: [P0][Grading/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Highest-confidence money bug from the grading audit — the code path is described concretely and matches the reclaim-cron design. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the double-charge is FIXED at the root (AC1, AC3, AC4); AC2 is defence-in-depth that now needs a migration, and AC5 is an operator action. RE-VERIFIED FIRST, as the note asked: gradeBatchItem created a submission and called runPaymentPrecedence unconditionally on every invocation, and runJob called it again on every reclaim with no reference to the submission a prior attempt had created and paid for. Confirmed the two windows that made it reachable rather than theoretical: GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS was 240s while one garment's worst case is (AI_MAX_RETRIES + 1) x AI_TIMEOUT_MS = 3 x 120s = 360s (ai-config.ts DEFAULTS), so the worker abandoned a pipeline that was still running; and GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS was 360s — EQUAL to that worst case — so the reclaim cron could pick up a job nobody had abandoned. With MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS at 5 that is up to 5 credits and 5 certificates for one garment. AC1 DONE: the submission id is written to the job row IMMEDIATELY after creation and BEFORE any money moves, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission instead of creating another. The ordering is the point — writing it after the charge would leave exactly the window this story is about; writing it before means a container death mid-flight leaves an UNPAID submission, which the resume path declines and starts clean, costing nothing. The fix is deliberately NOT a smarter charge: payment is per-submission, so resuming skips the charge BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard someone has to remember. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/paid-submission.ts holds isPaidSubmissionStatus as its own pure module — it is the hinge the whole fix turns on and keeping it out of the worker means it can be tested without booting the grading pipeline. It fails CLOSED on unknown/NULL/unpaid, and the asymmetry is the reason: a false negative re-creates a submission nobody paid for (free), a false positive skips a real charge or resumes a row we do not own. The paid values are the three grade-billing.ts actually writes — included, credits, paid_stripe — read off the source, not guessed. The resume path also re-stamps status=processing (tenant-scoped, mirroring the charging chokepoint's own .eq(user_id)) and records the API usage the abandoned attempt never got to record, exactly once. AC3 DONE: both windows are now DERIVED from the AI budget instead of written down beside it, because two hardcoded numbers that must track a third are two numbers that drift — which is precisely how the lease ended up shorter than the work it was leasing. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS = (getAiMaxRetries()+1) * getAiTimeoutMs() + 90s composite headroom (450s at current defaults, up from 240s); GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS = 1.5x the lease (675s, up from 360s) so a merely-slow worker is never mistaken for a dead one; GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS is floored above the job window so the batch sweeper cannot fire before its jobs are even reclaimable. The pre-existing assertion (timeout < stale) in grading-batch_test.ts still holds. AC4 DONE: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/grading-batch-recharge_test.ts, 6 Deno cases pinning the lease-exceeds-worst-case relationship, the stale margin, the sweeper ordering, the derivation arithmetic (asserted rather than the literal, so raising AI_TIMEOUT_MS keeps it green), and both directions of the paid-status rule. VERIFIED: 20 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled paid-submission module plus the timing arithmetic reproduced independently (old lease 240000 confirmed BELOW the 360000 worst case); all four changed edge files parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: (AC2) the idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions. The column and partial unique index exist (00216:35-42) but the credit debit goes through the debit_grade_credits RPC, so threading a key needs a FUNCTION SIGNATURE CHANGE — a migration, which cannot be pushed from this host under the held-migration rule. It is defence-in-depth behind the root fix, not the fix itself. (AC5) audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers — an operator action; the query is: grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. Nothing here is holding the branch. | AC2 DONE 2026-08-03, migration 00516 (HELD). The note above said this needed a function signature change and so a migration, and that is exactly what it took. debit_grade_credits gains a TRAILING p_idempotency_key defaulting to NULL, so every existing 4-arg caller is untouched; the old 4-arg overload is DROPPED in the same file, because leaving it would let those callers silently keep resolving to the pre-idempotency body. When a key is supplied and a ledger row already carries it the function debits nothing and returns the current balance — returning rather than raising on purpose, since the caller intent (this submission is paid for) is already satisfied and an error would make a harmless retry look like a billing failure and push the caller into a checkout it does not need. The edge passes grade-batch-job:{jobId}, keyed on the JOB rather than the submission because the job is what a reclaim re-runs. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, not by inspection: applied to the local stack and exercised in a rolled-back transaction — the same key three times debits ONCE (10 -> 7 -> 7 -> 7, exactly one ledger row), a different key debits normally, and a call with no key debits every time, which is the assertion that protects the existing callers. Storage needed no migration: 00216 already had the column and its partial unique index, unused. REMAINING: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. That is an operator action; the query is grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. Edge suite 5155/0.

userStories.title: The golden-set eval gate never runs in CI and the live prompt versions have no DB row
userStories.description: Two compounding problems. (1) The grading eval appears in none of the 16 files in .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json. The only eval task there is the agent eval, and CI does not call that either. No build, deploy or PR is blocked by golden-set accuracy. runScheduledEval raises alerts and blocks nothing. (2) The code defaults are per_image_v5 and composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63) but the only grading seed migration (00050_grading_self_improvement.sql:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 and composite_v2, and no migration sets is_active. So the live prompts have no row and were never evaluated. (3) The repo contains no golden-set data at all: zero INSERTs into grading_eval_cases, no seed, no fixture. A fresh database has an empty golden set; runEval throws on empty but grading-monitor.ts:287-294 treats zero cases as a clean skip, so an empty set is silent. Net effect: editing prompt text in ai-grading.ts ships straight to customers without ever touching an eval.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm first, against prod, whether grading_eval_cases has any rows and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active. Record the answer in the story before building.
The golden-set eval runs in CI and fails the build on regression, or the reason it cannot is written down.
Every prompt version the code can use has a DB row with eval results and qualified_model, including the code defaults.
An empty golden set is treated as a hard failure, not a clean skip.
Prompt text in ai-grading.ts cannot ship without a corresponding evaluated version — enforced by a test, not by convention.
EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 (grading-eval.ts:26-29) is reconsidered: on a 1.0-10.0 scale a prompt can be a full grade point off on average and pass.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Lifecycle] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The prompt-lifecycle doc reads as if a pipeline gate exists. It does not. Either add one or correct the doc. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — ALL FOUR factual claims independently RE-VERIFIED and TRUE; AC4 and AC5 shipped, the doc corrected; AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 need prod access or a migration and are recorded with why. VERIFICATION (mechanical, not by reading the cited lines): (1) NO CI GATE — the golden-set eval appears in no file under .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json; the only match anywhere in those trees is a mention in scripts/ralph/progress.txt. Nothing blocks a build, PR or deploy on grading accuracy. (2) THE LIVE PROMPTS HAVE NO ROW — code defaults are per_image_v5 / composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63); the sole seed migration (00050:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 / composite_v2 with is_active false. Scanned EVERY migration touching ai_prompt_versions: neither v5 nor v4 appears. (3) ZERO GOLDEN-SET DATA — no INSERT into grading_eval_cases in any migration. A fresh database starts with an empty set. (4) EMPTY WAS SILENT — grading-monitor.ts runScheduledEval returned skipped_reason "no active eval cases" and moved on. AC4 DONE, and the reasoning matters: an empty set is the accuracy gate being SWITCHED OFF, not "nothing to check". With no cases the eval never runs, so eval_passed is null rather than false and NO other rule in evaluateAlerts fires — the state where no prompt has ever been evaluated, and none can be, produced complete silence from the only component whose job is to notice. evaluateAlerts now raises golden_set_empty at CRITICAL. Deliberately an ALERT rather than a thrown error: throwing would break the monitor cron on a fresh deploy, trading a silent gap for a noisy one and teaching operators to ignore the job. The message names the remedy AND the anti-remedy ("never synthetic") because an operator reading "the set is empty" under pressure will reach for fabricated cases, which makes every future eval meaningless while reading green. Kept DISTINCT from golden_set_shrank: a 40→0 set is both, and collapsing them loses the deliberate-abuse signal US-2037 exists for. AC5 DONE as a PIN rather than a fix, since seeding rows is a migration this host cannot push: a new case reads both prompt-version constants, scans every migration that touches ai_prompt_versions, and asserts the unseeded set equals KNOWN_UNSEEDED_PROMPT_VERSIONS exactly — both ways. So a FURTHER version bump fails until its author seeds a row or amends the declaration, and seeding one without amending also fails. That converts "nobody noticed for four versions" into "you cannot bump a version without deciding".
