userStories.title: A denied function call from anon or authenticated SEGFAULTS Postgres and restarts the whole database
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a permission-denied RPC to return an error instead of crashing the database, so that anyone holding the public anon key cannot restart production at will.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish whether the PROD Postgres image reproduces it. On the local Supabase image (PG 17.6) it reproduces every time; prod is a separate self-hosted image and this has NOT been tested there, deliberately, because the test is a denial of service against production. The safe check is to read the image tag and the supautils.hint_roles setting, not to call a denied RPC.

If prod reproduces: mitigate BEFORE anything else. Clearing supautils.hint_roles (it exists only to append a GRANT hint to the error message) or upgrading the image are the two candidates; whichever is chosen, prove it with a denied call against a staging copy of the same image.

A regression check that survives an image upgrade: a throwaway-stack test that revokes EXECUTE on a scratch function, calls it as anon, and asserts a clean 'permission denied for function' error with the connection still alive.

supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED is renamed back to .sql, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00527 in the same commit, and US-2282 closed — the SQL is already written and verified, it is only blocked on this.

The 5 functions already revoked from anon before this was known (refund_grade 00048, credit_ledger_reconciliation 00093, release_job_lock + try_acquire_job_lock 00094, reserve_snap/refund_snap 00099, reconcile_payout_link 00117, equity_snapshot_owners) are enumerated in the notes as the CURRENTLY reachable crash entry points, since they are what an attacker could use today.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] Found 2026-08-04 by accident while verifying US-2282 on a throwaway stack, and it is the reason US-2282 is not shipping. ISOLATED, not guessed — four probes on the local Supabase image (PostgreSQL 17.6, shared_preload_libraries includes supautils): (1) a trivial scratch function with EXECUTE revoked, called as anon => SIGNAL 11 SEGMENTATION FAULT, 'terminating any other active server processes', full database recovery; (2) same as authenticated => same crash; (3) same as a custom role NOT listed in supautils.hint_roles => clean 'ERROR: permission denied for function', connection alive; (4) a denied TABLE read as anon => clean error PLUS the supautils hint 'Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT SELECT ON public.applied_migrations TO anon;'. supautils.hint_roles is set to exactly 'anon, authenticated, service_role', which is exactly the set that crashes. So the crash is in the supautils hint path for FUNCTION permission denials specifically; the table path is fine. ALREADY REACHABLE TODAY, WITHOUT ANY NEW MIGRATION: public.refund_grade(uuid) has been revoked from anon since 00048/00093, and calling it as anon crashes the database the same way — verified, not inferred. PostgREST exposes it as an RPC, so the input needed is the public anon key and one HTTP call. WHY US-2282 IS BLOCKED ON THIS RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY AROUND: 00527 does not create the bug, it multiplies the entry points — from the handful of functions already revoked to ~80. Applying it into an unpatched image would hand an attacker eighty ways to restart the database instead of eight. The SQL is written, verified on a fresh stack, and parked at supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED; the .BLOCKED suffix is what keeps apply-prod-migrations.sh (which globs *.sql) from applying it. NOT TESTED AGAINST PROD ON PURPOSE. The test IS the denial of service, so running it would be the attack. The safe next step is to read the prod image tag and 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql — both read-only — and compare against the local image. If prod's image differs enough not to reproduce, this closes as a local-only artifact and US-2282 unblocks immediately.

userStories.title: Feature-flag plan targeting is never applied at runtime — plan_targets is an admin control that does nothing
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a flag limited to a plan tier to actually be limited, because today it is not. resolveFlagRule (feature-flags.ts:155) only applies plan_targets when the caller SUPPLIES a plan: `if (opts.plan && rule.plan_targets.length > 0 && …)`. No runtime caller does. Every one of the ~25 isFeatureEnabled() call sites passes either nothing or `{ userId }` (flipdesk-forecast.ts:171 is the only one that passes a userId at all), so `opts.plan` is always undefined and the plan check is SKIPPED — the rule falls straight through to the percentage rollout. An operator who sets plan_targets: ['pro'] believes the flag is limited to Pro; in reality it is on for everyone the rollout percentage admits. The admin 'who does this reach' preview is the ONLY code that supplies a plan (admin-flags.ts), which is why the control looks like it works: the preview computes a reach the runtime does not honour. US-2398 fixed the COLUMN that preview samples (users.plan → flipdesk_plan) and the vocabulary it offers; it deliberately did NOT fix this, because threading a plan through every call site is a design decision, not a column swap.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the shape FIRST: either isFeatureEnabled resolves the caller's plan itself (one cached lookup keyed by userId, so no call site changes) or every call site that can target a plan passes one. Do not fix half — a flag whose targeting works at some call sites and not others is worse than one where it never works.
A rule with plan_targets set and a caller that cannot resolve a plan must FAIL CLOSED or say so, not silently fall through to the rollout percentage as it does today.
The admin preview and the runtime resolve identically for the same rule and user — a preview that disagrees with the behaviour is what hid this.

A test pins the property that a plan-targeted rule excludes a non-matching user through the REAL entry point (isFeatureEnabled), not only through the pure resolveFlagRule helper — the existing feature-flags_test.ts covers the helper and passed throughout.
Audit whether any flag in prod currently has plan_targets set; if one does, it has been wide open and whoever set it should be told.
userStories.notes: [P2][Admin/Flags] Found 2026-08-05 while fixing US-2398's TypeScript readers. NOT a regression from that work — the gap has been there since US-886 shipped targeting v2. Filed separately rather than folded in because the fix is a design choice about where a plan is resolved, and US-2398's change (sampling flipdesk_plan instead of the frozen users.plan) is correct and complete on its own terms. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the failure is fail-OPEN. A flag an operator believes is limited to paying tiers is serving free accounts, so the blast radius of a bad flag is the whole user base rather than the slice that was chosen. Nothing errors and nothing logs, which is why it survived a targeting feature, its admin UI and a unit-test suite: resolveFlagRule is tested WITH a plan supplied (feature-flags_test.ts:93-97) and behaves correctly there — the defect is that production never supplies one. | Done 2026-08-05. ALL FIVE AC MET; the operator audit came back empty, so this ships with no live behaviour change. SHAPE DECIDED (AC1): isFeatureEnabled RESOLVES THE PLAN ITSELF. New dbLoadEffectivePlan() in lib/feature-flags.ts reads users(flipdesk_plan, subscription_status, trial_ends_at, past_due_since) through effectivePlanFor() and caches it on the SAME 30s clock as the rule, bounded at PLAN_CACHE_MAX=5000 (long-lived process, key space is every user who hits a targeted flag; past the cap the map is dropped whole rather than evicted). It is the EFFECTIVE plan deliberately, not the raw column: a canceled Pro targets as Free and a US-2398 comp targets as its granted tier, matching the caps, gates and MRR. An UNTARGETED rule never triggers the lookup at all, which is every flag in the system today, so the common path costs exactly what it did before -- pinned by a test that counts lookups rather than inferring from the answer. BUT THE OTHER HALF WAS REQUIRED TOO, and calling it done without it would have been the half-fix AC1 forbids: a callee that resolves from opts.userId is useless if no call site passes one. userId (the WORKSPACE OWNER -- the billed party, whose plan every other entitlement reads; scoping to the acting member would give two people in one workspace different features off one subscription) now threaded through grade.ts /submit /pay/:id /snap + authenticity_addon + forensic_grade, api-v1.ts /grades and /grades/batch, flipdesk-grading.ts /submit, flipdesk-autolister.ts /batch, jobs-journey-tick.ts content_ai, and featureGate() reads c.get('userId') defensively so the /api/content/* route group is covered without touching seven mounts. AC2 -- FAIL CLOSED, and where the interesting decision is: resolveFlagRule step 5 went from  to , so a rule that names plans is NOT satisfied by a caller who cannot present one. No userId, an unreadable users row and a missing user all resolve OFF and log feature_flag.plan_unresolved with the reason. Fail-closed alone would have been a bad answer for a CRON, though -- plan_targets on 'newsletter' would silently stop every send at 3am -- so the mistake is refused where it is MADE instead: new PLAN_TARGETABLE_FLAGS (grading, autolister, content_ai, authenticity_addon, forensic_grade, passport_forecast) is the set whose EVERY call site can name a user, PUT /:key/rule 400s on plan_targets for anything else naming why, GET / returns plan_targetable per flag, and the editor greys the control out with the reason in place of the usual hint. Membership is a property of the CALL SITES, not the feature -- repricing and inventory_equity are excluded only because handleRepriceScanCron / handleEquitySnapshotCron run them fleet-wide -- so a test scans src/routes, src/lib and src/middleware and FAILS if a listed key is ever checked without a userId. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by planting a bare isFeatureEnabled('grading') in admin-journeys.ts and watching it fail, then removing it. AC3 -- the preview now runs effectivePlanFor over the same four columns the runtime resolves (it sampled the raw flipdesk_plan, which over-counts a lapsed Pro), and a test walks 60 users asserting preview and runtime agree per user; a disagreement is what hid this for two stories. AC4 -- NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/feature-flag-plan-targeting_test.ts (12 cases) goes through isFeatureEnabled with injectable FeatureFlagDeps (__testing.setDeps, mirroring lib/plan-gate.ts), because the existing suite tested the PURE resolver and passed the entire time the feature was broken -- the helper was always correct, production just never fed it a plan. The old assertion that encoded the bug ('No plan supplied -> plan targeting is skipped') is flipped in place with a comment saying what it used to claim. AC5 -- NEW section 18 in scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql lists flags with plan_targets set OR rollout_percentage < 100; the operator RAN IT AND IT RETURNED EMPTY, so nothing was ever targeted, nobody needs telling, and the fail-closed change alters no live behaviour. FOUND WHILE DOING IT, unrelated to the feature: scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (generated, and the only copy that works in a SQL editor -- psql meta-commands make the original error with 42601 at the first \pset) had been STALE since section 17 shipped. The sync test spot-checked four hand-listed section numbers and 'every FROM public.<table>', and section 17 reads users, a table five other sections already read -- so a section adding no NEW table was invisible. The check now derives the section list from the source; negative-verified by reverting the console copy and watching it name section 17. VERIFIED: deno lint + check clean, full edge suite 5439 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, eslint clean, ui:check 0 findings, vault:index + a new vault/10-ops/feature-flag-targeting.md contract note. Two web-suite cases (users-self-update-allowlist, legacy-user-plan-readers) time out at the 5s default under full-suite load on this Windows host and pass in isolation -- whole-tree walkers, pre-existing, unrelated.
